card.summary_ko: 박지원의 《열하일기》 첫 편 〈도강록〉의 앞부분. 1780년(음력) 6월 24일 의주에서 압록강을 건너 책문에 들어서 봉황성 일대를 보는 6월 28일까지의 기록.
card.summary_en: The opening of Park Ji-won's Dogangnok, the first part of the Yeolha ilgi: the entries from 24 June 1780 (lunar), crossing the Yalu from Uiju, to 28 June at the Chaekmun gate and Fenghuang city. The famous passage on weeping (Hogokjang) is not included.
card.edition_ko: 한국어 위키문헌 「열하일기/도강록」 (개정 413682, 2025-10-28), 원저작 퍼블릭 도메인, 전사 CC BY-SA 4.0 — 머리말과 6월 24~28일치만 수록. 도강록의 나머지(6월 29일~7월 8일, 호곡장 포함)는 없고 6월 28일 기록의 끝에서 멈춘다. 한글 소제목은 편집자 것, 원문만·번역 없음
card.edition_en: Korean Wikisource 「열하일기/도강록」 (revision 413682, 2025-10-28); original in the public domain, transcription CC BY-SA 4.0. The preface and the entries for 24-28 June only. The rest of the Dogangnok (29 June to 8 July, including the Hogokjang passage) is not included; the text stops at the end of the 28 June entry. The Korean section headings are the editors', not the author's. Original text only, no translation.

notes.ko:
**저자** 박지원(1737–1805, 호 연암)은 반남 박씨로 서울의 노론 명문 양반 집안 출신입니다. 젊어서 과거를 포기하고 홍대용, 박제가, 이덕무 등과 어울리며 청의 발전된 문물을 배우자는 북학을 주장한 북학파의 대표입니다. 한때 홍국영의 정치적 압박을 피해 황해도 연암골에 숨어 살아 호가 연암이 되었습니다. 1780년 청 건륭제 칠순 축하 사절의 일원으로 중국에 다녀와 《열하일기》를 썼습니다. 늦게 음직으로 출사하여 안의현감, 면천군수, 양양부사 등을 지냈습니다. 정조의 문체반정(1792) 때 《열하일기》의 문체가 문제 되어 자송문을 지어 올리라는 요구를 받았다고 전합니다. 1805년에 세상을 떠났습니다. 〈도강록〉은 《열하일기》의 첫머리로, 압록강을 건너는 대목부터 시작합니다.

**시대적 맥락** 1780년 박지원은 팔촌형 박명원이 이끄는 건륭제 칠순 축하 사절에 수행해 압록강을 건넜습니다. 당시 청은 강희·옹정·건륭 시대를 거치며 번영하고 있었으나, 조선의 사대부 다수는 병자호란의 상처와 명에 대한 의리 때문에 청을 오랑캐로 여기는 북벌 의식을 지니고 있었습니다. 〈도강록〉은 압록강 도하에서 요동까지의 여정을 기록한 부분으로, 청의 성곽·수레·벽돌 같은 실용 기술에 주목하는 북학의 관점을 보여 줍니다. 《열하일기》는 필사본으로 널리 읽혔고 정조 때 문체 문제로 비판받았으나, 조선 후기 기행문학과 실학의 대표작으로 평가됩니다.

**배경**
박지원(1737–1805)은 1780년(건륭 45) 청 황제 건륭제의 칠순을 축하하는 사절단에 정사 박명원(삼종형)의 수행원으로 따라갔다. 이때의 여행기가 《열하일기》이다. 북경에서 황제가 있는 열하까지 가는 여정이 들어 있어 이런 제목이 붙었다. 〈도강록〉 전체는 압록강을 건넌 날부터 요양에 이르는 15일의 기록(‘起辛未, 止乙酉’)이다. 《열하일기》는 필사본으로 널리 퍼졌고, 그 문체가 정조 때 문체반정과 관련해 비판받았다고 전하지만 세부는 확실하지 않다.

**내용 (이 판)**
머리말: 연도를 ‘후삼경자(後三庚子)’로 적은 까닭을 문답으로 설명한다. 숭정 기원 후 세 번째 경자년이 1780년이고, 강을 건너면 청나라 땅이라 청의 연호를 쓰지 않고 이렇게 돌려 적는다는 것이다.
이 판은 다음 날짜의 기록을 싣는다. 6월 24일 장마로 불어난 압록강을 건너 구련성에서 노숙. 25일 냇가에서 낚시, 26일 강세작(명에서 건너와 정착한 인물) 이야기와 총수(葱秀) 숙영, 27일 책문 도착과 뇌물·예물 흥정, 28일 봉황성 일대 관찰, 벽돌집·기와 만드는 법, 안시성 위치론. 한글 소제목(‘압록강을 건너다’ 등)은 위키문헌 편집자가 붙인 것이다.
카탈로그가 약속한 요동 벌판의 ‘호곡장’ 논의는 7월 8일 무렵 기록에 있어 이 판에는 없다. 기록은 6월 28일에서 끝나며 이후 7월 8일까지의 도강록은 이 판에 없다.

**의의**
청의 선진 문물을 눈여겨보라는 ‘북학’ 정신이 처음 드러나는 대목이다. 벽돌·수레·기와 같은 생활 기술을 자세히 관찰하고 ‘이용후생’의 시각으로 쓴다.

**읽기 도움**
- 後三庚子, 崇禎紀元後: 청 연호를 피하는 연도 표기.
- 洌上外史: 머리말 끝에 박지원이 쓴 자기 호칭.
- 裨將·首譯·上判事·馬頭: 사절단의 수행 무관, 수석 역관, 하급 수행원.
- 刷馬驅人: 짐말을 모는 인부.
- 方物: 청에 바치는 토산물. 八包: 역관 등에게 허용된 인삼·은 무역 한도.
- 灣賈: 의주 상인.
- 柵門·架子門·邊門: 같은 문을 부르는 세 이름(조선·현지·내지).
- 旗下·民家: 만주인·한인 호칭. 官話: 중국 표준어.
- 甓·甎: 벽돌. 簟: 대자리.
- 六月二十四日辛未: 날짜 뒤에 간지와 날씨(朝小雨)를 적는 일기 형식.
notes.en:
**About the author** Park Ji-won (1737–1805, pen name Yeonam), of the Bannam Park clan, came from a distinguished Noron yangban family of Seoul. He gave up the examinations when young and, with Hong Dae-yong, Park Je-ga and Yi Deok-mu, became a leading figure of the Northern Learning (북학) school, which urged learning from Qing China. He hid for a time in Yeonam valley, Hwanghae, to escape Hong Guk-yeong's pressure, which gave him his pen name. In 1780 he went to China with the mission for Emperor Qianlong's seventieth birthday and wrote the Yeolha ilgi. He entered office late by a recommended (eum) appointment and served as magistrate of Anui, Myeoncheon and Yangyang. In Jeongjo's literary-style reform (1792) the Yeolha ilgi's style was criticised and he was reportedly asked for a letter of self-criticism. He died in 1805. 'Dogangnok' opens the Yeolha ilgi, beginning with the crossing of the Yalu.

**Historical context** In 1780 Park Ji-won crossed the Yalu as a member of the mission for Emperor Qianlong's seventieth birthday, led by his distant cousin Park Myeong-won. The Qing was then prospering through the Kangxi, Yongzheng and Qianlong reigns, but many Joseon scholar-officials, because of the wound of the Manchu invasion and loyalty to Ming, still held the northern-expedition view of the Qing as barbarians. 'Dogangnok' records the journey from the crossing of the Yalu to Liaodong and shows the Northern Learning outlook in its attention to practical technology such as Qing walls, carts and bricks. The Yeolha ilgi was widely read in manuscript and was criticised under Jeongjo for its style, but is rated as the leading work of late Joseon travel writing and practical learning.

**Background**
In 1780 (Qianlong 45) Park Ji-won (1737-1805) went to the Qing as a member of the mission celebrating the Qianlong Emperor's seventieth birthday, under his distant cousin Park Myeong-won. His travel record is the Yeolha ilgi (Jehol Diary), named for the trip from Beijing on to the emperor's summer residence at Rehe. The Dogangnok as a whole covers the 15 days from crossing the Yalu to Liaoyang ("from sinmi to eulyu"). The Yeolha ilgi circulated widely in manuscript and is said to have been criticised for its style under King Jeongjo, in connection with the literary-style reform campaign (munche banjeong), though the details are uncertain.

**Contents (this edition)**
The preface explains in question and answer why the year is written "after Chongzhen, the third gyeongja": 1780 is the third gyeongja year since Chongzhen, and, since across the river lies Qing land, the Qing reign name is avoided.
The entries given are: 24 June, crossing the swollen Yalu and camping out at Gouliancheng; 25 June, fishing by a stream; 26 June, the tale of Gang Se-jak (a man from Ming China who settled in Korea) and the camp at Chongxiu (Ch'ongsu); 27 June, arrival at the Chaekmun gate and haggling over gifts; 28 June, Fenghuang city, brick houses and tile-making, and the debate on where Ansi fortress stood. The Korean section headings ("Crossing the Yalu", etc.) were added by Wikisource editors.
The Hogokjang discourse on the Liaodong plain, promised in the catalogue, falls in the entries of around 8 July and is not here: the text stops at 28 June, and the rest of the Dogangnok up to 8 July is not in this edition.

**Significance**
Here the Northern Learning outlook appears early: close observation of bricks, carts and tiles with an eye to "using things to enrich the people" (iyong husaeng).

**Reading help**
- 後三庚子, 崇禎紀元後: a dating form avoiding the Qing reign name.
- 洌上外史: the author's own sobriquet in the preface.
- 裨將, 首譯, 上判事, 馬頭: aides, chief interpreter, senior interpreter, groom.
- 刷馬驅人: drivers of the baggage horses.
- 方物: local tribute goods; 八包: the ginseng/silver trade allowance for officials.
- 灣賈: merchants of Uiju.
- 柵門, 架子門, 邊門: three names for the same gate (Korean, local, inland).
- 旗下, 民家: Manchu and Han; 官話: Mandarin.
- 甓, 甎: brick; 簟: reed mat.
- 六月二十四日辛未: entries give the cyclical day and weather (朝小雨).

paragraphs.orig: 渡江錄
paragraphs.reading: 도강록
paragraphs.en: The Record of Crossing the River

paragraphs.orig: ## 머리말
paragraphs.en: Preface

paragraphs.orig: 起辛未, 止乙酉。 自鴨綠江, 至遼陽。 十五日。
paragraphs.reading: 기신미, 지을유. 자압록강, 지요양. 십오일.
paragraphs.en: From the sinmi day to the eulyu day. From the Amnok (Yalu) River to Liaoyang. Fifteen days.

paragraphs.orig: 曷爲後三庚子。 記行程陰晴, 將年以係月日也。 曷稱後。 崇禎紀元後也。 曷三庚子。 崇禎紀元後三周庚子也。 曷不稱崇禎。 將渡江故諱之也。 曷諱之。 江以外淸人也。 天下皆奉淸正朔, 故不敢稱崇禎也。 曷私稱崇禎。皇明中華也。吾初受命之上國也。 崇禎十七年, 毅宗烈皇帝殉社稷。 明室亡, 于今百三十餘年, 曷至今稱之。 淸人入主中國, 而先王之制度變而爲胡。 環東土數千里, 畫江而爲國, 獨守先王之制度, 是明明室猶存於鴨水以東也。 雖力不足以攘除戎狄肅淸中原, 以光復先王之舊。 然皆能尊崇禎, 以存中國也。
paragraphs.reading: 갈위후삼경자. 기행정음청, 장연이계월일야. 갈칭후. 숭정기원후야. 갈삼경자. 숭정기원후삼주경자야. 갈불칭숭정. 장도강고휘지야. 갈휘지. 강이외청인야. 천하개봉청정삭, 고불감칭숭정야. 갈사칭숭정. 황명중화야. 오초수명지상국야. 숭정십칠년, 의종열황제순사직. 명실망, 우금백삼십여년, 갈지금칭지. 청인입주중국, 이선왕지제도변이위호. 환동토수천리, 화강이위국, 독수선왕지제도, 시명명실유존어압수이동야. 수역부족이양제융적숙청중원, 이광복선왕지구. 연개능존숭정, 이존중국야.
paragraphs.en: Why “the Third Gyeongja After”? It is to record the stages of the journey and the weather, fair or foul, by attaching the year to the months and days. Why “After”? It means after the beginning of the Chongzhen era. Why “Third Gyeongja”? It means the third gyeongja cycle since the Chongzhen era began. Why not say “Chongzhen” outright? Because we were about to cross the river, and so we avoided the name. Why avoid it? Beyond the river are the Qing. All the world honors the Qing calendar, and so we do not dare to say “Chongzhen.” Why, then, do I privately say “Chongzhen”? Because Ming China is the Middle Kingdom, the superior state from which we first received our mandate. In the seventeenth year of Chongzhen, the Emperor Yizong Lie died with his altars of state, and the Ming house perished. It is now more than a hundred and thirty years since; why do we still call it by that name today? Because when the Qing entered and took possession of China, the institutions of the former kings were changed into barbarian ones; but around the Eastern Land, across thousands of li, we have drawn the river as our boundary and made a state of it, and alone keep the institutions of the former kings. This means that the Ming house still survives east of the Amnok. Though our strength does not suffice to drive out the Rong and Di, to purify the Central Plain, and to restore the old ways of the former kings to their glory, we can all still honor Chongzhen and so preserve China.

paragraphs.orig: 崇禎百五十六年癸卯 洌上外史題
paragraphs.reading: 숭정백오십육년계묘 열상외사제
paragraphs.en: The 156th year of Chongzhen, the gyemyo year. Inscribed by Yeolsang oesa, the Unofficial Historian of the Yeol River.

paragraphs.orig: ## 압록강을 건너다
paragraphs.en: Crossing the Amnok River

paragraphs.orig: 後三庚子, 我聖上四年, 淸乾隆四十五年。
paragraphs.reading: 후삼경자, 아성상사년, 청건륭사십오년.
paragraphs.en: The Third Gyeongja After: the fourth year of our Sovereign; the forty-fifth year of Qianlong of the Qing.

paragraphs.orig: 六月二十四日辛未 (朝小雨 終日乍灑乍止)
paragraphs.reading: 육월이십사일신미 (조소우 종일사쇄사지)
paragraphs.en: The 24th day of the sixth month, sinmi (a little rain in the morning; all day it sprinkled and stopped by turns).

paragraphs.orig: 午後渡鴨綠江。 行三十里, 露宿九連城。 夜大雨卽止。
paragraphs.reading: 오후도압록강. 행삼십리, 노숙구련성. 야대우즉지.
paragraphs.en: After noon we crossed the Amnok River. We traveled thirty li and slept in the open at Jiuliancheng. In the night there was heavy rain, which soon stopped.

paragraphs.orig: 初留龍灣義州舘。 十日, 方物盡到, 行期甚促, 而一雨成霖, 兩江通漲。 中間快晴, 亦已四日, 而水勢益盛。 木石俱轉, 濁浪連空, 盖鴨綠江, 發源最遠故耳。 按唐書, 高麗馬訾水, 出靺鞨之白山, 色若鴨頭 故號鴨綠江。 所謂白山者, 卽長白山也。 山海經, 稱不咸山, 我國稱白頭山。 白頭山, 爲諸江發源之祖, 西南流者爲鴨綠江。 皇輿考云, 「天下有三大水, 黃河, 長江, 鴨綠江也。」 兩山墨談, 陳霆著, 云, 「自淮以北爲北條, 凡水皆宗大河。 未有以江名者, 而北之在高麗曰鴨綠江。」 盖是江也, 天下之大水也。 其發源之地, 方旱方潦, 難度於千里之外也。 以今漲勢觀之, 白山長霖, 可以推知。 况此非尋常津涉之地乎。 今當盛潦, 汀步艤泊, 皆失故處, 中流礁沙, 亦所難審。 操舟者少失其勢, 則有非人力所可廻旋。 一行譯員迭援故事, 固請退期, 灣尹 李在學, 亦送親裨, 爲挽數日。 而正使堅以是日, 爲渡江之期, 狀啓已書塡日時矣。
paragraphs.reading: 초유용만의주관. 십일, 방물진도, 행기심촉, 이일우성림, 양강통창. 중간쾌청, 역이사일, 이수세익성. 목석구전, 탁랑연공, 개압록강, 발원최원고이. 안당서, 고려마자수, 출말갈지백산, 색약압두 고호압록강. 소위백산자, 즉장백산야. 산해경, 칭불함산, 아국칭백두산. 백두산, 위제강발원지조, 서남유자위압록강. 황여고운, 「천하유삼대수, 황하, 장강, 압록강야.」 양산묵담, 진정저, 운, 「자회이북위북조, 범수개종대하. 미유이강명자, 이북지재고려왈압록강.」 개시강야, 천하지대수야. 기발원지지, 방한방요, 난탁어천리지외야. 이금창세관지, 백산장림, 가이추지. 황차비심상진섭지지호. 금당성료, 정보의박, 개실고처, 중류초사, 역소난심. 조주자소실기세, 칙유비인력소가회선. 일행역원질원고사, 고청퇴기, 만윤 이재학, 역송친비, 위만수일. 이정사견이시일, 위도강지기, 상계이서전일시의.
paragraphs.en: At first we stayed at the Uiju guesthouse in Yongman. After ten days the tribute goods had all arrived and the date of departure pressed hard; but one rain turned into a long downpour, and both rivers rose in flood together. In between, the weather cleared for four days, yet the water only grew greater. Timbers and boulders rolled along together, and muddy waves joined the sky, for the Amnok has the most distant source of all. According to the Tang shu, the Majasu of Goguryeo issues from the White Mountain of the Malgal, and its color is like a duck’s head, hence the name Amnok, “Duck-Green.” The so-called White Mountain is Mount Changbai. The Shanhai jing calls it Mount Buxian; in our country it is called Mount Baekdu. Mount Baekdu is the ancestor of the sources of many rivers, and what flows to the southwest is the Amnok River. The Huangyu kao says: “There are three great waters under heaven: the Yellow River, the Yangzi, and the Amnok.” The Liangshan motan, by Chen Ting, says: “From the Huai northward is the northern branch, and all waters take the Great River as their ancestor. None of them is named a jiang; but in the north, in Goryeo, there is one called the Amnok jiang.” Truly this river is one of the great waters of the world. At the place where it rises, whether drought or flood prevails now is hard to judge from a thousand li away. But judging by the swelling of the water today, one can infer that long rains have fallen on the White Mountain. How much more so when this is no ordinary ford! Now, at the height of the flood, the stepping-stones and the mooring places have all lost their old positions, and the shoals and sandbars in mid-stream are hard to make out. If the boatmen lose their command of the current even slightly, there are things that human strength cannot turn back. The interpreters of the party, citing precedents in turn, firmly asked for a postponement, and the Magistrate of Uiju, Yi Jae-hak, also sent a close aide-de-camp to hold us back a few days. But the Chief Envoy insisted on this very day as the day for crossing the river, and the date and hour had already been entered in the report to the throne.

paragraphs.orig: 朝起開牕, 濃雲密布, 雨意彌山。 盥櫛已罷, 整頓行李。 手封家書及諸處答札, 出付撥便。 於是略啜早粥, 徐往舘所。 諸裨已著軍服戰笠矣。 頂起銀花雲月, 懸孔雀羽, 腰繫藍方紗紬纏帶, 佩環刀, 手握短鞭。 相視而笑曰, 「貌樣何如。」 盧參奉以漸上房裨將, 視帖裏時, 更加豪健矣。 帖裏方言天翼, 裨將我境則著帖裏, 渡江則換着狹袖。 鄭進士珏上房裨將 笑迎曰 「今日眞得渡江矣。」 盧從傍曰, 「乃今將渡江矣。」 余皆應曰 「唯唯。」 盖一旬留館, 擧懷支離之意, 皆畜奮飛之氣。 加以霖雨江漲, 益生躁鬱, 及此期日倐屆, 則雖欲無渡, 不可得也。 遙瞻前途, 溽暑蒸人, 回想家鄕, 雲山渺漠。 人情到此, 安得無憮然退悔。 所謂平生壯遊, 恒言曰, 「不可不一觀」云者, 眞屬第二義。 其曰,「今日渡江」云者, 非快暢得意之語, 「乃無可奈何」之意耳。 譯官金震夏, 二上堂, 以年老病重, 落後而去。 辭別鄭重, 不覺悵然。
paragraphs.reading: 조기개창, 농운밀포, 우의미산. 관즐이파, 정돈행리. 수봉가서급제처답찰, 출부발편. 어시약철조죽, 서왕관소. 제비이착군복전립의. 정기은화운월, 현공작우, 요계남방사주전대, 패환도, 수악단편. 상시이소왈, 「모양하여.」 노참봉이점상방비장, 시첩리시, 갱가호건의. 첩리방언천익, 비장아경즉착첩리, 도강칙환착협수. 정진사각상방비장 소영왈 「금일진득도강의.」 노종방왈, 「내금장도강의.」 여개응왈 「유유.」 개일순유관, 거회지리지의, 개축분비지기. 가이임우강창, 익생조울, 급차기일숙계, 칙수욕무도, 불가득야. 요첨전도, 욕서증인, 회상가향, 운산묘막. 인정도차, 안득무무연퇴회. 소위평생장유, 항언왈, 「불가불일관」운자, 진속제이의. 기왈,「금일도강」운자, 비쾌창득의지어, 「내무가내하」지의이. 역관김진하, 이상당, 이연로병중, 낙후이거. 사별정중, 불각창연.
paragraphs.en: In the morning I got up and opened the window; thick clouds were spread dense, and the look of rain filled the hills. When I had washed and combed my hair, I put the baggage in order. I sealed with my own hands the letters home and the replies to various quarters, and handed them to the courier. Then I sipped a little early gruel and walked slowly to the guesthouse. The aides were already in military dress and battle hats. On their crowns they wore silver flowers and cloud-and-moon ornaments and hung peacock feathers; at the waist they tied a sash of indigo square-woven silk; they wore curved swords at their sides and held short whips in their hands. We looked at one another and laughed. “How do I look?” No I-jeom, the cham-bong, an aide of the Chief Envoy’s quarters, looked more vigorous than ever in his tieli. (Tieli is the vernacular word for cheonik, the military robe; within our own borders the aides wear the tieli, and on crossing the river they change to narrow sleeves.) Jeong Gak, the jinsa, another aide of the Chief Envoy’s quarters, greeted me with a laugh: “Today we truly get to cross the river!” No said from the side, “Now at last we are about to cross the river.” I answered, “Yes, yes.” For ten days of lodging at the guesthouse we had all nursed weariness at the dragging on, and all of us were storing up a spirit to fly. On top of that, the long rains and the swollen river had bred in us still more restlessness and gloom; and now that the appointed day had suddenly arrived, we could not have avoided crossing even if we had wished not to. Looking far down the road ahead, I saw the sultry heat steaming the people; looking back toward home, I thought of its clouds and hills, vast and faint. When a man’s feelings come to this point, how could he not feel dismay and regret? What is called the grand tour of a lifetime, which we always said “one must see,” is truly only of secondary meaning. And when we say “Today we cross the river,” it is no phrase of delighted satisfaction; it means rather “There is nothing to be done.” The interpreter Gim Jin-ha, a second-ranked senior interpreter, because of his age and grave illness, fell behind and went away. His farewell was solemn, and I felt downcast without knowing it.

paragraphs.orig: 朝飯後, 余獨先一騎而出。 馬紫騮而白題, 脛瘦而蹄高, 頭銳而腰短, 竦其雙耳, 眞有萬里之想矣。 昌大前控, 張福後囑, 鞍掛雙囊。左硯右鏡, 筆二墨一, 小空冊四卷, 程里錄一軸。 行裝至輕, 搜檢雖嚴, 可以無虞矣。 未及城門, 而驟雨一陣。 從東而至, 遂促鞭而行, 下馬城闉。 獨步上樓, 俯視城底, 獨昌大持馬而立, 不見張福。 少焉, 張福出立道傍小角門。 望上望下, 攲笠遮雨, 手提烏瓷小壺, 颯颯而來。 盖兩人者, 自檢其囊中得廿六文。 而東錢有禁, 不可出境, 棄之道則可惜, 故沽酒。 云 「問汝輩能飮幾何」, 皆對不能近口。 余罵曰 「竪子惡能飮乎。」 又自慰曰, 「遠道一助」, 於是悄然獨酌 。東望龍鐵諸山, 皆入萬重雲矣。 滿酌一盞, 酹第一柱, 自祈利涉。 又斟一杯, 酹第二柱, 爲張福昌大祈。 搖壺則猶餘數杯, 使昌大酹地禱馬。
paragraphs.reading: 조반후, 여독선일기이출. 마자류이백제, 경수이제고, 두예이요단, 송기쌍이, 진유만리지상의. 창대전공, 장복후촉, 안괘쌍낭. 좌연우경, 필이묵일, 소공책사권, 정리록일축. 행장지경, 수검수엄, 가이무우의. 미급성문, 이취우일진. 종동이지, 수촉편이행, 하마성인. 독보상루, 부시성저, 독창대지마이입, 불견장복. 소언, 장복출입도방소각문. 망상망하, 기입차우, 수제오자소호, 삽삽이내. 개양인자, 자검기낭중득입육문. 이동전유금, 불가출경, 기지도칙가석, 고고주. 운 「문여배능음기하」, 개대불능근구. 여매왈 「수자오능음호.」 우자위왈, 「원도일조」, 어시초연독작. 동망용철제산, 개입만중운의. 만작일잔, 뇌제일주, 자기이섭. 우짐일배, 뇌제이주, 위장복창대기. 요호칙유여수배, 사창대뇌지도마.
paragraphs.en: After breakfast I went out alone, ahead of the others, on one horse. The horse was a dark chestnut with a white blaze, thin in the shanks and high in the hoof, sharp of head and short in the loins; it pricked up both its ears, and truly seemed to have ten thousand li in mind. Changdae led it from the front and Jang Bok followed behind. At the saddle hung a pair of bags: on the left an inkstone, on the right a mirror; two brushes and one inkstick, four small blank notebooks, and one scroll for recording the stages of the road. My traveling gear was extremely light; however strict the search, I could have no fear. Before I reached the city gate a sudden shower came upon us from the east, so I urged on my whip and went on, and dismounted at the gate. I climbed the tower alone and looked down to the foot of the wall: only Changdae stood there holding the horse, and Jang Bok was nowhere to be seen. Presently Jang Bok came out and stood at a small side gate by the road. He looked up the road and down it, tilting his hat to keep off the rain, carrying a small black porcelain flask in his hand, and came hurrying toward me. The two of them, it seems, had searched their own bags and found twenty-six coins; and since eastern coins were forbidden and could not be taken beyond the border, and it would be a pity to throw them away on the road, they had bought wine. I said, “Let me ask how much you fellows can drink,” and both answered that they could scarcely bring it to their lips. I scolded them: “Brats, how could you drink?” Then I consoled myself: “It will help me on the long road.” And so, forlorn, I drank alone. Looking east toward the mountains of Yongcheon and Cheolsan, I saw them all gone into ten thousand layers of cloud. I filled a cup and poured a libation to the first pillar, praying for a safe crossing. I poured another cup and poured a libation to the second pillar, praying for Jang Bok and Changdae. When I shook the flask there were still a few cups left, and I had Changdae pour them on the ground as a prayer for the horse.

paragraphs.orig: 倚墻東望, 蒸雲乍騰。 白馬山城西邊一峯, 忽露半面, 其色深靑。 恰似吾燕岩書堂, 望見佛日後峯矣。
paragraphs.reading: 의장동망, 증운사등. 백마산성서변일봉, 홀노반면, 기색심청. 흡사오연암서당, 망견불일후봉의.
paragraphs.en: Leaning against the wall, I looked east. Steaming clouds were just rising. One peak on the west side of Baengma Fortress suddenly showed half its face, a deep blue-green. It looked exactly like the rear peak of Buril, seen from my Yeonam study.

paragraphs.orig: 紅粉樓中別莫愁秋風數騎出邊頭畵船簫鼓無消息斷膓淸南第一州
paragraphs.reading: 홍분루중별막수추풍수기출변두화선소고무소식단장청남제일주
paragraphs.en: In the rouge-and-powder tower I took leave of Mochou; / on the autumn wind, a few horsemen ride out to the frontier. / Painted boat, flute and drum—no news of them now; / it breaks the heart, that first town south of the Cheong.

paragraphs.orig: 此柳惠風入瀋陽時作也。 余浪咏數回, 獨自大笑曰, 「此出疆人漫作無聊語爾。 安得有畵船簫皷哉。」 昔荊卿將渡易水, 頃之未發。 太子疑其改悔, 請先遣秦舞陽。 荊軻怒叱曰, 「僕所以留者, 待吾客與俱。」 此荊卿漫作無聊語耳。 若疑荊卿改悔, 則可謂淺之知荊卿, 而荊卿所待之客, 亦未必有姓名其人也。 夫提一匕首, 入不測之强秦, 已多一秦舞陽, 復安用他客耶。 寒風歌筑, 聊盡今日之歡而已。 然而作者曰, 「其人居遠未來。」 巧哉其居遠也。 其人者, 天下之至交也。 是期也, 天下之大信也。 以天下之至交, 臨一往不返之期, 夫豈日暮而不至哉。 故其人所居未必楚吳三晉之遠, 亦未必以是日爲入秦之期, 而有握手丁寧之約也。 只在荊卿意中, 忽待是客, 作之者乃就荊卿意中之客. 而演之曰其人。 其人者, 所不知何人也。 以所不知何人而曰居遠, 爲荊卿慰之。 又恐其人之或來也。 則曰, 「未來」, 爲荊卿幸之耳。 誠若天下眞有其人, 吾且見之矣。 其人身長七尺二寸, 濃眉綠髯, 下豊上銳, 何以知其然也。 吾讀惠風此詩知之矣。 惠風名得恭 號泠齋。
paragraphs.reading: 차유혜풍입심양시작야. 여낭영수회, 독자대소왈, 「차출강인만작무료어이. 안득유화선소고재.」 석형경장도역수, 경지미발. 태자의기개회, 청선견진무양. 형가노질왈, 「복소이유자, 대오객여구.」 차형경만작무료어이. 약의형경개회, 칙가위천지지형경, 이형경소대지객, 역미필유성명기인야. 부제일비수, 입불측지강진, 이다일진무양, 부안용타객야. 한풍가축, 요진금일지환이이. 연이작자왈, 「기인거원미래.」 교재기거원야. 기인자, 천하지지교야. 시기야, 천하지대신야. 이천하지지교, 임일왕불반지기, 부기일모이부지재. 고기인소거미필초오삼진지원, 역미필이시일위입진지기, 이유악수정령지약야. 지재형경의중, 홀대시객, 작지자내취형경의중지객. 이연지왈기인. 기인자, 소부지하인야. 이소부지하인이왈거원, 위형경위지. 우공기인지혹내야. 칙왈, 「미래」, 위형경행지이. 성약천하진유기인, 오차견지의. 기인신장칠척이촌, 농미녹염, 하풍상예, 하이지기연야. 오독혜풍차시지지의. 혜풍명득공 호영재.
paragraphs.en: This was written by Yu Hye-pung when he entered Shenyang. I chanted it aloud several times, then laughed to myself: “This is the idle, aimless talk of a man leaving his country. How could there be painted boats, flutes and drums?” Long ago, when Jing Ke was about to cross the Yi River, he lingered a while and did not set out. The Crown Prince suspected that he had changed his mind, and asked to send Qin Wuyang ahead. Jing Ke angrily rebuked him: “The reason I have stayed is to wait for my guest to go with me.” This too was Jing Ke’s idle, aimless talk. If one suspected Jing Ke of having changed his mind, one would be shallow in one’s knowledge of Jing Ke; and the guest Jing Ke was waiting for most likely had neither name nor person. For a man carrying a single dagger into the unfathomable might of Qin already has one Qin Wuyang too many; what further use would he have for another companion? Singing to the zhu in the cold wind, he meant only to take his fill of that day’s joy, and nothing more. And yet the author wrote, “That man lived far away and had not yet come.” How clever, that he lived far away! That man was the closest friend under heaven; that appointment was the greatest trust under heaven. Would a man of the closest friendship under heaven, facing a day of departure from which there is no return, fail to come though the day grew dark? So the place where that man lived was not necessarily as far off as Chu, Wu or the Three Jin, nor was that day necessarily the day set for entering Qin, with a promise sealed by earnest clasping of hands. It was only in Jing Ke’s mind: he suddenly waited for this guest, and the author took the guest in Jing Ke’s mind and elaborated him as “that man.” “That man”—someone no one knows. To say of someone no one knows that “he lives far away” is to console Jing Ke. And then, fearing that the man might in fact come, he says “has not yet come,” to bring Jing Ke luck. If there truly were such a man in the world, I should have seen him. That man is seven chi two cun tall, with thick eyebrows and a green beard, broad below and narrow above. How do I know it? I know it from reading Hye-pung’s poem. Hye-pung’s given name was Deuk-gong, and his pen name was Yeongjae.

paragraphs.orig: 正使前排拂拂出城, 旗幟棍棒之屬。 排立於前, 故謂之前排。 來源與周主簿雙行矣。 來源, 余三從弟, 周主簿名命新, 俱上房裨將。 鞭鞘仗脇, 聳身據鞍, 肩高項長, 非不驍勇。 而坐下衾袋 太厖氄, 僕夫藁鞋, 遍掛鞍後。 來源軍服, 靑苧也。 舊件新浣, 鬅騰郭索, 可謂太崇儉矣。 稍俟副使之出城, 乃按轡徐行最後, 至九龍亭, 卽發船所也。 灣尹已設幕出待, 而書狀淸晨先出, 與灣尹眼同搜檢, 例也。 方校閱人馬, 人籍姓名, 居住, 年甲, 髯疤有無, 身材短長, 馬錄其毛色。 立三旗爲門, 搜其禁物, 大者如黃金, 眞珠, 人參, 貂皮及包外濫銀, 小者新舊名目, 不下數十種, 瑣雜難悉。 廝隷則披衣摸袴, 裨譯則解視行裝衾袋衣褓。 披猖江岸, 皮箱紙匣, 狼藉草莽, 爭自收拾, 睊睊相顧。 大抵不檢, 則無以防姦, 搜之則有傷軆貌, 而其實文具而已。 灣賈之先期潛越。 有誰禁之, 禁物之現捉於初旗者, 重棍而公屬, 其物入中旗者, 刑配, 入第三旗者, 梟首示衆, 其立法則嚴矣。 今行原包猶未及半, 多空包者, 其濫銀奚論。
paragraphs.reading: 정사전배불불출성, 기치곤봉지속. 배입어전, 고위지전배. 내원여주주부쌍행의. 내원, 여삼종제, 주주부명명신, 구상방비장. 편초장협, 용신거안, 견고항장, 비불효용. 이좌하금대 태방용, 복부고혜, 편괘안후. 내원군복, 청저야. 구건신완, 붕등곽색, 가위태숭검의. 초사부사지출성, 내안비서행최후, 지구룡정, 즉발선소야. 만윤이설막출대, 이서상청신선출, 여만윤안동수검, 예야. 방교열인마, 인적성명, 거주, 연갑, 염파유무, 신재단장, 마녹기모색. 입삼기위문, 수기금물, 대자여황금, 진주, 인참, 초피급포외남은, 소자신구명목, 불하수십종, 쇄잡난실. 시례칙피의모고, 비역칙해시행장금대의보. 피창강안, 피상지갑, 낭자초망, 쟁자수습, 견견상고. 대저불검, 칙무이방간, 수지칙유상체모, 이기실문구이이. 만가지선기잠월. 유수금지, 금물지현착어초기자, 중곤이공속, 기물입중기자, 형배, 입제삼기자, 효수시중, 기입법칙엄의. 금행원포유미급반, 다공포자, 기남은해논.
paragraphs.en: The Chief Envoy’s front escort streamed out of the city—banners, flags, staves and the like. They line up in front, which is why they are called the “front escort.” Rae-won and Chief Clerk Ju rode as a pair. Rae-won is my third cousin; Ju Myeong-sin is the chief clerk; both are aides of the Chief Envoy’s quarters. Whipping the crop and gripping with their flanks, bodies erect in the saddle, shoulders high and necks long, they were certainly not lacking in valor. But the bedding bag under their seats was far too bulging, and the servants’ straw sandals were hung all over the back of the saddle. Rae-won’s military uniform was of blue ramie, an old garment freshly washed, rumpled and crackling; one might say he took thrift too far. I waited a little until the Deputy Envoy had left the city, then let the reins go and rode slowly, last of all, to Guryongjeong, the Pavilion of Nine Dragons, which is the embarkation point. The Magistrate of Uiju had already set up a tent and was waiting there; and the Secretary had gone out at dawn to inspect jointly with the Magistrate in person, as is the rule. They were checking men and horses: for the men, they registered name, residence, age, whether they had a beard or scars, and height; for the horses, they recorded the color of the coat. Three flags were set up as a gate, and prohibited goods were searched for. The large items were such things as gold, pearls, ginseng and sable, and silver beyond what was packed in the bundles; the small items, of old and new designations, numbered not fewer than several dozen kinds, too petty and trivial to list in full. Servants were made to open their coats and feel their trousers; aides and interpreters had to unfasten and inspect their baggage, bedding bags and clothing bundles. Scattered all over the riverbank, leather trunks and paper boxes lay in disorder in the weeds, and the owners scrambled to gather them up, glaring at one another. In general, if one does not inspect, there is nothing to guard against smuggling; but searching damages dignity, and in fact it is mere formality. The Uiju merchants slip across ahead of time—who is there to stop them? Prohibited goods caught at the first flag bring heavy flogging and confiscation; those that get as far as the middle flag, penal exile; those that get as far as the third flag, beheading and public display of the head; the law is certainly strict. On this journey the original bundles were not even half filled, and many were empty bundles—to say nothing of the excess silver.

paragraphs.orig: 茶啖草草, 乍進旋退, 葢急於渡江, 無人下箸。 船只五隻, 如京江之津船, 而其制稍大。 先濟方物及人馬, 正使所乘, 載表咨文及首譯以下上房帶率同船, 副使書狀並其帶率合乘一船。 於是龍灣吏校房妓通引及平壤陪行營吏啓書等, 皆於船頭, 次第拜辭。 上房馬頭, 順安奴, 名時大, 唱謁未了, 篙師擧槳一刺, 水勢迅疾。 棹歌齊唱, 努力奏功, 星奔電邁, 怳若隔晨。 統軍亭楹楯欄檻, 八面爭轉辭別者, 猶立沙頭, 而渺渺如荳。 余謂洪君命福(首譯)曰, 「君知道乎。」 洪拱曰, 「 惡, 是何言也。」 余曰, 「道不難知, 惟在彼岸。」 洪曰, 「所謂誕先登岸耶。」 余曰, 「非此之謂也。 此江乃彼我交界處也。 非岸則水。 凡天下民彛物則, 如水之際岸。 道不他求, 卽在其際。」 洪曰, 「敢問何謂也。」 余曰, 「人心惟危, 道心惟微。 泰西人辨幾何一畫, 以一線諭之。 不足以盡其微, 則曰, 有光無光之際, 乃佛氏臨之曰, 不卽不離。 故善處其際, 惟知道者能之。 鄭之子產。」
paragraphs.reading: 다담초초, 사진선퇴, 개급어도강, 무인하저. 선지오척, 여경강지진선, 이기제초대. 선제방물급인마, 정사소승, 재표자문급수역이하상방대솔동선, 부사서상병기대솔합승일선. 어시용만이교방기통인급평양배행영리계서등, 개어선두, 차제배사. 상방마두, 순안노, 명시대, 창알미료, 고사거장일자, 수세신질. 도가제창, 노력주공, 성분전매, 황약격신. 통군정영순란함, 팔면쟁전사별자, 유입사두, 이묘묘여두. 여위홍군명복(수역)왈, 「군지도호.」 홍공왈, 「오, 시하언야.」 여왈, 「도불난지, 유재피안.」 홍왈, 「소위탄선등안야.」 여왈, 「비차지위야. 차강내피아교계처야. 비안칙수. 범천하민이물칙, 여수지제안. 도불타구, 즉재기제.」 홍왈, 「감문하위야.」 여왈, 「인심유위, 도심유미. 태서인변기하일획, 이일선유지. 부족이진기미, 칙왈, 유광무광지제, 내불씨임지왈, 부즉불리. 고선처기제, 유지도자능지. 정지자산.」
paragraphs.en: The tea and refreshments were hasty, set out and taken away again; everyone was so eager to cross that no one lifted his chopsticks. There were only five boats, like the ferries of Gyeonggang, though somewhat larger in build. First the tribute goods, men and horses were ferried across. The Chief Envoy’s boat carried the memorial and the diplomatic notes, and the Chief Interpreter and the retinue of the Chief Envoy’s quarters rode in the same boat; the Deputy Envoy and the Secretary, with their retinues, shared one boat. Then Yongman’s clerks, officers, courtesans and attendants, and the Pyeongyang escort’s yamen clerks and report-writers, all bowed their farewells in order at the bow. The chief groom of the Chief Envoy’s quarters, a slave from Sunan named Si-dae, had not finished his announcement when the boatmen heaved their poles and the current rushed. The rowing song rose in chorus, “Put forth your strength, achieve the task!” and we sped like shooting stars and racing lightning, till it seemed we were a whole morning away. The pillars and railings of the Tonggunjeong Pavilion turned about on all eight sides, and those who stood on the sand-head to bid us farewell were already faint, small as peas. I said to Hong Myeong-bok, the Chief Interpreter, “Do you know the Way?” Hong folded his hands: “Oh! What kind of talk is that?” I said, “The Way is not hard to know. It lies only on the other shore.” Hong said, “You mean ‘first to climb onto the shore’?” I said, “That is not what I mean. This river is where they and we meet at the border. If it is not bank, it is water. All the norms of men and the laws of things under heaven are like the water’s edge at the bank. The Way is not to be sought elsewhere; it lies precisely in that edge.” Hong said, “May I ask what you mean?” I said, “‘The human mind is perilous; the mind of the Way is subtle.’ When the Westerners explain a single stroke in geometry, they illustrate it with a line; and when that does not exhaust its subtlety, they say it is ‘the boundary between light and no light.’ Approaching it, the Buddhists say: ‘Neither the same nor apart.’ Therefore only one who knows the Way can deal well with that edge. Zichan of Zheng.”

paragraphs.orig: 船已泊岸, 蘆荻如織, 下不見地。 下隷輩爭下岸折蘆荻, 忙掇船上茵席, 欲爲鋪設。 而蘆根如戟, 黑土泥濃。自正使以下, 茫然露立於蘆荻中矣。 問, 「人馬先渡者何去。」 左右對曰, 「不知。」 又問, 「方物安在。」 又對曰, 「不知。」 遙指九龍亭沙岸曰 「一行人馬太半未濟。 彼蟻屯者是也。」 遙望龍灣, 一片孤城, 如晒匹練, 城門如針孔。 漏出天光, 如一點晨星。 有大筏乘漲而下, 時大遙呼曰, 「位。」 盖呼聲也, 位者, 尊稱也。 有一人起立應聲曰 「爾們的不時節, 緣何朝貢入大國, 暑天裏長途, 辛苦時大。」 又問, 「爾們的那地人民往何處砍木。」 答曰 「俺等俱鳳城居住, 往長白山砍來。」 說猶未了, 筏已杳然去矣。 時兩江合漲, 而中間爲孤島。 人馬先濟者, 誤爲下此, 相距雖五里, 無船復渡。 遂嚴勅兩船篙工, 速濟人馬, 則對以逆漲行船, 非時日可及。 使臣皆躁怒, 欲治領船灣校, 而無軍牢。 軍牢亦先渡, 誤下於中島故耳。 副房裨將李瑞龜, 不勝忿憤, 叱副旁馬頭, 捽入灣校。 而無可覆之地, 於是, 半開其臀, 以馬鞭略扣四五。 喝令拿出, 斯速擧行。 灣校一手著笠, 一手係袴, 連聲唱喏。
paragraphs.reading: 선이박안, 노적여직, 하불견지. 하례배쟁하안절노적, 망철선상인석, 욕위포설. 이노근여극, 흑토이농. 자정사이하, 망연노립어노적중의. 문, 「인마선도자하거.」 좌우대왈, 「부지.」 우문, 「방물안재.」 우대왈, 「부지.」 요지구룡정사안왈 「일행인마태반미제. 피의둔자시야.」 요망용만, 일편고성, 여쇄필련, 성문여침공. 누출천광, 여일점신성. 유대벌승창이하, 시대요호왈, 「위.」 개호성야, 위자, 존칭야. 유일인기립응성왈 「이문적불시절, 연하조공입대국, 서천리장도, 신고시대.」 우문, 「이문적나지인민왕하처감목.」 답왈 「엄등구봉성거주, 왕장백산감래.」 설유미료, 벌이묘연거의. 시양강합창, 이중간위고도. 인마선제자, 오위하차, 상거수오리, 무선부도. 수엄칙양선고공, 속제인마, 칙대이역창행선, 비시일가급. 사신개조로, 욕치영선만교, 이무군뢰. 군뢰역선도, 오하어중도고이. 부방비장이서구, 불승분분, 질부방마두, 졸입만교. 이무가복지지, 어시, 반개기둔, 이마편약구사오. 갈령나출, 사속거행. 만교일수착입, 일수계고, 연성창야.
paragraphs.en: The boat had reached the shore. Reeds and rushes grew woven thick, and one could not see the ground beneath. The servants scrambled ashore to cut the reeds, and hurriedly snatched the mats from the boat, wishing to spread them. But the reed roots were like halberds, and the black soil was thick with mud. From the Chief Envoy on down, we stood in the open amid the reeds, at a loss. I asked, “Where have the men and horses that crossed first gone?” Those around me answered, “We do not know.” I asked again, “Where are the tribute goods?” Again they answered, “We do not know.” Someone pointed far off to the sandbank at Guryongjeong: “Most of the party’s men and horses have not yet crossed. That swarm like ants over there is them.” Gazing toward Yongman, I saw one lonely town like a piece of bleached silk spread out to dry, and its city gate like the eye of a needle; the daylight leaking through it was like a single morning star. A great raft came down on the flood, and Si-dae called out from afar, “Wei!” This is a call, and wei is a term of respect. A man on the raft stood up and answered: “You people, coming in tribute to the Great Country at such an unseasonable time—a long road in the heat of summer, what hard going, Si-dae.” Si-dae asked again, “Where are you people of that place going to cut timber?” He answered, “We all live in Fengcheng; we cut it at Mount Changbai and bring it down.” Before he had finished speaking, the raft had vanished from sight. At that time both rivers had risen together, and in the middle lay a solitary island. The men and horses that had crossed first had landed there by mistake; though it was only five li away, there was no boat to cross again. We strictly ordered the boatmen of the two boats to ferry the men and horses over at once, but they replied that poling a boat against the flood could not be done in a matter of hours. The envoys were all irritable and furious and wished to punish the Uiju officer in charge of the boats, but there were no military orderlies; the orderlies too had crossed first and landed on the middle island by mistake. Yi Seo-gu, an aide of the Deputy Envoy’s quarters, unable to contain his rage, berated the Deputy Envoy’s chief groom and had the Uiju officer seized and dragged in. But there was no place where he could be laid down, so they bared half his buttocks and gave him four or five light strokes with a horsewhip. They shouted orders: “Carry it out at once!” The Uiju officer, holding his hat with one hand and tying up his trousers with the other, answered “Yes! Yes!” again and again.

paragraphs.orig: 驅下兩船篙工, 入水曳船, 而水勢悍急, 進寸退尺, 威令無所施少焉。 一隻船沿岸飛下, 軍牢領三房轎馬而來。 張福呼昌大曰, 「汝亦來乎 葢幸之也。」 使兩漢點視行裝, 則俱得無恙矣。 裨譯所騎, 或來或否。 於是正使先發軍牢一雙騎而吹角引路。 一雙步而前導, 颼飀穿蘆荻而行。 余於馬上拔佩刀, 斬蘆一竿。 皮堅肉厚而不堪作箭, 只合筆管矣。 一鹿驚起, 超越蘆荻, 如麥際飛鳥, 一行皆驚。 行十里至三江。 江淸如練, 名愛刺河。 而不知何處發源, 與鴨綠江相去不過十里, 而獨無潦漲之意。 其各地發源可知矣。 有兩隻船, 類我國上游船, 而長廣皆不及。 制甚堅緻, 刺船者皆鳳城人。 待此三日, 糧盡告飢云。 葢此河, 彼我不得往來之地。 而我國譯學及大國, 移咨不時, 有交關之事。 故鳳城將軍爲置船隻云, 船泊處甚沮洳。 余呼一胡曰,「位。」 葢俄者纔學于時大也。 其人欣然捨槳而來。 余騰身載其背, 其人笑嘻嘻入船。 出氣長息曰, 「黑旋風媽媽這樣沉挑時, 巴不得上了沂風嶺。」 趙主簿明會大笑。 余曰, 「彼鹵漢不知江革, 但知李逵。」 趙君曰 「所謂目不識丁。 正道此輩, 而稗官奇書。 皆其牙頰間常用例語。 所謂官話者是也”
paragraphs.reading: 구하양선고공, 입수예선, 이수세한급, 진촌퇴척, 위령무소시소언. 일척선연안비하, 군뢰영삼방교마이내. 장복호창대왈, 「여역내호 개행지야.」 사양한점시행장, 칙구득무양의. 비역소기, 혹내혹부. 어시정사선발군뢰일쌍기이취각인로. 일쌍보이전도, 수류천로적이행. 여어마상발패도, 참로일간. 피견육후이불감작전, 지합필관의. 일녹경기, 초월로적, 여맥제비조, 일행개경. 행십리지삼강. 강청여연, 명애자하. 이부지하처발원, 여압록강상거불과십리, 이독무요창지의. 기각지발원가지의. 유양척선, 유아국상유선, 이장광개불급. 제심견치, 자선자개봉성인. 대차삼일, 양진고기운. 개차하, 피아부득왕래지지. 이아국역학급대국, 이자불시, 유교관지사. 고봉성장군위치선척운, 선박처심저여. 여호일호왈,「위.」 개아자재학우시대야. 기인흔연사장이내. 여등신재기배, 기인소희희입선. 출기장식왈, 「흑선풍마마저양침도시, 파부득상료기풍령.」 조주부명회대소. 여왈, 「피노한부지강혁, 단지이규.」 조군왈 「소위목불식정. 정도차배, 이패관기서. 개기아협간상용예어. 소위관화자시야”
paragraphs.en: He drove the boatmen of both boats down into the water to haul the boats, but the current was fierce and hard, and for an inch gained they slipped back a foot; authority had nothing to bear on. Presently one boat came flying down along the bank; the military orderlies were leading the sedan-chair horses of the three quarters and came with them. Jang Bok called to Changdae, “You’ve come too?”—glad indeed to see him. I had the two fellows check the baggage, and everything was found safe. As for the horses of the aides and interpreters, some came and some did not. Then the Chief Envoy sent a pair of orderlies ahead on horseback, blowing a horn to lead the way, and another pair on foot to go in front; they went through the reeds, rustling. On horseback I drew the sword at my side and cut a single reed. Its skin was hard and its flesh thick, so it was no good for arrows, only fit for a pen shaft. A deer, startled, sprang up and leaped over the reeds like a bird flying over barley, and the whole party was startled. After ten li we came to Sanjiang, the Three Rivers. The river was clear as white silk; it is called the Aici River. No one knows where it rises; it is no more than ten li from the Amnok, yet it alone showed no sign of flooding. From this one can know that each river has its own source. There were two boats, like the boats of our upper rivers but not as long or as wide as they. They were of very sturdy and fine build, and the men poling them were all from Fengcheng. They said they had waited here three days, their food had run out, and they were hungry. This river is a place where they and we are not permitted to cross. But when our interpreters and the Great Country have diplomatic notes to exchange at irregular times, there is traffic, and so the General of Fengcheng provided boats, they said. The mooring place was very marshy. I called to one barbarian, “Wei!”—for I had just learned that from Si-dae. The man gladly dropped his oar and came. I leapt onto his back, and the man, grinning, waded into the boat. Panting, he said, “If Black Whirlwind’s old mother had been this heavy to carry, he’d have been dying to get up Yifeng Ridge!” Chief Clerk Jo Myeong-hoe laughed loudly. I said, “That boor does not know Jiang Ge; he knows only Li Kui.” Jo said, “It is what is called ‘not knowing a single character.’ These are exactly the type, and the fantastic tales and curious books of the novelists are all stock phrases always on their tongues. That is what is called guanhua, the official speech.”

paragraphs.orig: 河廣似我國臨津。 卽向九連城, 綠蕪列幕, 周羅虎網。 義州鎗軍, 處處伐木, 聲震原野。獨立高阜, 擧目四望, 山明水淸。 開局平遠, 樹木連天, 隱隱有大邨落, 如聞鷄犬之聲。 土地肥沃, 可以耕墾。 浿江以西, 鴨綠以東, 無與此比。 合置巨鎭雄府, 彼我兩棄, 遂成閒區。 或云, 「高句麗時, 亦甞都此」, 所謂國內城。 皇明時爲鎭江府。 今淸陷遼, 則鎭江民人, 不肯剃頭, 或投毛文龍, 或投我國。 其後投我者, 盡爲淸人所刷還, 投文龍者, 多死于劉海之亂矣。 其爲空地, 且將百餘年, 漠然徒見山高而水淸者是也。 行視諸露屯處, 譯官或三人一幕, 或五人同帳。 譯卒及刷馬驅人, 伍伍什什, 靠溪搆木, 炊烟相連。 人喧馬嘶, 儼成村閭, 灣商一隊, 自爲一屯。 臨溪洗數十鷄, 張網獵魚, 烹羹煑蔬, 飯顆明潤, 最爲豊腴。 良久副使書狀, 次第來到。 日旣黃昏, 設燎三十餘處, 皆鋸截連抱巨木。 達曙通明, 軍牢吹角一聲, 則三百餘人, 齊聲吶喊, 所以警虎也。 竟夜如此, 軍牢自灣府選待最健者, 一行皁隷中, 最多事而亦最多食云, 其打扮令人絶倒。 藍雲紋緞, 着裏氈笠, 鬉結高頂, 雲月懸茜紅, 毦毛帽前, 縷金着一個勇字。 鴉靑麻布, 狹袖戰服, 木紅綿布褙子, 腰繫藍方紗紬纏帶, 肩掛朱紅綿絲大絨, 足穿多耳麻鞋。 觀其身手, 果然是一對健兒也。 但所坐馬, 所謂半駙擔, 不鞍而駄, 非騎而踞, 背揷着正藍色小令旗, 一手持軍令版, 一手執筆硯蠅拂及一條如腕大馬家木短鞭, 口吹吶叭。 坐下斜揷十餘塗朱木棍。 各房少有號令, 則輒呼軍牢. 軍牢陽若未聞, 連呼十數次, 則口中剌剌的誶責, 始乃高聲應喏。 若初聞呼聲然, 一躍下馬, 豕奔牛喘, 而吶叭及軍令版筆硯等物, 都掛一肩, 曳了一棍而去矣。
paragraphs.reading: 하광사아국임진. 즉향구련성, 녹무열막, 주나호망. 의주쟁군, 처처벌목, 성진원야. 독입고부, 거목사망, 산명수청. 개국평원, 수목연천, 은은유대촌락, 여문계견지성. 토지비옥, 가이경간. 패강이서, 압록이동, 무여차비. 합치거진웅부, 피아량기, 수성한구. 혹운, 「고구려시, 역상도차」, 소위국내성. 황명시위진강부. 금청함요, 칙진강민인, 불긍체두, 혹투모문룡, 혹투아국. 기후투아자, 진위청인소쇄환, 투문룡자, 다사우유해지난의. 기위공지, 차장백여년, 막연도견산고이수청자시야. 행시제노둔처, 역관혹삼인일막, 혹오인동장. 역졸급쇄마구인, 오오십십, 고계구목, 취연상련. 인훤마시, 엄성촌려, 만상일대, 자위일둔. 임계세수십계, 장망엽어, 팽갱자소, 반과명윤, 최위풍유. 양구부사서상, 차제래도. 일기황혼, 설요삼십여처, 개거절연포거목. 달서통명, 군뢰취각일성, 칙삼백여인, 제성눌함, 소이경호야. 경야여차, 군뢰자만부선대최건자, 일행조례중, 최다사이역최다식운, 기타분영인절도. 남운문단, 착리전립, 종결고정, 운월현천홍, 이모모전, 누금착일개용자. 아청마포, 협수전복, 목홍면포배자, 요계남방사주전대, 견괘주홍면사대융, 족천다이마혜. 관기신수, 과연시일대건아야. 단소좌마, 소위반부담, 불안이태, 비기이거, 배삽착정람색소령기, 일수지군령판, 일수집필연승불급일조여완대마가목단편, 구취납팔. 좌하사삽십여도주목곤. 각방소유호령, 칙첩호군뢰. 군뢰양약미문, 연호십수차, 칙구중랄랄적수책, 시내고성응야. 약초문호성연, 일약하마, 시분우천, 이납팔급군령판필연등물, 도괘일견, 예료일곤이거의.
paragraphs.en: The river was as wide as our Imjin. Making straight for Jiuliancheng, we found green grass hung with curtain tents and tiger nets spread all around. The Uiju spearmen were felling timber here and there, and the sound shook the plain. Standing alone on a high mound, I lifted my eyes and looked all around: the mountains bright and the waters clear, the prospect open, level and distant, the trees joined to the sky, and dimly a large village, as if I heard the sound of chickens and dogs. The soil was fertile and could be tilled. West of the Pae River and east of the Amnok, there is nothing to compare with it. A great garrison and a mighty prefecture should have been set up here; but both they and we gave it up, and it became an idle region. Some say, “In Goguryeo times they once made their capital here as well”—the so-called Gungnaeseong. In the Ming it was Zhenjiang Prefecture. When the Qing took Liao, the people of Zhenjiang, unwilling to shave their heads, went over, some to Mao Wenlong and some to our country. Afterward all those who came to us were rounded up by the Qing and sent back, while those who went to Wenlong mostly died in the rebellion of Liu Hai. It has been empty ground now for nearly a hundred years and more, and all one sees, vacantly, is mountains high and waters clear—that is what it is. Walking about to look at the various bivouacs, I found that the interpreters were three men to a tent, or five to a tent, while the interpreters’ soldiers and the packhorse drivers, in fives and tens, had built shelters of timber by the stream, their cooking smoke running one into another. With the noise of men and the neighing of horses it had become a regular village; the Uiju merchants, a company by themselves, made their own camp. By the stream they washed several dozen chickens, spread nets to catch fish, boiled soups and stewed vegetables; the grains of rice were bright and glossy, and the fare was very rich. After a long while the Deputy Envoy and the Secretary arrived in turn. By the time it was dusk, fires were lit in more than thirty places, all of them logs sawn off, too thick to be embraced. They burned bright until dawn; when a military orderly blew a horn once, over three hundred people shouted together at the top of their voices—this was to scare the tigers. So it went all night. The military orderlies are chosen from the strongest men at the Uiju prefecture; among the party’s menials, they are said to have the most business and also to eat the most, and their get-up makes one collapse with laughter. A hat of indigo cloud-patterned satin, a felt hat with a lining, horsehair knotted high on the crown, a cloud-and-moon ornament hung with madder red, plumes of feather-fur before the hat, and the single character “valor” worked in gold thread. A narrow-sleeved battle tunic of raven-blue hemp cloth, a jacket of reddish-brown cotton, at the waist a sash of indigo square-woven silk, over the shoulder a great vermilion cotton-silk tassel, and on their feet many-eared hemp sandals. Looking at their build and hands, they were indeed a pair of sturdy fellows. But the horse they ride is what is called a “half-load horse”: without a saddle but loaded, not riding but squatting; on the back a small indigo command flag was stuck, in one hand they held a command tablet, and in the other a brush, an inkstone, a fly-whisk and a short whip of Ma-family wood as thick as a wrist, while the mouth blew a trumpet. Beneath the seat, at a slant, were stuck a dozen or so vermilion-painted wooden staves. Whenever any quarter issues the slightest order, it calls for the orderly. The orderly pretends not to hear; when called a dozen times in a row, he mutters scolding under his breath, and only then answers aloud, “Yes!” As if hearing the call for the first time, he leaps down from the horse, running like a pig and panting like an ox, with trumpet, command tablet, brush and inkstone all hung on one shoulder, and dragging a staff, off he goes.

paragraphs.orig: 夜未半. 大雨暴霔。帳幕上漏 ,草氣下濕, 無處可避。 少焉開霽, 天星四垂, 若可捫也。
paragraphs.reading: 야미반. 대우폭주. 장막상누,초기하습, 무처가피. 소언개제, 천성사수, 약가문야.
paragraphs.en: Before midnight there was a sudden downpour of heavy rain. The tent leaked from above, the damp rose from the grass below, and there was no place to avoid it. Presently it cleared, and the stars hung down on all sides, as if one could touch them.

paragraphs.orig: ## 낚시를 하다
paragraphs.en: Fishing

paragraphs.orig: 二十五日壬申 (朝小雨 午晴)
paragraphs.reading: 이십오일임신 (조소우 오청)
paragraphs.en: The 25th day, imsin (a little rain in the morning; clear at noon).

paragraphs.orig: 各房及譯員等諸屯。 處處出晒衣衾。 見濕於夜雨故也。 刷馬驅人中, 有負酒而來。 戴宗, 宣川奴, 御醫卞主簿馬頭, 沽獻一甁, 遂相携臨溪命酌。 渡江後望絶東酒, 而今忽得之, 非但酒味大佳, 暇日臨流, 趣不可勝。 馬頭輩爭投竿釣魚。 余醉, 奪一緡投之, 卽得二小魚。 葢魚未慣釣故也。 以方物未及到, 又露宿九連城
paragraphs.reading: 각방급역원등제둔. 처처출쇄의금. 견습어야우고야. 쇄마구인중, 유부주이내. 대종, 선천노, 어의변주부마두, 고헌일병, 수상휴임계명작. 도강후망절동주, 이금홀득지, 비단주미대가, 가일임류, 취불가승. 마두배쟁투간조어. 여취, 탈일민투지, 즉득이소어. 개어미관조고야. 이방물미급도, 우노숙구련성
paragraphs.en: The various quarters and the interpreters at their camps everywhere put out their clothes and bedding to dry, because they had been soaked in the night rain. Among the packhorse drivers one came carrying wine: Dae-jong, a slave from Seoncheon, the groom of Byeon, the royal physician and chief clerk, bought a bottle and presented it, and so we took it with us to the stream and called for cups. After crossing the river we had given up hope of Eastern wine, and now suddenly to get some—not only was the wine very fine, but, on a day of leisure beside flowing water, the pleasure was beyond measure. The grooms vied with one another in casting rods to fish. Drunk, I seized a line and threw it in, and at once caught two small fish; the fish were not used to being angled for. Because the tribute goods had not yet arrived, we again slept in the open at Jiuliancheng.

paragraphs.orig: ## 강세작 이야기
paragraphs.en: The Story of Kang Shijue

paragraphs.orig: 二十六日癸酉 (朝霧晩晴)
paragraphs.reading: 이십육일계유 (조무만청)
paragraphs.en: The 26th day, gyeyu (fog in the morning; clear later).

paragraphs.orig: 發九連城, 行三十里, 到金石山下中火。 又行三十里, 露宿葱莠。
paragraphs.reading: 발구련성, 행삼십리, 도금석산하중화. 우행삼십리, 노숙총유.
paragraphs.en: We left Jiuliancheng, traveled thirty li, and ate the midday meal at the foot of Mount Jinshi. We traveled another thirty li and slept in the open at Congxiu.

paragraphs.orig: 旣曉, 冐霧發行。 上判事馬頭得龍, 與刷馬驅人輩, 談說康世爵事。 霧中遙指金石山曰, 「此荊州人康世爵所隱處。」 其說津津可聽。 葢世爵祖霖 從楊鎬東援我國, 死於平山。 父國泰官靑州通判, 萬曆丁巳, 坐事謫遼陽, 世爵年十八, 隨父在遼陽。 明年, 淸人陷撫順, 游擊將軍李永芳降, 經略楊鎬, 分遣諸將, 摠兵杜松出開原, 摠兵王尙乾出撫順, 摠兵李如栢出淸河, 都督劉綎出毛嶺。 國泰父子從劉綎。 淸伏兵從陿中出, 大軍前後不相救。 劉綎自燒死, 國泰中流矢仆。 世爵日暮得父屍, 埋谷中, 聚石以識之。 時朝鮮都元帥姜弘立, 副元帥金景瑞, 陣山上, 朝鮮左右營將, 陣山下。 世爵投元帥陣。 明日, 淸兵擊朝鮮左營, 無一人得脫。 山上軍望見皆股栗, 弘立不戰而降。 淸人圍弘立軍數匝, 搜明兵之竄入者, 反縛驅出, 皆劒斬之。 世爵被縛坐大石下, 主者忽忘而去。 世爵目朝鮮兵, 乞解其縛, 朝鮮兵相睥睨莫敢動。 世爵自以背磨之石, 楞縛繩斷, 遂起脫朝鮮死者衣, 換着之, 攛入朝鮮兵中以得免, 於是走還遼陽。
paragraphs.reading: 기효, 모무발행. 상판사마두득룡, 여쇄마구인배, 담설강세작사. 무중요지금석산왈, 「차형주인강세작소은처.」 기설진진가청. 개세작조림 종양호동원아국, 사어평산. 부국태관청주통판, 만력정사, 좌사적요양, 세작연십팔, 수부재요양. 명년, 청인함무순, 유격장군이영방항, 경략양호, 분견제장, 총병두송출개원, 총병왕상건출무순, 총병이여백출청하, 도독유정출모령. 국태부자종유정. 청복병종협중출, 대군전후불상구. 유정자소사, 국태중유시부. 세작일모득부시, 매곡중, 취석이지지. 시조선도원수강홍립, 부원수김경서, 진산상, 조선좌우영장, 진산하. 세작투원수진. 명일, 청병격조선좌영, 무일인득탈. 산상군망견개고율, 홍립부전이항. 청인위홍립군수잡, 수명병지찬입자, 반박구출, 개검참지. 세작피박좌대석하, 주자홀망이거. 세작목조선병, 걸해기박, 조선병상비예막감동. 세작자이배마지석, 능박승단, 수기탈조선사자의, 환착지, 찬입조선병중이득면, 어시주환요양.
paragraphs.en: At daybreak we set out through the fog. Deuk-ryong, the chief groom of the Chief Interpreter, was talking with the packhorse drivers about Kang Shijue. Pointing far into the fog toward Mount Jinshi, he said, “That is where Kang Shijue of Jingzhou hid.” His tale was enthralling to hear. Shijue’s grandfather Kang Lin followed Yang Hao on the eastern expedition to relieve our country and died at Pyeongsan. His father Kang Guotai was a subprefectural judge of Qingzhou; in the jeongsa year of Wanli, he was convicted in some affair and banished to Liaoyang, and Shijue, then eighteen, followed his father to Liaoyang. The next year the Qing took Fushun, and the Vanguard General Li Yongfang surrendered. The Military Commissioner Yang Hao sent out his generals in separate columns: the Regional Commander Du Song came out by Kaiyuan, the Regional Commander Wang Shangqian by Fushun, the Regional Commander Li Rubai by Qinghe, and the Commissioner Liu Ting by Maoling. Guotai and his son followed Liu Ting. The Qing hidden troops came out of a defile, and the great army, front and rear, could not rescue each other. Liu Ting burned himself to death, and Guotai was struck by a stray arrow and fell. At nightfall Shijue found his father’s corpse, buried it in a valley, and piled stones to mark it. At that time the Joseon commander-in-chief Gang Hong-rip and deputy commander Gim Gyeong-seo were encamped on the hill, and the Joseon left and right camp commanders were encamped below. Shijue went over to the commander-in-chief’s camp. The next day the Qing troops attacked Joseon’s left camp, and not one man escaped. The soldiers on the hill watched and all trembled in the thighs, and Hong-rip surrendered without a fight. The Qing surrounded Hong-rip’s army several times round, searched out the Ming soldiers who had slipped in, trussed them with their hands tied behind and drove them out, and cut them all down with swords. Shijue, bound, sat beneath a great stone, and the man in charge suddenly forgot him and went away. Shijue signaled with his eyes to the Joseon soldiers and begged them to untie his bonds, but the Joseon soldiers only glared at one another and none dared move. Shijue himself rubbed the rope with his back against the edge of the stone until the binding snapped; then he rose, stripped the clothes from a dead Joseon soldier, changed into them, darted in among the Joseon troops and so escaped, and then fled back to Liaoyang.

paragraphs.orig: 及熊廷弼鎭遼陽, 招世爵使復父讎。 是年, 淸人連陷開原鐵嶺, 則逮廷弼, 以薛國用代之。 世爵仍留薛軍中, 及瀋陽陷, 世爵晝伏夜行, 抵鳳凰城, 與廣寧人劉光漢, 收遼陽散卒, 共守之。 未幾, 光漢戰死, 世爵亦被十餘鎗。 自念中原路絶, 不如東出朝鮮, 猶得免薙髮左衽, 遂走穿塞, 隱金石山。 燎羊裘, 裹木葉以咽之, 數月得不死。 遂渡鴨綠江, 遍歷關西諸郡, 轉入會寧。 遂娶東婦生二子, 世爵年八十餘卒。 子孫蕃衍, 至百餘人. 而猶同居云。 得龍, 嘉山人也, 自十四歲, 出入燕中, 今三十餘次。 最善華語, 行中大小事例, 非得龍, 莫可當此任者。 已經本郡及龍鐵等諸府中軍, 階得嘉善。 而每使行, 則預關本郡, 囚其次知, 家屬, 謂之次知, 以防其逃避。 其爲人之幹能可知。 方世爵初出時, 客得龍家, 與得龍祖善, 互學華東語。 得龍之善漢語, 乃其家學云。
paragraphs.reading: 급웅정필진요양, 초세작사복부수. 시년, 청인연함개원철령, 칙체정필, 이설국용대지. 세작잉유설군중, 급심양함, 세작주복야행, 저봉황성, 여광령인유광한, 수요양산졸, 공수지. 미기, 광한전사, 세작역피십여쟁. 자염중원노절, 불여동출조선, 유득면치발좌임, 수주천새, 은금석산. 요양구, 과목엽이연지, 수월득불사. 수도압록강, 편역관서제군, 전입회령. 수취동부생이자, 세작연팔십여졸. 자손번연, 지백여인. 이유동거운. 득룡, 가산인야, 자십사세, 출입연중, 금삼십여차. 최선화어, 행중대소사례, 비득룡, 막가당차임자. 이경본군급용철등제부중군, 계득가선. 이매사행, 칙예관본군, 수기차지, 가속, 위지차지, 이방기도피. 기위인지간능가지. 방세작초출시, 객득룡가, 여득룡조선, 호학화동어. 득룡지선한어, 내기가학운.
paragraphs.en: When Xiong Tingbi took command of Liaoyang, he summoned Shijue so that he might avenge his father. That year the Qing took Kaiyuan and Tieling in succession; Tingbi was arrested and Xue Guoyong replaced him. Shijue remained in Xue’s army, and when Shenyang fell, he traveled hidden by day and moving at night, reached Fenghuangcheng, and with Liu Guanghan of Guangning gathered the scattered soldiers of Liaoyang and defended it together. Before long Guanghan died in battle, and Shijue too was pierced by more than ten spears. He thought to himself that the road to the Central Plain was cut; it would be better to go out east to Joseon and still escape the shaved head and the left-fastened robe. So he ran, passed through the palisade, and hid on Mount Jinshi. He singed his sheepskin coat and, wrapping it in tree leaves, swallowed it, and for several months he did not die. Then he crossed the Amnok River, passed through all the counties of the Northwest, and moved on to Hoeryeong. There he married a Joseon wife and had two sons; Shijue died at over eighty. His descendants flourished to over a hundred people, and they are said to be still living together. Deuk-ryong is a man of Gasan, and from the age of fourteen he has gone in and out of Yan, now more than thirty times. He is the best at Chinese; in all the matters, great and small, of the party, none but Deuk-ryong could take on this task. He has already served as commander of the garrison of his own county and of the prefectures of Yongcheon and Cheolsan and the like, and has attained the rank of gaseon. And at every mission, an order is sent in advance to his home county, imprisoning his chaji, his family—they are called chaji—to prevent his fleeing. From this one can know his ability. When Shijue first came out, he lodged at Deuk-ryong’s house and was a good friend of Deuk-ryong’s grandfather, and they taught each other Chinese and Korean. Deuk-ryong’s skill in Chinese is said to be his family learning.

paragraphs.orig: 日旣暮, 抵葱莠。 恰似平山葱莠。 想我國人所名, 抑平山葱秀, 以類爲名否。
paragraphs.reading: 일기모, 저총유. 흡사평산총유. 상아국인소명, 억평산총수, 이유위명부.
paragraphs.en: At sunset we reached Congxiu. It looked just like Chongsu in Pyeongsan. I suppose it was named so by our countrymen; or was Chongsu in Pyeongsan named after it, by resemblance?

paragraphs.orig: ## 책문에 들어서다
paragraphs.en: Entering the Border Gate

paragraphs.orig: 二十七日甲戌 (朝霧晩晴)
paragraphs.reading: 이십칠일갑술 (조무만청)
paragraphs.en: The 27th day, gapsul (fog in the morning; clear later).

paragraphs.orig: 平明發行。 路逢五六胡人, 皆騎小驢。 帽服繿縷, 容貌疲殘。 皆鳳城甲軍, 往戍愛刺河, 而雇人倩往云, 「東方則誠無慮矣。 然中國邊備可謂踈矣。」 馬頭及刷馬驅人輩, 喝令下驢, 前行兩胡, 下驢側行, 後行三胡, 不肯下驢。 馬頭輩齊聲叱下, 則怒目直視曰, 「爾們的大人干我甚事。」 馬頭直前奪其鞭, 擊其赤脚曰 「吾們的大人, 陪奉是何等物件, 賫來是何等文書, 黃旗上明明的寫着萬歲爺御前上用。 爾們好不患瞎, 還不認過了皇上御用的。」 其人下驢伏地, 稱死罪, 一人起抱咨文馬頭腰, 滿面歡笑曰, 「老爺息怒。 小人們該死的。」 馬頭輩皆大笑, 叱令叩頭謝罪, 皆跪伏于泥中, 以首頓地。 黃泥滿額, 一行皆大笑, 叱令退去。 余曰 「聞汝輩入中國, 多惹鬧端云, 吾今目覩, 果驗前聞。 俄者亦涉不緊, 此後切勿因戱起鬧。」 皆對曰 「不如此, 長途永,日 無以消遣。」
paragraphs.reading: 평명발행. 노봉오륙호인, 개기소려. 모복람루, 용모피잔. 개봉성갑군, 왕수애자하, 이고인천왕운, 「동방칙성무려의. 연중국변비가위소의.」 마두급쇄마구인배, 갈령하여, 전행양호, 하여측행, 후행삼호, 불긍하여. 마두배제성질하, 칙로목직시왈, 「이문적대인간아심사.」 마두직전탈기편, 격기적각왈 「오문적대인, 배봉시하등물건, 재내시하등문서, 황기상명명적사착만세야어전상용. 이문호불환할, 환불인과료황상어용적.」 기인하여복지, 칭사죄, 일인기포자문마두요, 만면환소왈, 「노야식로. 소인문해사적.」 마두배개대소, 질령고두사죄, 개궤복우이중, 이수돈지. 황니만액, 일행개대소, 질령퇴거. 여왈 「문여배입중국, 다야료단운, 오금목도, 과험전문. 아자역섭불긴, 차후절물인희기료.」 개대왈 「불여차, 장도영,일 무이소견.」
paragraphs.en: We set out at first light. On the road we met five or six barbarians, all riding small donkeys. Their caps and clothes were in rags, and their faces worn out. They were all armored soldiers of Fengcheng going to garrison the Aici River, and had hired men to go in their place, it was said. “In the East we truly have nothing to worry about. But China’s border defenses may be called lax.” The grooms and the packhorse drivers shouted orders to dismount from the donkeys; the two in front got off and walked to one side, but the three behind refused to get down. The grooms shouted together for them to get off, and they glared and said straight out, “What does your Great Man have to do with me?” The groom stepped straight forward, seized his whip, and struck his bare feet: “What kind of thing is our Great Man escorting, what kind of documents is he carrying? On the yellow banner it is plainly written ‘For the Use of His Majesty.’ Are you blind? Don’t you even recognize what is for the Emperor’s use?” The men dismounted and threw themselves on the ground, calling themselves deserving of death; one stood up and embraced the waist of the groom who carried the diplomatic notes, laughing all over his face: “Master, calm your anger. We little ones deserve to die.” The grooms all laughed loudly and ordered them to kowtow in apology; they all knelt in the mud and knocked their heads on the ground. Their foreheads were covered with yellow mud. The whole party burst out laughing and ordered them to be gone. I said, “I have heard that when you people go into China you stir up a great deal of trouble. Now I have seen it with my own eyes, and the old report is confirmed. That just now was a bit uncalled for, too; from now on, be careful never to start trouble in jest.” They all answered, “If we didn’t do this, we’d have nothing to pass the time on the long road and the long days.”

paragraphs.orig: 望見鳳凰山, 恰是純石造成。 拔地特起, 如擘掌立指, 如半開芙蓉, 如天末夏雲。 秀峭戌削, 不可名狀, 而但欠淸潤之氣。 甞謂我京道峯三角, 勝於金剛。 何則, 金剛卽其洞府所謂萬二千峯, 非不奇峻雄深, 獸挐禽翔, 仙騰佛跌, 而陰森渺冥, 如入鬼窟。 余甞與申元發登斷髮嶺, 望見金剛山。 時方秋天深碧, 夕陽斜映, 無干霄秀色, 出身潤態, 未甞不爲金剛一歎。 及自上流舟下, 出頭尾江口, 西望漢陽, 三角諸山, 摩霄出靑, 微嵐淡靄, 明媚婀娜。 又甞坐南漢南門, 北望漢陽, 如水花鏡月。 或曰, 「光風浮空, 乃旺氣也。」 旺氣者, 王氣也。 爲我京億萬載龍盤虎踞之勢, 其靈明之氣, 宜異乎他山也。 今此山勢之奇峭峻拔, 雖過道峯三角, 而其浮空光氣, 大不及漢陽諸山矣。
paragraphs.reading: 망견봉황산, 흡시순석조성. 발지특기, 여벽장입지, 여반개부용, 여천말하운. 수초술삭, 불가명상, 이단흠청윤지기. 상위아경도봉삼각, 승어금강. 하칙, 금강즉기동부소위만이천봉, 비불기준웅심, 수나금상, 선등불질, 이음삼묘명, 여입귀굴. 여상여신원발등단발령, 망견금강산. 시방추천심벽, 석양사영, 무간소수색, 출신윤태, 미상불위금강일탄. 급자상류주하, 출두미강구, 서망한양, 삼각제산, 마소출청, 미람담애, 명미아나. 우상좌남한남문, 북망한양, 여수화경월. 혹왈, 「광풍부공, 내왕기야.」 왕기자, 왕기야. 위아경억만재용반호거지세, 기영명지기, 의이호타산야. 금차산세지기초준발, 수과도봉삼각, 이기부공광기, 대불급한양제산의.
paragraphs.en: We saw Mount Fenghuang, which seemed built entirely of solid stone. It stood up straight from the ground, like a hand spread with the fingers pointing up, like a half-opened lotus, like a summer cloud at the edge of the sky. Lofty and steep, carved and cut, it could not be named; only it lacked the air of freshness and moisture. I have always said that Dobong and Samgak near our capital are better than Geumgang. Why? Geumgang is a grotto-heaven of its own, the so-called Twelve Thousand Peaks; it is not that they are not strange, steep, mighty and deep, with beasts clawing and birds soaring, immortals ascending and Buddhas squatting; but it is gloomy and dim, as if one were entering a ghost’s cave. Once I climbed Danbal Pass with Sin Won-bal and looked at Mount Geumgang. It was then the deep blue of autumn, with the evening sun slanting across; it lacked the exquisite color that touches the heavens, or the glossy bearing of a form just emerging, and I never failed to sigh once for Geumgang. And when I went down the river by boat from the upper reaches and came out at the mouth of the Dumi River and looked west to Hanyang, the mountains of Samgak, brushing the sky, rose blue, with faint mists and light haze, bright, charming and graceful. Another time I sat at the South Gate of Namhan and looked north to Hanyang, and it was like flowers in water, a moon in a mirror. Someone said, “The light wind floating in the air is the air of prosperity.” The air of prosperity is the royal air. It means that our capital has the terrain of the coiled dragon and the crouching tiger for ten thousand ages, and its luminous spirit must surely differ from that of other mountains. Now the steepness and strength of this mountain, though it surpasses Dobong and Samgak, is far inferior to the mountains of Hanyang in the light and air that float above it.

paragraphs.orig: 原野平濶, 雖不耕墾, 而處處砍柴根杮狼藉。 牛蹄轍跡, 縱橫艸間, 已知其近柵, 而居民之尋常出柵, 亦可驗矣。 疾驅行七八里, 抵柵外。 羊豕彌山, 朝烟繚靑, 刳木樹柵, 畧識經界。 可謂,折柳樊圃矣。 柵門覆以苫草, 板扉深鎖。 離柵數十步, 設三使幕次。 少憩, 方物齊到, 露積柵外。 群胡觀光者列立柵內, 無不口含烟竹。 光頭搖扇, 或黑貢緞衣 或秀花紬衣, 或生布生苧, 或三升布, 或野繭絲。 袴亦如之。 所佩繽紛, 或繡囊, 三四小佩刀, 皆揷雙牙箸。 烟袋, 如胡盧樣, 或繡刺花草禽鳥, 又古人名句。 譯官及諸馬頭輩, 爭立柵外, 兩相握手。 殷勤勞問, 群胡問,「你在王京那日起程, 在途時得免天水麽。家裏都是太平麽。 充得包銀麽。」 人人酬酢如出一口, 又爭問 「韓相公安相公來麽。」 此數人者, 俱義州人, 歲歲販燕, 皆巨猾, 習知燕中事。所謂相公者, 商賈相尊之稱也。
paragraphs.reading: 원야평활, 수불경간, 이처처감시근폐랑자. 우제철적, 종횡초간, 이지기근책, 이거민지심상출책, 역가험의. 질구행칠팔리, 저책외. 양시미산, 조연요청, 고목수책, 약식경계. 가위,절유번포의. 책문복이점초, 판비심쇄. 이책수십보, 설삼사막차. 소게, 방물제도, 노적책외. 군호관광자열립책내, 무불구함연죽. 광두요선, 혹흑공단의 혹수화주의, 혹생포생저, 혹삼승포, 혹야견사. 고역여지. 소패빈분, 혹수낭, 삼사소패도, 개삽쌍아저. 연대, 여호로양, 혹수자화초금조, 우고인명구. 역관급제마두배, 쟁입책외, 양상악수. 은근노문, 군호문,「이재왕경나일기정, 재도시득면천수마. 가리도시태평마. 충득포은마.」 인인수초여출일구, 우쟁문 「한상공안상공내마.」 차수인자, 구의주인, 세세판연, 개거활, 습지연중사. 소위상공자, 상가상존지칭야.
paragraphs.en: The plain was broad and open; though it was not tilled, stumps and wood chips from the cutting of firewood lay strewn about everywhere. Ox hoofprints and wheel ruts crossed and recrossed amid the grass; I knew already that we were near the palisade, and that the inhabitants went out beyond the palisade as a matter of course. Riding hard for seven or eight li, we arrived outside the palisade. Sheep and pigs covered the hills, morning smoke wound in blue; hollowed logs were set up as a palisade, only roughly marking the boundary. It could be called “breaking willow branches to fence a garden.” The Border Gate was covered with thatch, and its plank doors were deeply barred. Some tens of paces from the palisade the tents for the three envoys were set up. We rested a little; the tribute goods all arrived and were stacked in the open outside the palisade. Crowds of barbarians who had come to watch stood in line inside the palisade, every one with a pipe in his mouth. Bareheaded and waving fans, some in clothes of black tribute satin, some in fine flowered pongee, some in raw cloth or raw ramie, some in coarse three-sheng cloth, some in wild-silk; their trousers were the same. What they wore at the belt was profuse: embroidered pouches, three or four small knives, each with a pair of ivory chopsticks. Their tobacco pouches, shaped like gourds, were embroidered with flowers, grasses, birds, and also famous lines of ancient men. The interpreters and all the grooms jostled to stand outside the palisade, and shook hands with them on both sides. With earnest greetings the barbarian crowds asked: “What day did you set out from the royal capital? On the road, did you escape the heavenly waters? Is everyone at home at peace? Was your silver bundle filled?” Everyone answered as with one mouth, and they also vied to ask, “Are Mr. Han and Mr. An coming?” These several men were all Uiju people who traded in Yan year after year; they were all great crafty fellows, and well versed in the affairs of Yan. The “Mr.” here is the term merchants use to honor one another.

paragraphs.orig: 使行時, 例給正官八包。 正官者, 裨譯共三十員。 八包者, 舊時, 官給正官, 人人蔘幾斤, 謂之八包。 今不官給 令自備銀, 只限包數。 堂上包銀三千兩, 堂下二千兩。 自帶入燕, 貿易諸貨爲奇羡。 貧不能自帶, 則賣其包窠松都, 平壤, 安州等處, 燕商買其包窠 充銀以去。 然諸處燕商, 法不得身自入燕, 將包交付灣人, 貿易以來。 如韓林諸賈, 連歲入燕, 視燕如門庭, 與燕市裨販, 連膓互肚。 兌發低仰, 都在其手, 燕貨之日增厥價, 亶由此輩。 擧國都不理會, 專責譯官。 譯官失權於灣賈, 拱手而已。 諸處燕商, 雖知爲灣賈之所操縱, 而事非目覩, 則敢怒而不敢言。 其來已久, 今者灣賈之蹔爲隱身, 不卽相見, 亦一鉤引小數也。
paragraphs.reading: 사행시, 예급정관팔포. 정관자, 비역공삼십원. 팔포자, 구시, 관급정관, 인인삼기근, 위지팔포. 금불관급 영자비은, 지한포수. 당상포은삼천량, 당하이천량. 자대입연, 무역제화위기선. 빈불능자대, 칙매기포과송도, 평양, 안주등처, 연상매기포과 충은이거. 연제처연상, 법부득신자입연, 장포교부만인, 무역이래. 여한임제가, 연세입연, 시연여문정, 여연시비판, 연장호두. 태발저앙, 도재기수, 연화지일증궐가, 단유차배. 거국도불리회, 전책역관. 역관실권어만가, 공수이이. 제처연상, 수지위만가지소조종, 이사비목도, 칙감노이불감언. 기내이구, 금자만가지잠위은신, 부즉상견, 역일구인소수야.
paragraphs.en: On a mission, the principal officials are customarily granted eight bundles. The principal officials are the interpreters and aides, thirty in all. “Eight bundles”: in the old days, the state granted each principal official so many catties of ginseng apiece, which was called the “eight bundles.” Now the state no longer grants it, and they provide the silver themselves, with only a limit on the number of bundles. The silver in the bundles of senior officials is three thousand taels, and of junior officials two thousand. They carry it into Yan themselves and trade it for various goods for the profit. If a man is too poor to carry it himself, he sells his bundle-quota in places like Songdo, Pyeongyang and Anju, and the Yan merchants buy the quota, fill it with silver and carry it off. But by law the Yan merchants of the various places may not enter Yan in person; they hand the bundles over to the Uiju men and have them trade and bring back the goods. Merchants such as Han and Im, who go into Yan year after year, treat Yan like their front yard and are connected gut to gut with the middlemen of the Yan market. The fixing of exchange, its high and low, is all in their hands; that the price of Yan goods rises day by day is due solely to this lot. The whole nation pays no attention, and lays the entire responsibility on the interpreters. The interpreters, having lost their authority to the Uiju traders, fold their hands and do nothing. The merchants of the various places, though they know they are manipulated by the Uiju traders, since the matter is not before their eyes, dare to be angry but dare not speak. It has been so for a long time; today the Uiju traders’ temporarily hiding themselves and not meeting us at once is also a little trick of luring us on.

paragraphs.orig: 朝飯於柵外, 整頓行裝, 則雙囊左鑰, 不知去處。 遍覔草中, 終未得。 責張福曰 「汝不存心行裝, 常常遊目, 纔及柵門, 已有閪失。 諺所謂,‘三三程一日未行’, 若復行二千里, 比至皇城, 還恐失爾五臟。吾聞, 舊遼東及東岳廟, 素號姦細人出沒處, 汝復賣眼, 又未知幾物見失。」 張福閔然搔首曰, 「小人已知之兩處觀光時。小人當雙手護眼, 誰能拔之。」 余不覺寒心, 乃應之曰, 「善哉,」 葢福也。 年少初行, 性又至迷, 同行馬頭輩, 多以戲語誑之, 則福也眞個信聽。 每事所認, 皆此類也。 遠途所仗, 可謂寒心。
paragraphs.reading: 조반어책외, 정돈행장, 칙쌍낭좌약, 부지거처. 편멱초중, 종미득. 책장복왈 「여부존심행장, 상상유목, 재급책문, 이유서실. 언소위,‘삼삼정일일미행’, 약부행이천리, 비지황성, 환공실이오장. 오문, 구요동급동악묘, 소호간세인출몰처, 여부매안, 우미지기물견실.」 장복민연소수왈, 「소인이지지양처관광시. 소인당쌍수호안, 수능발지.」 여불각한심, 내응지왈, 「선재,」 개복야. 연소초행, 성우지미, 동행마두배, 다이희어광지, 칙복야진개신청. 매사소인, 개차류야. 원도소장, 가위한심.
paragraphs.en: I had breakfast outside the palisade and put the baggage in order; the left-hand lock of the paired saddlebags had gone missing, and no one knew where. I searched all through the grass but never found them. I scolded Jang Bok: “You take no care for the baggage and are always letting your eyes wander; we have barely reached the Border Gate and already something is lost. As the proverb says, ‘Three times three stages, and not a single day gone by.’ If we go two thousand li more, I fear that by the time we reach the imperial city you will have lost your five organs. I hear that old Liaodong and the Dongyue Temple have always been famed as places where spies come and go; if you sell your eyes again, who knows how many things will be lost.” Jang Bok sadly scratched his head: “I already know it. When I go sightseeing at those two places, I will protect my eyes with both hands; who can pull them out?” I could not help shuddering, and answered, “Good,” for Bok is young and on his first journey, and by nature utterly muddle-headed. The grooms who travel with us often fool him with jests, and Bok really believes them and listens. All that he takes in is of this kind. What we depend on for the long distance—one may well say it chills the heart.

paragraphs.orig: 復至柵外, 望見柵內, 閭閻皆高起五樑, 苫艸覆盖, 而屋脊穹崇, 門戶整齊。 街術平直, 兩沿若引繩, 然墻垣皆甎築。 乘車及載車, 縱橫道中, 擺列器皿, 皆畵瓷。 已見其制度絶無邨野氣, 往者洪友德保, 甞言大規模細心法。 柵門天下之東盡頭, 而猶尙如此, 前道遊覽, 忽然意沮, 直欲自此徑還, 不覺腹背沸烘。 余猛省曰 「此妒心也。 余素性淡泊, 慕羡猜妒, 本絶于中, 今一涉他境, 所見不過萬分之一, 乃復浮妄若是, 何也。 此直所見者小故耳, 若以如來慧眼, 遍觀十方世界, 無非平等, 萬事平等, 自無妒羡。」 顧謂張福曰, 「使汝往生中國何如。」 對曰 「中國胡也, 小人不願。」 俄有一盲人肩掛錦囊, 手彈月琴而行。 余大悟曰, 「彼豈非平等眼耶。」 少焉大開柵門, 鳳城將軍及柵門御史, 方來坐店房云。 群胡闐門而出, 爭閱視方物及私,卜輕重, 葢自此雇車而運也。 來觀使臣坐處, 含烟睥睨, 指點相謂曰, 「王子麽。」 宗室正使, 稱王子故也。 有認之者曰 「不是這個斑白的駙馬大人。 頃歲來的。」 指副使曰 「這髯的雙鶴補子, 乃是乙大人。」 指書狀曰 「三大人俱翰林出身的文官之稱也。」
paragraphs.reading: 부지책외, 망견책내, 여염개고기오량, 점초복개, 이옥척궁숭, 문호정제. 가술평직, 양연약인승, 연장원개전축. 승거급재거, 종횡도중, 파열기명, 개화자. 이견기제도절무촌야기, 왕자홍우덕보, 상언대규모세심법. 책문천하지동진두, 이유상여차, 전도유람, 홀연의저, 직욕자차경환, 불각복배비홍. 여맹성왈 「차투심야. 여소성담박, 모선시투, 본절우중, 금일섭타경, 소견불과만분지일, 내부부망약시, 하야. 차직소견자소고이, 약이여래혜안, 편관십방세계, 무비평등, 만사평등, 자무투선.」 고위장복왈, 「사여왕생중국하여.」 대왈 「중국호야, 소인불원.」 아유일맹인견괘금낭, 수탄월금이행. 여대오왈, 「피기비평등안야.」 소언대개책문, 봉성장군급책문어사, 방내좌점방운. 군호전문이출, 쟁열시방물급사,복경중, 개자차고거이운야. 내관사신좌처, 함연비예, 지점상위왈, 「왕자마.」 종실정사, 칭왕자고야. 유인지자왈 「불시저개반백적부마대인. 경세내적.」 지부사왈 「저염적쌍학보자, 내시을대인.」 지서상왈 「삼대인구한림출신적문관지칭야.」
paragraphs.en: Going back outside the palisade, I looked inside it, and saw that the houses in the villages were all raised high on five beams, covered with thatch, their ridges lofty and towering, their doors and windows neat. The streets were level and straight, and both sides of the road were as if drawn with a cord; the walls were all of brick. Riding carts and loaded carts crisscrossed the road, and the utensils on display were all painted porcelain. I could see already that their way of building had absolutely no rustic air. Long ago my friend Hong Deok-bo used to speak of “large design, careful method.” The Border Gate is at the very eastern end of the world, and even so it is like this; as for the sights further on, I suddenly lost heart, and I wanted to turn straight back from here; my belly and back seethed hot without my noticing. I woke up sharply: “This is jealousy. By nature I am plain and detached; admiration and envy, suspicion and jealousy have by nature been cut off in me. Now I have only just stepped into another land, and seen no more than a ten-thousandth of it, and I am already so frivolous and wild—why? It is only because what I have seen is small. If with the Tathagata’s wisdom eye I surveyed the worlds of the ten directions, none would be other than equal; with all things equal, there would naturally be no jealousy or envy.” Turning to Jang Bok, I said, “What if you were reborn in China?” He answered, “China is barbarian; I don’t want it.” Just then a blind man passed with a brocade bag hung on his shoulder, strumming a moon lute as he walked. I was greatly enlightened: “Is that not the equal eye?” Presently the Border Gate was thrown wide open, and the General of Fengcheng and the censor of the Border Gate were coming to sit in the inn, it was said. The barbarian crowds poured out of the gate and jostled to inspect the tribute goods and the private goods and weigh them, for from here the carts were hired to carry them. They came to watch where the envoys were sitting, pipes in their mouths, eyeing them askance, pointing and saying to one another, “Is that the prince?” This was because the Chief Envoy, being of the royal clan, was called a prince. One who recognized him said, “No, this is that gray-haired Prince Consort Great Man. He came some years ago.” Pointing at the Deputy Envoy: “This one with the beard and the double-crane insignia is the Second Great Man.” Pointing at the Secretary: “The Third Great Man—all of them Hanlin-trained”: this is the term for civil officials.

paragraphs.orig: 溪邊有喧讙爭辨之聲, 而語音啁啾。 莫識一句, 急往觀之, 得龍方與群胡, 爭禮物多寡也。 禮單贈遺時, 攷例分給, 而鳳城姦胡, 必增名目, 加數要責。 其善否, 都係上判事馬頭。 若値生手, 不嫺漢語, 則不能爭詰, 都依所要。 今歲如此, 則明年已成前例, 故必爭之。 使臣不知此理, 常急於入柵, 必促任譯, 任譯又促馬頭, 其弊原久矣。 象三, 上判事馬頭, 方分傳禮單, 群胡環立者百餘人。 衆中一胡, 忽高聲罵象三, 得龍奮髯張目, 直前揪其胸, 揮拳欲打。 顧謂衆胡曰, 「這個潑皮好無禮, 往年大膽, 偸老爺鼠皮項子, 又去歲, 欺老爺睡了, 拔俺腰刀, 割取了鞘綬, 又割了俺所佩的囊子。 爲俺所覺送, 與他一副老拳, 作知面禮。 這個萬端哀乞, 喚俺再生的爺孃, 今來年久, 還欺老爺。 不記面皮好大膽高聲大叫如此。 鼠子輩拿首了鳳城將軍。」 衆胡齊聲勸解, 有一老胡, 美鬚髯衣服鮮麗, 前抱得龍腰曰, 「請大哥息怒。」 得龍回怒作哂曰, 「若不看賢弟面皮時這部, 截筒鼻一拳, 歪在鳳凰山外。」 其擧措恇攘可笑。 趙判事達東來立余傍, 余爲說俄間光景, 可惜獨觀。 趙君笑曰 「這是殺威棒法。」 趙君促得龍曰, 「使道今將入柵, 禮單 火速分給。」 得龍連聲唱喏, 故作遑遽之色。 余故久立詳觀所給物件名目, 極爲恠雜。

paragraphs.en: By the stream there was a clamor of wrangling, and the speech was chirping and twittering. I could not make out a single phrase, and hurried over to look: Deuk-ryong was disputing with a crowd of barbarians over the amount of the gifts. When the gift lists are handed over, they are distributed according to precedent; but the crafty barbarians of Fengcheng always add new items and demand more. Whether it goes well or not depends entirely on the Chief Interpreter’s groom. If it falls to a green hand who is not fluent in Chinese, he cannot argue the point, and gives them all they demand. If it is so this year, next year it will already have become precedent, and so one must contest it. The envoys, not knowing this principle, are always anxious to enter the palisade, and press the appointed interpreters, who press the grooms in turn; this abuse is of long standing. Sangsam, the Chief Interpreter’s groom, was distributing the gift lists, and over a hundred barbarians stood around him in a ring. Among the crowd one barbarian suddenly shouted abuse at Sangsam. Deuk-ryong shook his beard and glared, strode forward, grabbed him by the chest and raised a fist to hit him. Turning to the crowd of barbarians he said: “This ruffian is shockingly rude. In years past he had the cheek to steal His Honor’s rat-skin collar; and last year, taking advantage of my sleeping, he drew the saber from my waist, cut off the sheath-cord, and cut off the pouch I wore as well. When I found out, I gave him a good old fist as a first-meeting gift. This fellow begged ten thousand ways, calling me the father and mother who gave him new life. Now, after all these years, he bullies His Honor again. Not minding my face, how bold, to shout so loudly! You rats—I’ll haul you before the General of Fengcheng!” The crowd all shouted together to calm him. An old barbarian with a fine beard and bright clothes stepped forward, embraced Deuk-ryong’s waist and said, “Please, elder brother, calm your anger.” Deuk-ryong turned from anger to a snicker: “If it weren’t for my worthy brother’s face, this fist would have flattened your tube of a nose and sent you sprawling beyond Mount Fenghuang!” His behavior in his bluster was laughable. The interpreter Jo Dal-dong came and stood beside me; I told him what had just happened, regretting that he had missed it. Jo said, laughing, “That is the ‘show of force’ technique.” Jo pressed Deuk-ryong: “The envoy is about to enter the palisade; hand out the gift lists quickly.” Deuk-ryong answered “Yes, yes” again and again, putting on a flustered look. I deliberately stood a long time observing the names of the items distributed; they were extremely strange and miscellaneous.

paragraphs.orig: 群胡不做一聲, 肅然受去。 趙君曰 「得龍能則能矣。 彼往歲元無失, 揮項刀囊等事。 公然惹閙, 罵折一人, 衆人自沮。 皆面面相顧, 無聊卻立。 若不如此, 雖三日不决, 無入柵之期矣。」 已而, 軍牢跪告曰 「門上御史, 鳳城將軍出坐收稅廳。」 於是三使次第入柵 狀啓例付義州鎗軍而回矣 一入此門 則中土也 鄕園消息 從此絶矣 悵然東面而立良久 轉身緩步入柵
paragraphs.reading: 군호부주일성, 숙연수거. 조군왈 「득룡능칙능의. 피왕세원무실, 휘항도낭등사. 공연야료, 매절일인, 중인자저. 개면면상고, 무료각립. 약불여차, 수삼일불결, 무입책지기의.」 이이, 군뢰궤고왈 「문상어사, 봉성장군출좌수세청.」 어시삼사차제입책 상계예부의주쟁군이회의 일입차문 칙중토야 향원소식 종차절의 창연동면이입양구 전신완보입책
paragraphs.en: The barbarian crowd uttered not a sound, but solemnly received them and went off. Jo said, “Deuk-ryong is capable, to be sure. But those fellows last year had in fact lost no collars, sabers or pouches. He openly stirred up a row, cursed and broke one man, and the others lost heart. They all looked at one another, with nothing to say, and backed away. If it were not done so, even three days would not settle it, and there would be no date for entering the palisade.” Presently a military orderly knelt and reported: “The censor of the gate and the General of Fengcheng have come out and are seated in the tax-collection office.” Then the three envoys entered the palisade in order. The report to the throne, as usual, was entrusted to the Uiju spearmen and went back. Once one enters this gate, it is the Middle Land; news of one’s home village is cut off from here. Sadly I stood facing east for a long time; then I turned and walked slowly into the palisade.

paragraphs.orig: 路右有草廳三間, 自御史將軍下至衙譯, 分班列椅而坐, 首譯以下拱手前立。 使臣至此, 馬頭叱隷, 「停轎。」 乍脫驂若將卸駕者, 因卽疾驅而過。 副三房亦如之, 有若相救者, 令人捧腹。 裨將譯官, 皆下馬步過, 獨卞季涵騎馬突過。 末坐一胡, 忽以東話高聲大罵曰, 「無禮無禮。 幾位大人坐此, 外國從官, 焉敢唐突。 遄告使臣, 打臀可也。」 聲雖嘶哮, 舌强喉澁, 如乳孩弄嬌, 醉客使癡。 此卽護行通官雙林云。 首譯對曰 「這是弊邦太醫官。 初行未諳事體。 且太醫, 奉國命, 隨護大大人, 大大人亦不敢擅勘。 諸老爺仰體皇上字小之念, 免其深究, 則益見大國寬恕之量。」 諸人皆點頭微笑曰 「是也是也。」 獨雙林視猛聲高, 怒氣未解。 首譯目余使去, 道逢卞君。 卞君曰 「大辱逢之。」 余曰 「臀字可慮。」 相與大笑, 遂聯袂行翫, 不覺讚歎。
