paragraphs.en: To the right of the road stood a thatched hall of three bays; from the censor and the general down to the yamen interpreters, they sat in ranks on chairs, divided into rows, and the Chief Interpreter and those below stood before them with hands folded. When the envoy arrived here, the grooms barked at the servants, “Halt the chair!” and made as if to unharness the side horses, then immediately whipped on and passed by. The Deputy Envoy’s and the Secretary’s parties did the same, as though rescuing one another, making people hold their bellies with laughter. The aides and interpreters all dismounted and passed on foot; only Byeon Gye-ham rode right through. A barbarian seated at the end suddenly shouted abuse loudly in the Eastern tongue: “Rude! Rude! Several Excellencies sit here, how dare a foreign attendant barge in! Quickly inform your envoy and give him a spanking on the buttocks!” Though his voice was hoarse and roaring, his tongue was stiff and his throat rough, like a suckling baby playing coy, a drunkard playing the fool. This, it was said, was the escort interpreter Shuanglin. The Chief Interpreter answered: “This is our country’s royal physician. It is his first journey, and he does not understand the proper form. Moreover, a physician, by national command, accompanies and protects the Great Great Lord, and the Great Great Lord himself dares not punish him on his own authority. If your lordships, honoring His Majesty’s thought of cherishing the small, would spare him a deep inquiry, it would show all the more the breadth of the Great Country’s tolerance.” They all nodded and smiled: “That’s right, that’s right.” Only Shuanglin glared fiercely, his voice high, his anger undiminished. The Chief Interpreter signaled me with his eyes to leave; on the road I met Byeon. Byeon said, “I met with a great humiliation.” I said, “The word ‘buttocks’ is cause for worry.” We laughed together, and linking arms went on to look about, and without noticing began to marvel.

paragraphs.orig: 柵內人家, 不過二三十戶, 莫不雄深軒鬯。 柳陰中挑出一竿靑帘, 相携而入, 東人已彌滿其中矣。 赤脚突鬢, 騎椅呼呶, 見余皆奔避出去。 主人大怒指着, 卞君道「不解事的官人, 好妨人賣買。」 戴宗撫其背曰, 「哥哥, 不必饒舌。 兩位老爺, 略飮一兩杯, 便當起身, 這等𩴌魀, 那敢橫椅。 蹔相回避, 卽當復來。 已飮的, 計還酒錢, 未飮的暢襟快飮, 哥哥放心。 先斟四兩酒。」 主人堆着笑臉道, 「賢弟, 往歲, 不曾瞧瞧麽。 這等𩴌魀於鬧攘裡, 都白喫一道烟, 走了罷那地覔酒錢。」 戴宗曰 「哥哥勿慮。 兩位老爺飮後卽起, 弟當盡驅這廝回店賣買。」 店主曰 「是也。 兩位都斟四兩麽。 各斟四兩麽。」 戴宗道 「每位四兩。」 卞君罵曰 「四兩酒誰盡飮之。」 戴宗笑曰, 「四兩非酒錢也, 乃酒重也。」 其卓上列置斟器, 自一兩至十兩。 各有其器, 皆以鍮鑞造觶, 出色似銀。 喚四兩酒, 則以四兩觶斟來。 沽酒者更不較量多少, 其簡便若此。 酒皆白燒露, 味不甚佳, 立醉旋醒。 周視鋪置, 皆整飭端方, 無一事苟且彌縫之法, 無一物委頓雜亂之形。 雖牛欄豚柵, 莫不疎直有度, 柴堆糞庤, 亦皆精麗如畵。 嗟乎, 如此然後始可謂之利用矣。 利用然後可以厚生, 厚生然後正其德矣。 不能利其用而能厚其生, 鮮矣。 生旣不足以自厚, 則亦惡能正其德乎。 正使已入鄂姓家, 主人身長七尺, 豪健鷙悍, 其母年近七旬, 滿頭揷花, 眉眼韶雅, 聞其子孫滿前云。
paragraphs.reading: 책내인가, 불과이삼십호, 막불웅심헌창. 유음중도출일간청렴, 상휴이입, 동인이미만기중의. 적각돌빈, 기의호노, 견여개분피출거. 주인대로지착, 변군도「불해사적관인, 호방인매매.」 대종무기배왈, 「가가, 불필요설. 양위노야, 약음일량배, 편당기신, 저등𩴌魀, 나감횡의. 잠상회피, 즉당부내. 이음적, 계환주전, 미음적창금쾌음, 가가방심. 선짐사량주.」 주인퇴착소검도, 「현제, 왕세, 부증초초마. 저등𩴌魀어요양리, 도백끽일도연, 주료파나지멱주전.」 대종왈 「가가물려. 양위노야음후즉기, 제당진구저시회점매매.」 점주왈 「시야. 양위도짐사량마. 각짐사량마.」 대종도 「매위사량.」 변군매왈 「사량주수진음지.」 대종소왈, 「사량비주전야, 내주중야.」 기탁상열치짐기, 자일량지십량. 각유기기, 개이유랍조치, 출색사은. 환사량주, 칙이사량치짐래. 고주자갱불교량다소, 기간편약차. 주개백소로, 미불심가, 입취선성. 주시포치, 개정칙단방, 무일사구차미봉지법, 무일물위돈잡란지형. 수우란돈책, 막불소직유도, 시퇴분치, 역개정려여화. 차호, 여차연후시가위지이용의. 이용연후가이후생, 후생연후정기덕의. 불능이기용이능후기생, 선의. 생기부족이자후, 칙역오능정기덕호. 정사이입악성가, 주인신장칠척, 호건지한, 기모연근칠순, 만두삽화, 미안소아, 문기자손만전운.
paragraphs.en: Inside the palisade there were no more than two or three dozen households, and all were stately and bright. From among the willows a blue banner stuck out on a pole; we went in arm in arm, and Eastern people already filled the place. Barefoot, with unruly hair, sitting astride chairs, they were shouting noisily, but seeing me they all dashed away out. The master was furious and pointed at Byeon: “Officials who don’t understand things, ruining trade!” Dae-jong patted his back: “Brother, no need to waste words. These two gentlemen will drink a cup or two and set off; those rascals, how dare they straddle chairs! They will step aside for a moment and come back. Those who have drunk will pay up for the wine; those who have not will drink freely—rest easy, brother. First pour four taels of wine.” The master piled on a smile: “Brother, last year, didn’t I see you? Rascals like that, in the commotion, just get a free smoke and run off—where am I to find the wine money?” Dae-jong said, “Don’t worry, brother. The two gentlemen will leave after drinking; I will drive these scoundrels back to the shop to trade.” The shopkeeper said, “Right. Four taels each for the two gentlemen? Four taels each?” Dae-jong said, “Four taels per man.” Byeon cursed: “Who can drink four taels of wine?” Dae-jong laughed: “Four taels is not the price of the wine, it is the weight of the wine.” On the counter were set measures from one tael up to ten, each with its own vessel, goblets all made of brass and tin that looked like silver. If you call for four taels of wine, they pour it with the four-tael goblet. Buyers of wine never again compare how much is in it; so convenient is it. The wine was all white spirit, not very good in taste, quickly drunk and quickly sobered. Looking all around at the arrangements, I found them all neat, orderly and upright, without a single makeshift or patched-over method, without a single object left drooping or in disorder. Even the ox pens and pig sties were neat, straight and measured, and the heaps of firewood and piles of manure were all as exquisite as paintings. Alas, only when it is like this can one begin to call it “making use of things.” With use made beneficial, then livelihood can be enriched; with livelihood enriched, then virtue is set right. Few are those who cannot make use beneficial yet can enrich their livelihood. If livelihood is not enough to enrich oneself, how can one set virtue right? The Chief Envoy had already entered the house of a man surnamed E. The master was seven chi tall, hearty and fierce; his mother, nearly seventy, had a head full of flowers and bright, graceful eyes, and it was said that her sons and grandsons filled the place before her.

paragraphs.orig: 點心後, 與來源及鄭進士, 出行觀翫鳳凰山。 離此六七里, 看其前面, 眞覺奇峭。 山中有安市城舊址, 遺堞尙存云. 非也。 三面皆絶險, 飛鳥莫能上, 惟正南一面稍平, 周不過數百步, 卽此彈丸小城, 非久淹大軍之地。 似是句麗時小小壘堡耳。 相携至大柳樹下納凉。 有井甎甃, 又磨治全石爲覆盖, 穿其兩傍, 劣容汲器。 所以防人墮溺, 且鄣塵土。 又水性本陰, 故使蔽陽養活水也。 井葢上設轆轤, 下垂雙綆, 結柳爲棬。 其形如瓢而深, 一上一下. 終日汲, 不勞人力。 水桶皆鐵箍, 以細釘緊約, 絶勝於綰竹。 爲經歲久則朽斷, 且桶身乾曝, 則竹箍自然寬脫。 所以鐵箍爲得也, 汲水皆肩擔而行, 謂之扁擔。 其法削一條木如臂膊大, 其長一丈, 兩頭懸桶, 去地尺餘, 水窸窣不溢。 惟平壤有此法, 然不肩擔而背負之故, 甚妨於窄路隘巷。其擔法又此爲得之。 昔鮑宣妻提瓮出汲, 余甞疑何不頭戴而手提之。 乃今見之, 婦人皆爲高髻不可戴矣。
paragraphs.reading: 점심후, 여내원급정진사, 출행관완봉황산. 이차육칠리, 간기전면, 진각기초. 산중유안시성구지, 유첩상존운. 비야. 삼면개절험, 비조막능상, 유정남일면초평, 주불과수백보, 즉차탄환소성, 비구엄대군지지. 사시구려시소소루보이. 상휴지대류수하납량. 유정전추, 우마치전석위복개, 천기양방, 열용급기. 소이방인타닉, 차장진토. 우수성본음, 고사폐양양활수야. 정개상설녹로, 하수쌍경, 결유위권. 기형여표이심, 일상일하. 종일급, 불로인력. 수통개철고, 이세정긴약, 절승어관죽. 위경세구칙후단, 차통신건폭, 칙죽고자연관탈. 소이철고위득야, 급수개견담이행, 위지편담. 기법삭일조목여비박대, 기장일장, 양두현통, 거지척여, 수실솔불일. 유평양유차법, 연불견담이배부지고, 심방어착로애항. 기담법우차위득지. 석포선처제옹출급, 여상의하부두대이수제지. 내금견지, 부인개위고계불가대의.
paragraphs.en: After the midday meal, I went out with Rae-won and the jinsa Jeong to see Mount Fenghuang. Six or seven li from here, looking at its front, I truly felt how strange and steep it is. Within the mountain are the old remains of Ansi Fortress, and the broken battlements still stand, it is said; this is not so. It is wholly precipitous on three sides, where birds cannot fly up; only the due south side is a little flat, and its circumference is no more than some hundreds of paces. This pellet-sized small fortress is not a place that could have detained a great army for long. It seems to be a small rampart of the Goguryeo period. Together we went to cool ourselves beneath a great willow tree. There was a well lined with brick, covered with a whole stone worked smooth, pierced on both sides, barely wide enough to admit a bucket. This is to prevent people from falling in and drowning, and also to keep out dust. Also, the nature of water is yin, so they cover it from the sun to keep the water alive. On the well cover was a windlass, with a pair of ropes hanging down, with willow-wood loops tied to them. Shaped like a gourd and deep, one going up and one going down, they draw water all day without tiring human strength. The water buckets are all iron-hooped, tightly bound with thin nails, far superior to binding with bamboo, which rots and snaps over the years, and when the bucket body dries in the sun, the bamboo hoops loosen and fall off by themselves. That is why iron hoops are better. They all carry the water on a shoulder pole, which is called a biandan. The method is to shave a piece of wood as thick as an arm, ten chi long, with a bucket hung at each end a foot or so off the ground, so that the water ripples but does not spill. Only Pyeongyang has this method, but because they carry on the back and not on the shoulder, it badly hampers narrow roads and alleys. This way of carrying is better than that. Long ago Bao Xuan’s wife carried a jar out to draw water, and I used to wonder why she did not carry it on her head instead of lifting it by hand. Now that I have seen this, I understand that the women all wear high topknots and cannot carry on their heads.

paragraphs.orig: 西南廣濶, 作平遠山淡沱水。
paragraphs.reading: 서남광활, 작평원산담타수.
paragraphs.en: To the southwest it was broad and open, making a picture of level, distant hills and pale, winding water.

paragraphs.orig: 千柳陰濃茅簷疎籬時露林間平堤綠蕪牛羊散牧遠橋行人有擔有携立而望之
paragraphs.reading: 천류음농모첨소리시노임간평제녹무우양산목원교행인유담유휴입이망지
paragraphs.en: A thousand willows, shade thick; thatched eaves and sparse hedges, now and then showing amid the trees; on the level bank, green grass, cattle and sheep scattered at pasture; at the distant bridge, travelers, some carrying loads on poles, some leading by the hand; I stood and gazed at it.

paragraphs.orig: 頓忘間者行役之憊。 兩人者爲觀新刱佛堂, 棄我而去。 有十餘騎揚鞭馳過, 皆繡鞍駿馬, 意氣揚揚。 見余獨立, 滾鞍下馬, 爭執余手, 致慇懃之意。 其中一人美少年, 余畫地爲字以語之, 皆俯首熟視, 但點頭而已, 似不識爲何語也。
paragraphs.reading: 돈망간자행역지비. 양인자위관신창불당, 기아이거. 유십여기양편치과, 개수안준마, 의기양양. 견여독립, 곤안하마, 쟁집여수, 치은근지의. 기중일인미소년, 여화지위자이어지, 개부수숙시, 단점두이이, 사불식위하어야.
paragraphs.en: I suddenly forgot the fatigue of travel of the past days. The two others had gone to see a newly built Buddhist hall and left me. A dozen or so riders swept past with their whips, all on embroidered saddles and fine horses, high-spirited. Seeing me standing alone, they rolled out of their saddles and dismounted, and vied to grasp my hands and show their cordial feeling. Among them was a handsome young man; I drew characters on the ground to speak to him, and they all bowed their heads and gazed at them, only nodding, as if they did not recognize what language it was.

paragraphs.orig: 有兩碑, 皆靑石。 一門上御史善政碑, 一稅官某善政碑。 俱滿州人四字名, 撰書者 亦俱滿州人。 文與筆俱拙, 但碑制極佳。 功費甚省, 此可爲法。 碑之兩傍, 不磨滑, 甎築夾碑爲墻, 沒碑頂。 因瓦覆爲屋, 碑在𥦔中, 以備風雨, 勝於建閣韜碑。 碑趺贔屭 及碑文兩邊, 所鐫覇夏, 可數毫髮。 此不過窮邊民家所建, 然其精緻古雅 不可當也。
paragraphs.reading: 유양비, 개청석. 일문상어사선정비, 일세관모선정비. 구만주인사자명, 찬서자 역구만주인. 문여필구졸, 단비제극가. 공비심생, 차가위법. 비지양방, 불마활, 전축협비위장, 몰비정. 인와복위옥, 비재𥦔중, 이비풍우, 승어건각도비. 비부비희 급비문양변, 소전패하, 가수호발. 차불과궁변민가소건, 연기정치고아 불가당야.
paragraphs.en: There were two steles, both of blue stone. One was a stele to the good government of the censor of the gate, the other to that of a certain tax officer. Both men had four-character Manchu names, and the composers and calligraphers were also Manchu. Both prose and hand were clumsy, but the construction of the steles was excellent. The labor and cost were very small; this could serve as a model. The two sides of the stele were left unpolished, and brick was laid to make flanking walls on either side, covering the top of the stele. Then, roofed over with tiles to make a little house, the stele stands inside it, guarded from wind and rain, which is better than building a pavilion to shelter a stele. On the stele’s base, the bixi, and on both sides of the inscription, the bixia carved there, one could count the very hairs. This was built by nothing more than common households of the far frontier, yet its delicacy and antique elegance are beyond compare.

paragraphs.orig: 向夕暑氣益熾, 急往所寓。 高揭北牕, 脫衣而臥。 北庭平廣, 葱畦蒜𣎒, 端方正直。 蓏棚匏架, 磊落蔭庭。 籬邊紅白蜀葵及玉簪花, 方盛開。 簷外有石榴數盆及繡毬一盆, 秋海棠二盆。 鄂之妻手提竹籃, 次第摘花, 將爲夕粧也。 昌大得酒一觶卵炒一盤而來餉曰, 「何處去耶, 幾想殺我也。」 其故作癡態, 以納忠款, 可憎可笑。 然酒我所嗜也, 况卵炒亦我所欲乎。
paragraphs.reading: 향석서기익치, 급왕소우. 고게북창, 탈의이와. 북정평광, 총휴산𣎒, 단방정직. 나붕포가, 뇌락음정. 이변홍백촉규급옥잠화, 방성개. 첨외유석류수분급수구일분, 추해당이분. 악지처수제죽람, 차제적화, 장위석장야. 창대득주일치난초일반이내향왈, 「하처거야, 기상살아야.」 기고작치태, 이납충관, 가증가소. 연주아소기야, 황난초역아소욕호.
paragraphs.en: Toward evening the heat grew fiercer, and I hurried to my lodging. I raised the north window high, took off my clothes and lay down. The northern courtyard was broad and level, with leek beds and garlic plots, square and upright. Melon trellises and gourd frames cast a profusion of shade over the court. By the hedge, red and white hollyhocks and plantain lilies were in full bloom. Beyond the eaves were several pots of pomegranates, a pot of hydrangea, and two pots of autumn begonia. E’s wife, a bamboo basket in her hand, was picking the flowers one after another, apparently to prepare for her evening toilette. Changdae obtained a goblet of wine and a plate of scrambled eggs and brought them to me, saying, “Where did you go? I’ve been thinking myself to death about you!” His affected, silly act, to present his loyal feelings, was hateful and laughable. Yet wine is what I love, and how much more are scrambled eggs what I want.

paragraphs.orig: 是日行三十里, 自鴨綠江至此, 該有一百二十里。 我人曰, 「柵門。」 本處人曰,「架子門。」 內地人曰,「邊門。」
paragraphs.reading: 시일행삼십리, 자압록강지차, 해유일백이십리. 아인왈, 「책문.」 본처인왈,「가자문.」 내지인왈,「변문.」
paragraphs.en: That day we traveled thirty li; from the Amnok River to here should be one hundred and twenty li. Our people call it the “Border Gate.” The local people call it the “Frame Gate.” The people of the inner land call it the “Frontier Gate.”

paragraphs.orig: ## 책문의 모습과 옛 영토에 대한 생각
paragraphs.en: The Border Gate and Thoughts on the Old Territory

paragraphs.orig: 二十八日乙亥 (朝霧晩晴)
paragraphs.reading: 이십팔일을해 (조무만청)
paragraphs.en: The 28th day, eulhae (fog in the morning; clear later).

paragraphs.orig: 早與卞君先爲發行。 戴宗遙指一所大庄院曰, 「此通官徐宗孟家也。 皇城亦有家, 更勝於此。 宗孟貪婪多不法, 吮朝鮮膏血。 大致富厚, 旣老爲禮部所覺, 家之在皇城者被籍, 而此猶存。」 又指一所曰, 「雙林家也。」 其對門曰, 「文通官家也。」 舌本瀏利如誦熟文, 戴宗宣川人也。 已六七入燕云。
paragraphs.reading: 조여변군선위발행. 대종요지일소대장원왈, 「차통관서종맹가야. 황성역유가, 갱승어차. 종맹탐람다불법, 연조선고혈. 대치부후, 기노위예부소각, 가지재황성자피적, 이차유존.」 우지일소왈, 「쌍림가야.」 기대문왈, 「문통관가야.」 설본유리여송숙문, 대종선천인야. 이육칠입연운.
paragraphs.en: Early, I set out ahead with Byeon. Dae-jong pointed far off to a great manor and said, “That is the house of the escort interpreter Xu Zongmeng. He has one in the imperial city too, even finer than this. Zongmeng was greedy and lawless, sucking Joseon’s marrow and blood. He grew very rich, and when he was old the Board of Rites found him out; the house in the imperial city was confiscated, but this one remains.” He pointed to another: “That is Shuanglin’s house.” Across from it: “That is Interpreter Wen’s house.” His tongue was smooth and quick, as if he were reciting a memorized text; Dae-jong was a man of Seoncheon, and had already been to Yan six or seven times.

paragraphs.orig: 比至鳳城三十里, 衣服盡濕。 行人髭鬚結露, 如秧針貫珠。 西邊天際, 重霧忽透, 片碧纔露, 嵌空玲瓏, 如牕眼小琉璃。 須臾霧氣, 盡化祥雲, 光景無限。 回看東方, 一輪紅日, 已高三竿矣。
paragraphs.reading: 비지봉성삼십리, 의복진습. 행인자수결노, 여앙침관주. 서변천제, 중무홀투, 편벽재노, 감공령롱, 여창안소류리. 수유무기, 진화상운, 광경무한. 회간동방, 일륜홍일, 이고삼간의.
paragraphs.en: When we were still thirty li from Fengcheng, our clothes were wet through. The travelers’ mustaches and beards were heavy with dew, like pearls strung on rice-seedling needles. At the western edge of the sky, thick fog suddenly parted and a bit of azure showed, hollow and lustrous, like a small pane of glass in a window. In a moment the fog turned entirely into auspicious clouds—the scene was endless. Looking back east, the red wheel of the sun had already risen three poles high.

paragraphs.orig: 中火於康永太家。 永太年二十三, 自稱民家, 漢人。 稱民家, 滿人, 稱旗下。 白晢美麗, 能鼓西洋琴。 問,「讀書否。」 對曰, 「已誦四書, 尙未講義。」 所謂誦書講義, 有兩道, 非如我東初學之兼通音義。 中原初學者, 只學四書章句, 口誦而已, 誦熟然後, 更就師受旨曰, 「講義。」 設令終身未講義, 所習章句, 爲日用官話。 所以萬國方言, 惟漢語最易, 且有理也。 永太所㞐精洒華侈, 種種位置, 莫非初見。 炕上鋪陳, 皆龍鳳氍毺椅榻所藉, 皆以錦緞爲褥。 庭中設架 以細簟遮日, 四垂緗簾, 前列石榴五六盆, 就中白色石榴盛開。 又有異樹一盆, 葉類冬栢, 果似枳實, 問其名曰, 無花果。 果皆雙雙並蔕, 不花結實, 故名。
paragraphs.reading: 중화어강영태가. 영태연이십삼, 자칭민가, 한인. 칭민가, 만인, 칭기하. 백절미려, 능고서양금. 문,「독서부.」 대왈, 「이송사서, 상미강의.」 소위송서강의, 유양도, 비여아동초학지겸통음의. 중원초학자, 지학사서장구, 구송이이, 송숙연후, 갱취사수지왈, 「강의.」 설영종신미강의, 소습장구, 위일용관화. 소이만국방언, 유한어최이, 차유리야. 영태소거정쇄화치, 종종위치, 막비초견. 항상포진, 개용봉구유의탑소자, 개이금단위욕. 정중설가 이세점차일, 사수상렴, 전열석류오륙분, 취중백색석류성개. 우유이수일분, 엽유동백, 과사지실, 문기명왈, 무화과. 과개쌍쌍병체, 불화결실, 고명.
paragraphs.en: We had the midday meal at Kang Yongtai’s house. Yongtai was twenty-three, and called himself a “civilian,” a Han Chinese. (Han are called “civilian households”; Manchus are called “bannermen.”) White-skinned and handsome, he could play the Western zither. I asked, “Do you read books?” He answered, “I have already recited the Four Books, but have not yet had the meaning lectured.” The so-called reciting and lecturing are two separate paths; it is not like our East, where beginners study sound and meaning together. In China, beginners study only the chapters and verses of the Four Books and merely recite them aloud; after they have recited them thoroughly, they go again to a teacher to receive the meaning, which is called “lecturing.” Even if one never lectures in all one’s life, what one has learned of chapters and verses becomes everyday official speech. This is why, among the languages of the ten thousand nations, Chinese is the easiest, and also has reason in it. Yongtai’s residence was refined, bright and lavish, and every arrangement was something I had never seen. On the heated floor were spread dragon-and-phoenix rugs, and the chairs and couches were all upholstered with brocade cushions. In the courtyard a frame was set up and fine bamboo mats shaded the sun, with pale-yellow curtains hanging on all four sides; in front were five or six pots of pomegranate, and among them the white ones were in full bloom. There was also a pot of a strange tree, with leaves like winter camellia and fruit like the trifoliate orange; when I asked its name, I was told it was the “no-flower fruit.” The fruits all grow in pairs on one stem; without flowering they bear fruit, hence the name.

paragraphs.orig: 書狀來見, 趙鼎鎭, 各叙年甲。 長余五歲, 副使繼又來訪。 鄭元始, 爲叙萬里同苦之誼。 金子仁, 文淳, 爲道,「兄此行, 而我境冗擾, 未及相訪。」 余曰, 「定交於他國, 可謂異域親舊。」 副使書狀, 皆大笑曰, 「未知誰爲異域也。」 副使長余二歲, 余祖父與副使祖父甞同牕治功令, 有同硏錄。 余祖父爲京兆堂上時, 副使祖父以京兆郞投刺。 各道舊日同硏事。 余時八九歲, 在傍知有舊誼。
paragraphs.reading: 서상내견, 조정진, 각서연갑. 장여오세, 부사계우내방. 정원시, 위서만리동고지의. 김자인, 문순, 위도,「형차행, 이아경용요, 미급상방.」 여왈, 「정교어타국, 가위이역친구.」 부사서상, 개대소왈, 「미지수위이역야.」 부사장여이세, 여조부여부사조부상동창치공령, 유동연록. 여조부위경조당상시, 부사조부이경조랑투자. 각도구일동연사. 여시팔구세, 재방지유구의.
paragraphs.en: The Secretary, Jo Jeong-jin, came to see me, and we each told our ages. He is five years older than I. The Deputy Envoy followed and came to visit as well. Jeong Won-si spoke of the bond of shared hardship over ten thousand li. Gim Ja-in (Mun-sun) said, “On this journey of yours, my own district was in a turmoil, and I did not manage to call on you.” I said, “To form a friendship in another country—we may be called old friends in a foreign land.” The Deputy Envoy and the Secretary both laughed loudly: “Who can say who is the foreigner?” The Deputy Envoy is two years older than I; my grandfather and the Deputy Envoy’s grandfather once studied for the examinations together at the same window, and there is a register of fellow students. When my grandfather was a senior official of the capital magistracy, the Deputy Envoy’s grandfather, as a gentleman of that magistracy, presented his visiting card. Each of us spoke of those old days of studying together. I was then eight or nine years old, standing beside them, and was aware of the old ties.

paragraphs.orig: 書狀指白石榴曰, 「曾見此否。」 余對,「不曾見。」 書狀曰, 「吾童子時家有此榴, 國中更無。 葢此榴華而不實云。」 略叙閒話, 皆起去。 渡江日雖相識面於蘆荻叢中, 未甞叙話, 又兩日柵外, 連幕露宿, 亦未甞晤, 故今以異域相戱者此也。
paragraphs.reading: 서상지백석류왈, 「증견차부.」 여대,「부증견.」 서상왈, 「오동자시가유차유, 국중갱무. 개차유화이불실운.」 약서한화, 개기거. 도강일수상식면어노적총중, 미상서화, 우양일책외, 연막노숙, 역미상오, 고금이이역상희자차야.
paragraphs.en: The Secretary pointed at the white pomegranate: “Have you seen this before?” I answered, “Never.” The Secretary said, “When I was a child we had this pomegranate at home, and there was no other in the country. They say this pomegranate flowers but does not bear fruit.” After a brief idle talk they all rose and left. On the day of crossing the river we had known each other by sight amid the reeds, but had not yet talked; and for two days outside the palisade we had camped in tents in a row, and still had not met face to face, which is why we teased each other today about being “foreign.”

paragraphs.orig: 點心尙遠云, 不敢遲待, 遂忍飢行翫, 初由右邊小門而入。 故不知其家之雄侈若此, 今由前門而出, 則外庭數十百間。 三使帶率都入此家, 而不知着在何處。 非但我行區處綽綽有餘, 來商去旅, 絡繹不絶。 又有車二十餘輛, 闐門而入, 一車所駕馬騾必五六頭, 而不聞喧聲, 深藏若虛。 葢其妥置凡百, 自有規模, 不相妨礙。 觀此外貌, 其他細節 ,不須盡說矣。
paragraphs.reading: 점심상원운, 불감지대, 수인기행완, 초유우변소문이입. 고부지기가지웅치약차, 금유전문이출, 칙외정수십백간. 삼사대솔도입차가, 이부지착재하처. 비단아행구처작작유여, 내상거려, 낙역부절. 우유거이십여량, 전문이입, 일거소가마라필오륙두, 이불문훤성, 심장약허. 개기타치범백, 자유규모, 불상방애. 관차외모, 기타세절,불수진설의.
paragraphs.en: The midday meal was said to be still far off, and not daring to wait, I put up with the hunger and went sightseeing, first entering by a small gate on the right. So I did not know how grand and lavish the house was; but now, going out by the front gate, I found outer courtyards of several dozen to a hundred rooms. The three envoys with their retinues had all entered this house, yet I could not tell where they were lodged. Not only was the arrangement for our party ample, with room to spare, but merchants came and travelers went in an unbroken stream. Moreover more than twenty carts entered through the gate, each cart drawn by five or six horses and mules, and yet no clamor was heard—they hid deep, as if empty. For they arrange everything well, with a system of their own, and do not obstruct one another. From this outward look, there is no need to speak of the other details.

paragraphs.orig: 緩步出門, 繁華富麗。 雖到皇京, 想不更加。 不意中國之若是其盛也。 左右市廛, 連互輝耀, 皆彫牕綺戶, 畵棟朱欄, 碧榜金扁。所居物皆內地奇貨。 邊門僻奧之地, 乃有精鑑雅識也。 又入一宅, 其壯麗更勝於康家, 而其制度大約皆同。 凡室屋之制, 必除地數百步, 長廣相適, 剷剗平正, 可以測土圭安針盤, 然後築臺。 臺皆石址, 或一級或二級三級, 皆甎築而磨石爲甃。 臺上建屋, 皆一字, 更無曲折附麗。 第一屋爲內室, 第二屋爲中堂, 第三屋爲前堂, 第四屋爲外室。 外室前臨大道, 爲店房, 爲市廛。 每堂前, 有左右翼室, 是爲廊廡寮廂。 大約一屋長, 必六楹八楹十楹十二楹, 兩楹之間甚廣, 幾我國平屋二間。 未甞隨材短長. 亦不任意闊狹, 必準尺度爲間架。 屋皆五梁或七梁, 從地至屋脊, 測其高下, 簷爲居中, 故瓦溝如建瓴。 屋左右及後面, 無冗簷, 以甎築墻, 直埋椽頭。 盡屋之高, 東西兩墻, 各穿圓牕面南。 皆戶正中, 一間爲出入之門, 必前後直對, 屋三重四重 則門爲六重八重, 洞開則自內室門至外室門, 一望貫通, 其直如矢。 所謂「洞開重門, 我心如此」者, 以喩其正直也。
paragraphs.reading: 완보출문, 번화부려. 수도황경, 상불갱가. 불의중국지약시기성야. 좌우시전, 연호휘요, 개조창기호, 화동주란, 벽방금편. 소거물개내지기화. 변문벽오지지, 내유정감아식야. 우입일택, 기장려갱승어강가, 이기제도대약개동. 범실옥지제, 필제지수백보, 장광상적, 산잔평정, 가이측토규안침반, 연후축대. 대개석지, 혹일급혹이급삼급, 개전축이마석위추. 대상건옥, 개일자, 갱무곡절부려. 제일옥위내실, 제이옥위중당, 제삼옥위전당, 제사옥위외실. 외실전임대도, 위점방, 위시전. 매당전, 유좌우익실, 시위낭무료상. 대약일옥장, 필육영팔영십영십이영, 양영지간심광, 기아국평옥이간. 미상수재단장. 역불임의활협, 필준척도위간가. 옥개오량혹칠량, 종지지옥척, 측기고하, 첨위거중, 고와구여건령. 옥좌우급후면, 무용첨, 이전축장, 직매연두. 진옥지고, 동서양장, 각천원창면남. 개호정중, 일간위출입지문, 필전후직대, 옥삼중사중 칙문위륙중팔중, 동개칙자내실문지외실문, 일망관통, 기직여시. 소위「동개중문, 아심여차」자, 이유기정직야.
paragraphs.en: Walking slowly out the gate, I found a flourishing richness and splendor such that even in the imperial capital I doubt it could be exceeded. I had not expected China to be so prosperous. The shops on left and right shone one after another, all with carved windows and patterned doors, painted beams and vermilion balustrades, green signboards and golden plaques. The goods they held were all rare wares of the inner land. In so remote a frontier gate, there was such fine discernment and elegant knowledge. I entered another residence, whose grandeur was even greater than the Kang house, though the layout was much the same. In general, in the way of building houses, they must clear some hundreds of paces of ground, of matching length and breadth, and level it flat and true, so that one could measure with the gnomon and set the compass; only then do they build the platform. The platforms all have stone foundations, of one, two or three steps, all built of brick with polished stone as facing. On the platform they build the houses, all in a single line, with no turnings or attachments. The first house is the inner chamber, the second the middle hall, the third the front hall, the fourth the outer room. The outer room faces the main road, and is a shop or market stall. In front of each hall are left and right wing rooms; these are the corridors, galleries and side rooms. In general, a single house is long, necessarily six, eight, ten or twelve bays, and between two pillars it is very wide, nearly two bays of our flat houses. They never follow the shortness or length of the timber, nor make them wide or narrow as they please, but always make the bays and frames by the standard measure. The houses are all of five beams or seven beams; measuring the height from the ground to the ridge, the eaves come at the halfway point, so the tile furrows are steep as water poured from a jar. On the left and right of the house and at the back there are no superfluous eaves; the walls are built of brick, directly burying the ends of the rafters. Up to the full height of the house, in the east and west walls, each is pierced with a round window facing south. The doors are all at the exact center, and the middle bay is the door of entry and exit, which must be directly opposite, front and back; if a house is three or four ranges deep, the doors are six or eight, and when all are thrown open, from the door of the inner chamber to the door of the outer room one sees through in a single glance, straight as an arrow. The line “Throw open the doors, one after another: my heart is just so” is used to illustrate their straightness.

paragraphs.orig: 路逢李同知惠迪。 譯官三堂上。 李君笑曰, 「窮邊邨野, 何足掛眼。」 吾言, 「雖至皇城, 未必勝此。」 李君曰, 「然, 雖有大小奢儉之別, 規模大率相同耳。」
paragraphs.reading: 노봉이동지혜적. 역관삼당상. 이군소왈, 「궁변촌야, 하족괘안.」 오언, 「수지황성, 미필승차.」 이군왈, 「연, 수유대소사검지별, 규모대솔상동이.」
paragraphs.en: On the road I met Yi Hye-jeok, the dongji, one of the senior-ranked interpreters, the third of them. Yi said with a laugh, “A remote border village in the wilds—what is there worth catching the eye?” I said, “Even if we reach the imperial city, it will not necessarily surpass this.” Yi said, “True; though there are differences of large and small, extravagant and frugal, the layouts are for the most part the same.”

paragraphs.orig: 爲室屋, 專靠於甓, 甓者甎也。 長一尺, 廣五寸, 比兩甎則正方, 厚二寸。 一匡搨成, 忌角缺, 忌楞刓, 忌軆翻, 一甎犯忌, 則全屋之功左矣。 是故, 旣一匡印搨, 而猶患參差 必以曲尺見矩, 斤削礪磨, 務令匀齊, 萬甎一影。 其築法, 一縱一橫, 自成坎離, 隔以石灰。 其薄如紙, 僅取膠貼, 縫痕如線。 其和灰之法, 不雜麤沙, 亦忌黏土, 沙太麤則不貼, 土過黏則易坼。 故必取黑土之細膩者, 和灰同泥, 其色黛黧, 如新燔之瓦。 葢取其性之不黏不沙, 而又取其色質純如也。 又雜以檾絲, 細剉如毛, 如我東圬土. 用馬矢同泥, 欲其靭而無龜。 又調以桐油濃滑如乳, 欲其膠而無罅。

paragraphs.en: In building houses, they depend entirely on the brick. A brick is one chi long and five cun wide; two bricks side by side make an exact square; the thickness is two cun. Each is stamped out in a single mold; they avoid broken corners, avoid blunted edges, avoid warped bodies; if even one brick commits a fault, the work of the entire house is spoiled. For this reason, though each has been stamped in one mold, they still worry about irregularities, and always check with a carpenter’s square, trim with an adze and rub with a whetstone, striving to make them even and uniform—ten thousand bricks, one shadow. Their method of laying is one lengthwise, one crosswise, naturally forming the figures of kan and li, with lime between. It is as thin as paper, barely enough to take the glue and stick, and the seam is like a thread. Their method of mixing lime does not mix in coarse sand, and also avoids sticky clay: if the sand is too coarse it will not stick, and if the earth is too sticky it will easily crack. So they always take fine, smooth black earth and mix it with lime into a mud, which is of a dark, dusky color like freshly fired tile. They take its nature, neither sticky nor sandy, and also take the pure color of its substance. They also mix in hemp fiber finely chopped like hair, as our East’s plasterers use horse dung in the mud, wanting it to be tough and without cracks. They also blend in tung oil, thick and smooth like milk, wanting it to bind and be free of gaps.

paragraphs.orig: 其葢瓦之法, 尤爲可效。 瓦之體如正圓之竹而四破之。 其一瓦之大, 恰比兩掌, 民家不用䲶鴦瓦, 椽上不構散木, 直鋪數重蘆簟。 然後覆瓦, 簟上不藉泥土。 一仰一覆, 相爲雌雄, 縫瓦亦以石灰之泥, 鱗級膠貼。 自無雀鼠之穿屋。 最忌上重下虛。 我東葢瓦之法, 與此全異。 屋上厚鋪泥土, 故上重, 墻壁不甎築, 四柱無倚, 故下虛。 瓦軆過大, 故過彎, 過彎故自多空處, 不得不補以泥土。 泥土厭重, 已有棟撓之患, 泥土一乾, 則瓦底自浮, 鱗級流退, 乃生罅隙, 已不禁風透雨漏, 雀穿鼠竄, 蛇繆貓翻之患。

paragraphs.en: Their method of covering with tiles is even more worth imitating. A tile is shaped like a perfectly round bamboo split into four. One tile is just the size of two palms. Common houses do not use paired-bird tiles; above the rafters they do not lay loose timber, but spread several layers of reed mats directly. Then the tiles are laid over, with no mud on the mats. One faces up and one faces down, each the female and male of the other, and the joints between the tiles are also glued in scales with lime mud. Naturally there is no sparrow or rat piercing the house. Above all they avoid being heavy above and hollow below. Our East’s method of covering with tiles is wholly different from this. On the roof thick mud is spread, so it is heavy above; the walls are not built of brick and the four pillars have nothing to lean on, so it is hollow below. The bodies of the tiles are too large, so they are too curved; being too curved, they naturally leave many empty spaces, which have to be filled with mud. Mud is heavy, and already brings the trouble of a bent ridgepole; and once the mud dries, the undersides of the tiles float loose by themselves, the scales drift and slide back, and cracks arise, so that already one cannot keep out the wind that blows through and the rain that leaks, the sparrows that pierce, the rats that burrow, the snakes that twine and the cats that overturn.

paragraphs.orig: 大約立屋甎功居多。 非但竟高築墻, 室內室外, 罔不鋪甎。 盡庭之廣, 麗目井井, 如畫碁道, 屋倚於壁, 上輕下完, 柱入於墻, 不經風雨, 於是不畏延燒, 不畏穿窬, 尤絶雀鼠蛇猫之患。 一閉正中一門, 則自成壁壘城堡, 室中之物, 都似櫃藏。 由是觀之, 不須許多土木, 不煩鐵冶墁工, 甓一燔而屋已成矣。
paragraphs.reading: 대약입옥전공거다. 비단경고축장, 실내실외, 망불포전. 진정지광, 여목정정, 여화기도, 옥의어벽, 상경하완, 주입어장, 불경풍우, 어시불외연소, 불외천유, 우절작서사묘지환. 일폐정중일문, 칙자성벽루성보, 실중지물, 도사궤장. 유시관지, 불수허다토목, 불번철야만공, 벽일번이옥이성의.
paragraphs.en: In general, for putting up a house, brickwork accounts for most. Not only do they build high walls, but inside the rooms and outside the rooms they pave everything with brick. The whole breadth of the courtyard is gridded delightfully to the eye like a go board; the houses lean on the walls, light above and solid below; the pillars enter the walls and do not suffer wind and rain. So they do not fear the spread of fire, do not fear burglars, and above all have cut off the troubles of sparrows, rats, snakes and cats. Once the one main door in the center is shut, it naturally becomes a rampart and a fortress, and the things in the room are as if stored in a cabinet. Seen thus, one does not need so much earth and timber, nor trouble the ironworkers and plasterers: once the bricks are fired, the house is already built.

paragraphs.orig: 方新築鳳凰城, 或曰此則安市城也。 高勾麗方言, 稱大鳥曰, 「安市」, 今鄙語往往有訓鳳凰曰,「安市」 稱蛇曰 「白巖。」 隋唐時就國語, 以鳳凰城爲安市城, 以蛇城爲白巖城, 其說頗似有理。 又世傳安市城主楊萬春, 射帝中目。 帝耀兵城下, 賜絹百匹, 以賞其爲主堅守。 三淵金公昌翕, 送其弟老稼齋昌業入燕詩曰, 「千秋大膽楊萬春, 箭射虬髯落眸子」, 牧隱李公穡貞觀吟曰, 「爲是囊中一物爾, 那知玄花落白羽。」 玄花言其目, 白羽言其箭。 二老所咏, 當出於吾東流傳之舊。 唐太宗動天下之兵, 不得志於彈丸小城, 蒼黃旋師, 其跡可疑。 金富軾只惜其史失姓名。 葢富軾爲三國史, 只就中國史, 書抄謄一番, 以作事實。 至引柳公權小說, 以證駐驆之被圍, 而唐書及司馬通鑑, 皆不見錄, 則疑其爲中國諱之。 然至若本土舊聞, 不敢略載一句, 傳信傳疑之間, 葢闕如也。

paragraphs.en: As for the Fenghuang fortress now being newly built, some say this is Ansi Fortress. In the dialect of Goguryeo, a great bird was called “ansi,” and in vulgar speech today the phoenix is sometimes glossed as “ansi,” and a snake as “baegam.” In the Sui and Tang times, following the national language, Fenghuang Fortress was made Ansi Fortress and Snake Fortress was made Baegam Fortress; the argument seems reasonable. It is also handed down that the lord of Ansi Fortress, Yang Man-chun, shot the Emperor in the eye. The Emperor paraded his troops beneath the walls and bestowed a hundred bolts of silk to reward him for firmly defending the fortress as its lord. Gim Chang-heup of Samyeon, in his poem sending his younger brother Chang-eop of Nogajae to Yan, wrote: “The bold Yang Man-chun of a thousand autumns, / shot an arrow, and the pupil of the dragon-whiskered one fell.” Yi Saek of Mogeun, in his Jeonggwan Song, wrote: “It was only a thing in a bag; / who knew the dark flower would fall on the white feathers?” “Dark flower” speaks of the eye, “white feathers” of the arrow. What these two old gentlemen sang must have come from the old tradition handed down in our East. Taizong of Tang mobilized the troops of the whole world and could not have his way with a pellet-sized small fortress, and hurriedly turned his army back; the record is suspect. Gim Bu-sik only regretted that the history had lost the name. For Bu-sik, in compiling the Samguk sagi, only took the histories of China and copied them out once to make his record of facts. He even cited Liu Gongquan’s anecdotes to prove that the imperial carriage was besieged at its halt, yet neither the Tang shu nor Sima’s Tongjian records it, so I suspect it was to avoid disgracing China. But as for old native hearsay, he did not dare to set down a single line; between transmitting what is credible and what is doubtful, it is a blank.

paragraphs.orig: 余曰 「唐太宗失目於安市, 雖不可攷, 葢以此城爲安市, 愚以爲非也。 按唐書, 安市城去平壤五百里, 鳳凰城, 亦稱王儉城, 地志又以鳳凰城稱平壤, 雖不可攷, 未知此何以名焉。 又地志古安市城在葢平縣東北七十里, 自葢平東至秀巖河三百里, 自秀巖河東至二百里, 爲鳳城, 若以此爲古平壤, 則與唐書所稱五百里相合。 然吾東之士, 只知今平壤言箕子都平壤則信, 言平壤有井田則信, 言平壤有箕子墓則信, 若復言鳳城爲平壤, 則大驚, 若曰, '遼東復有平壤, 則叱爲恠駭。' 獨不知遼東本朝鮮故地。 肅愼濊貊東彝諸國, 盡服屬衛滿朝鮮, 又不知烏剌寧古塔後春等地本高勾麗疆, 嗟乎。 後世不詳地界, 則妄把漢四郡地, 盡局之於鴨綠江內, 牽合事實, 區區分排, 乃復覔浿水於其中, 或指鴨綠江爲浿水。 或指淸川江爲浿水, 或指大同江爲浿水, 是朝鮮舊疆, 不戰自蹙矣。 此其故何也, 定平壤於一處, 而浿水前郤, 常隨事跡。 吾甞以爲漢四郡地, 非特遼東, 當入女眞。 何以知其然也, 漢書地理志, 有玄莬樂浪, 而眞番臨芚無見焉。 葢昭帝始元五年, 合四郡爲二府, 元鳳元年, 又改二府爲二郡。 玄莬三縣, 有高勾麗, 樂浪二十五縣, 有朝鮮, 遼東十八縣, 有安市, 獨眞番, 去長安七千里, 臨芚, 去長安六千一百里, 金崙所謂我國界內不可得, 當在今寧古塔等地者。」

paragraphs.en: I said, “That Taizong of Tang lost an eye at Ansi, though it cannot be verified; as for taking this fortress to be Ansi, I think it is not so. According to the Tang shu, Ansi Fortress is five hundred li from Pyeongyang. Fenghuang Fortress is also called Wanggeom Fortress, and the gazetteers also call Fenghuang Fortress Pyeongyang, though this cannot be verified; I do not know why it is so named. Again the gazetteer says the old Ansi Fortress is seventy li northeast of Gaiping county; from Gaiping east to the Xiuyan River is three hundred li; from the Xiuyan River east two hundred li is Fengcheng; if this is taken as old Pyeongyang, it agrees with the five hundred li stated in the Tang shu. But the scholars of our East know only the present Pyeongyang: say that Gija made his capital at Pyeongyang, and they believe it; say that Pyeongyang has the well-field system, and they believe it; say that Pyeongyang has Gija’s tomb, and they believe it; but if one says that Fengcheng is Pyeongyang, they are greatly alarmed, and if one says, ‘Liaodong too has a Pyeongyang,’ they scold it as monstrous. They simply do not know that Liaodong was originally the old land of Joseon. Sushen, Ye, Maek and the Eastern Yi states all submitted to Wiman’s Joseon, and they also do not know that Wula, Ninguta, Hunchun and those places were originally the territory of Goguryeo. Alas! Later generations, not knowing the borders clearly, rashly confine the lands of the four Han commanderies entirely within the Amnok River, forcing facts together and dividing them up piecemeal, and then go looking for the Pae River within it, some pointing to the Amnok as the Pae, some to the Cheongcheon, some to the Daedong; so the old territory of Joseon shrinks without a battle. Why is this so? Because Pyeongyang is fixed at one place, while the Pae River advances and retreats, ever following the facts. I have thought that the lands of the four Han commanderies were not only in Liaodong but must reach into Jurchen land. How do I know it? The geographical treatise of the Han shu has Xuantu and Lelang, but Zhenfan and Lintun do not appear in it. For in the fifth year of Shiyuan under Emperor Zhao, the four commanderies were merged into two prefectures, and in the first year of Yuanfeng the two prefectures were again changed into two commanderies. Xuantu’s three counties include Goguryeo, Lelang’s twenty-five counties include Joseon, and Liaodong’s eighteen counties include Ansi; only Zhenfan, seven thousand li from Chang’an, and Lintun, six thousand one hundred li from Chang’an—what Gim Ryun called places that cannot be found within our country’s borders and must lie in the present Ninguta and thereabouts.”

paragraphs.orig: 是也, 由是論之。 眞番臨芚, 漢末卽入於扶餘挹婁沃沮。 扶餘五而沃沮四, 或變而爲勿吉, 變而爲靺鞨, 變而爲渤海, 變而爲女眞。 按渤海武王大武藝答日本聖武王書 有曰 「復古麗之舊居, 有扶餘之遺俗」, 以此推之, 漢之四郡半在遼東, 半在女眞, 跨踞包絡, 本我幅員, 益可驗矣。 然而自漢以來, 中國所稱浿水不定厥居, 又吾東之士, 必以今平壤立準, 而紛然尋浿水之跡。 此無他, 中國人凡稱遼左之水, 率號爲浿, 所以程里不合, 事實多舛者, 爲由此也。 故欲知古朝鮮, 高勾麗之舊域, 先合女眞於境內, 次尋浿水於遼東。 浿水定然後疆域明, 疆域明然後古今事實合矣。
paragraphs.reading: 시야, 유시논지. 진번임둔, 한말즉입어부여읍루옥저. 부여오이옥저사, 혹변이위물길, 변이위말갈, 변이위발해, 변이위여진. 안발해무왕대무예답일본성무왕서 유왈 「복고려지구거, 유부여지유속」, 이차추지, 한지사군반재요동, 반재여진, 과거포락, 본아폭원, 익가험의. 연이자한이래, 중국소칭패수부정궐거, 우오동지사, 필이금평양입준, 이분연심패수지적. 차무타, 중국인범칭요좌지수, 솔호위패, 소이정리불합, 사실다천자, 위유차야. 고욕지고조선, 고구려지구역, 선합여진어경내, 차심패수어요동. 패수정연후강역명, 강역명연후고금사실합의.
paragraphs.en: That is so. Seen in this way, Zhenfan and Lintun passed at the end of the Han into Buyeo, Eumnu and Okjeo. There were five Buyeos and four Okjeos, and some changed into Mulgil, changed into Malgal, changed into Balhae, changed into Jurchen. In the letter of King Mu of Balhae, Dae Mu-ye, in reply to King Shomu of Japan, it says, “We have restored the old dwelling of Goryeo, and hold the surviving customs of Buyeo.” From this one can infer that half of the four Han commanderies was in Liaodong and half in Jurchen land, bestriding and encompassing them, originally our territory, and can verify it all the more. Yet since the Han, the Pae River as named by China has had no fixed place, and the scholars of our East always take the present Pyeongyang as the standard and busily seek the traces of the Pae. There is no other reason: the Chinese generally call any water to the left of Liao a Pae, and this is why the distances do not agree and the facts are so often mistaken. So if one wishes to know the old territory of Ancient Joseon and Goguryeo, first put Jurchen land within the border, then seek the Pae River in Liaodong. When the Pae is fixed, the territory is clear; when the territory is clear, ancient and present facts will fit together.

paragraphs.orig: 然則鳳城果爲平壤乎。 曰此亦或箕氏衛氏高氏所都, 則爲一平壤也。 唐書裴矩傳, 言高麗本孤竹國, 周以封箕子, 漢分四郡, 所謂, 「孤竹地, 在今永平府。」 又廣寧縣, 舊有箕子廟, 戴冔冠塑像, 皇明嘉靖時, 燬於兵火。 廣寧人或稱平壤。 金史及文獻通考, 俱言廣寧咸平, 皆箕子封地, 以此推之, 永平廣寧之間, 爲一平壤也。 遼史, 「渤海顯德府, 本朝鮮地。 箕子所封平壤城。 遼破渤海, 改爲東京, 卽今之遼陽縣。」是也, 以此推之, 遼陽縣, 爲一平壤也。
paragraphs.reading: 연칙봉성과위평양호. 왈차역혹기씨위씨고씨소도, 칙위일평양야. 당서배구전, 언고려본고죽국, 주이봉기자, 한분사군, 소위, 「고죽지, 재금영평부.」 우광령현, 구유기자묘, 대후관소상, 황명가정시, 훼어병화. 광령인혹칭평양. 금사급문헌통고, 구언광령함평, 개기자봉지, 이차추지, 영평광령지간, 위일평양야. 요사, 「발해현덕부, 본조선지. 기자소봉평양성. 요파발해, 개위동경, 즉금지요양현.」시야, 이차추지, 요양현, 위일평양야.
paragraphs.en: Then is Fengcheng truly Pyeongyang? I say this too may be one of the capitals of the Gi, the Wi or the Go line, and so be one Pyeongyang. The biography of Pei Ju in the Tang shu says that Goryeo was originally the state of Guzhu, which Zhou enfeoffed to Gija, and which Han divided into four commanderies; “the land of Guzhu is at present Yongping Prefecture.” Again, in Guangning county there used to be a Temple of Gija, with a statue wearing the xu cap, burned in war in the Jiajing era of the Ming. The people of Guangning sometimes called it Pyeongyang. The Jin shi and the Wenxian tongkao both say that Guangning and Xianping were the land of Gija’s enfeoffment; from this one can infer that the region between Yongping and Guangning is one Pyeongyang. The Liao shi says, “Xiande Prefecture of Balhae was originally Joseon land; the Pyeongyang fortress with which Gija was enfeoffed. After Liao broke Balhae, it was renamed the Eastern Capital, which is the present Liaoyang county.” That is so; from this one can infer that Liaoyang county is one Pyeongyang.

paragraphs.orig: 愚以爲箕氏初居永廣之間, 後爲燕將秦開所逐, 失地二千里。 漸東益徙, 如中國晉宋之南渡, 所止皆稱平壤。 今我大同江上平壤 卽其一也。 浿水亦類此, 高勾麗封域時有贏縮, 則浿水之名, 亦隨而遷徙, 如中國南北朝時, 州郡之號互相僑置。 然而以今平壤爲平壞者, 指大同江曰此浿水也, 指平壤咸鏡兩界間山曰此葢馬大山也。 以遼陽爲平壤者, 指蓒芋濼水曰此浿水也, 指葢平縣山曰此葢馬大山也。 雖未詳孰是, 然必以今大同江爲浿水者, 自小之論耳。
paragraphs.reading: 우이위기씨초거영광지간, 후위연장진개소축, 실지이천리. 점동익사, 여중국진송지남도, 소지개칭평양. 금아대동강상평양 즉기일야. 패수역유차, 고구려봉역시유영축, 칙패수지명, 역수이천사, 여중국남북조시, 주군지호호상교치. 연이이금평양위평괴자, 지대동강왈차패수야, 지평양함경양계간산왈차개마대산야. 이요양위평양자, 지한우락수왈차패수야, 지개평현산왈차개마대산야. 수미상숙시, 연필이금대동강위패수자, 자소지논이.
paragraphs.en: I think that the Gi clan at first lived between Yongping and Guangning, and was later driven out by the Yan general Qin Kai, losing two thousand li of land. Gradually they moved ever further east, like the southward crossings of Jin and Song in China, and wherever they halted they called it Pyeongyang. The Pyeongyang on the Daedong River today is one of them. The Pae River is similar: as the borders of Goguryeo at times grew and shrank, the name of the Pae moved with them, as in the Northern and Southern Dynasties of China, when prefectures and commanderies set up exile duplicates of one another’s names. However, those who take today’s Pyeongyang as Pyeongyang point to the Daedong River and say, “This is the Pae River,” and point to the mountain between the two boundaries of Pyeongyang and Hamgyeong and say, “This is Mount Gaema.” Those who take Liaoyang as Pyeongyang point to the water of 蓒芋濼 and say, “This is the Pae River,” and point to the mountain of Gaiping county and say, “This is Mount Gaema.” Though I do not know which is right, to insist that it must be the present Daedong River as the Pae is merely a view that belittles ourselves.

paragraphs.orig: 唐儀鳳二年, 以高麗王臧, 高勾麗寶藏王高臧, 爲遼東州都督, 封朝鮮王, 遣歸遼東, 仍移安東都護府於新城以統之。 由是觀之, 高氏境土之在遼東者, 唐雖得之, 不能有而復歸之高氏, 則平壤本在遼東, 或爲寄名與浿水, 時有前郤耳。 漢樂浪郡治在遼東者, 非今平壤, 乃遼陽之平壤。 及勝國時, 王氏高麗, 遼東及渤海一境, 盡入契丹, 則謹畫慈鐵兩嶺而守之。 並棄先春鴨綠而不復顧焉。 而况以外一步地乎。 雖內幷三國, 其境土武力, 遠不及高氏之强大。 後世拘泥之士, 戀慕平壤之舊號, 徒憑中國之史傳, 津津隋唐之舊蹟曰 「此浿水也, 此平壤也。」 已不勝其逕庭, 此城之爲安市爲鳳凰, 惡足辨哉。
paragraphs.reading: 당의봉이년, 이고려왕장, 고구려보장왕고장, 위요동주도독, 봉조선왕, 견귀요동, 잉이안동도호부어신성이통지. 유시관지, 고씨경토지재요동자, 당수득지, 불능유이부귀지고씨, 칙평양본재요동, 혹위기명여패수, 시유전극이. 한낙랑군치재요동자, 비금평양, 내요양지평양. 급승국시, 왕씨고려, 요동급발해일경, 진입계단, 칙근화자철양령이수지. 병기선춘압록이불부고언. 이황이외일보지호. 수내병삼국, 기경토무력, 원불급고씨지강대. 후세구니지사, 연모평양지구호, 도빙중국지사전, 진진수당지구적왈 「차패수야, 차평양야.」 이불승기경정, 차성지위안시위봉황, 오족변재.
paragraphs.en: In the second year of Yifeng of Tang, the Goryeo king Zang, that is, the Goguryeo king Bojang, Go Jang, was made Governor-General of the Liaodong region and enfeoffed as King of Joseon, and sent back to Liaodong, and the Andong Protectorate was moved to Xincheng to control it. Seen from this, the territory of the Go clan that lay in Liaodong, though Tang obtained it, it could not hold, and returned it to the Go clan; so Pyeongyang was originally in Liaodong, or else the name was lent, and the Pae at times advanced and retreated. The seat of Han’s Lelang Commandery in Liaodong was not today’s Pyeongyang, but the Pyeongyang of Liaoyang. By the time of the former dynasty, the Wang clan’s Goryeo, when Liaodong and the whole territory of Balhae had entered Khitan, drew careful lines at the two ridges of Jabi and Cheol and defended them, and abandoned Seonchun and the Amnok without looking back—to say nothing of a single step beyond. Though it annexed the Three Kingdoms within, its territory and military power were far short of the strength of the Go clan. The pedantic scholars of later times, yearning for the old name Pyeongyang, merely rely on the histories of China and earnestly cite the old traces of the Sui and Tang, saying, “This is the Pae River, this is Pyeongyang.” They are already hopelessly wide of the mark; and as for whether this fortress is Ansi or Fenghuang, how could they ever settle it?

paragraphs.orig: 城周不過三里, 而甎築數十重, 制度雄侈, 四隅正方若置斗。 然今裁半築, 則其高低雖未可測。 門上建樓處, 設雲梯浮空駕起工役。 雖似浩大, 器械便利, 運甓輸土。 皆機動輪轉, 或自上汲引, 或自推自行, 不一其法。 皆事半功倍之術 莫非足法。 而非但行忙, 難以遍觀, 雖終日熟視 非造次可學 良可歎也。
paragraphs.reading: 성주불과삼리, 이전축수십중, 제도웅치, 사우정방약치두. 연금재반축, 칙기고저수미가측. 문상건누처, 설운제부공가기공역. 수사호대, 기계편리, 운벽수토. 개기동윤전, 혹자상급인, 혹자추자행, 불일기법. 개사반공배지술 막비족법. 이비단행망, 난이편관, 수종일숙시 비조차가학 양가탄야.
paragraphs.en: The circuit of the fortress is no more than three li, but the brickwork is piled in dozens of layers; its construction is grand and lavish, the four corners square as if a measure had been set down. Since it is now only half built, its height cannot yet be gauged. Over the gate, where a tower is to be built, a cloud ladder is set up, a scaffold raised in the air for the work. It seems vast and huge, but the tools are handy, and the carrying of brick and earth is all done by machines turned on wheels; some draw up from above, some are pushed and go by themselves, not one method only. All are techniques of half the effort for double the result, and none is not worth imitating. But not only was I busy traveling and unable to see it all, but even had I looked closely all day, it is not something that can be learned in haste—truly a pity.

paragraphs.orig: 食後, 與卞季涵鄭進士先行。 康永泰出門揖送, 頗有惜別之意。 且囑歸時當値冬節, 願賷賜一件時憲。 余解給一丸淸心。
paragraphs.reading: 식후, 여변계함정진사선행. 강영태출문읍송, 파유석별지의. 차촉귀시당치동절, 원재사일건시헌. 여해급일환청심.
paragraphs.en: After the meal, I went on ahead with Byeon Gye-ham and the jinsa Jeong. Kang Yongtai came out of the gate and bowed us off, showing quite a feeling of regret at parting. He also asked that on our return, which would coincide with the winter solstice, I would bring him as a gift one copy of the Shixian calendar. I took off and gave him a pill of Clear-Heart medicine.

paragraphs.orig: 過一鋪, 掛一面金書當字牌, 旁書, 「惟軍器不當」 五字。 此典當舖也。 有數三美少年, 走出舖中, 遮馬請少刻納凉, 遂相與下馬隨入。 其凡百位置, 更勝康家, 庭中有二大盆, 種三五柄蓮子, 養得五色鮒魚。 年少手持掌大紗罾, 向小瓮邊, 臽了幾顆紅蟲, 浮沉盆中。 蟲細如蟹卵, 皆蠕蠕。 少年更以扇敲響那盆郭, 念念招魚, 魚皆出水呷沫。
paragraphs.reading: 과일포, 괘일면금서당자패, 방서, 「유군기부당」 오자. 차전당포야. 유수삼미소년, 주출포중, 차마청소각납량, 수상여하마수입. 기범백위치, 갱승강가, 정중유이대분, 종삼오병연자, 양득오색부어. 연소수지장대사증, 향소옹변, 함료기과홍충, 부침분중. 충세여해란, 개연연. 소년갱이선고향나분곽, 염념초어, 어개출수합말.
paragraphs.en: Passing a shop, I saw hung there a signboard with the gold character “pawn,” and beside it written, “Only weapons of war not pawned”—five characters. It was a pawnshop. Two or three handsome youths ran out of the shop, stopped my horse and invited me to cool off for a moment, so we dismounted together and followed them in. All its arrangements surpassed the Kang house. In the courtyard were two large basins, in which three or five stalks of lotus were planted and five-colored carp raised. A young man holding a palm-sized gauze net scooped several red worms out of a small jar and dropped them floating and sinking in the basin. The worms were as fine as crab eggs, all wriggling. The young man tapped the rim of the basin with his fan, calling softly to beckon the fish; the fish all rose out of the water and gulped at the foam.

paragraphs.orig: 日方午天, 火傘下曝, 悶塞不可久居。 遂行, 與鄭進士或先或後, 余謂鄭曰, 「城制何如」, 鄭曰 「甓不如石也。」
paragraphs.reading: 일방오천, 화산하폭, 민색불가구거. 수행, 여정진사혹선혹후, 여위정왈, 「성제하여」, 정왈 「벽불여석야.」
paragraphs.en: The sun stood at noon, a parasol of fire baking us from above; it was stifling and one could not stay long. So we went on, Jeong and I sometimes ahead, sometimes behind. I said to Jeong, “What do you think of the construction of the fortress?” Jeong said, “Brick is not as good as stone.”

paragraphs.orig: 余曰, 「君不知也。 我國城制不甎而石, 非計也。 夫甎一凾出矩則萬甎同樣. 更無費力. 磨琢之功, 一窰燒成, 萬甎坐得。 更無募人運致之勞, 齊匀方正, 力省功倍, 運之輕而築之易, 莫甎若也。 今夫石劚之於山, 當用匠幾人, 輦運之時, 當用夫幾人, 旣運之後, 當用匠幾人, 以琢治之, 其琢治之功, 又當再費幾日。 築之之時, 安排一石之功, 又當再用夫幾人, 於是削崖而被之, 是土肉而石衣也。 外似峻整, 內實臲卼。 石旣參差不齊, 則恒以小石撑其尻跗, 崖與城之間, 實以碎礫, 雜以泥土, 一經潦雨, 膓虛腹漲, 一石踈脫, 萬石爭潰, 此易見之勢也。 且石灰之性, 能黏於甎, 而不能貼石, 余嘗與次修論城制。 或曰 '甓之堅剛安能當石', 次修大聲曰, '甓之勝於石, 豈較一甓一石之謂哉'。 此可爲鐵論。 大約石灰不能貼石, 則用灰彌多, 而彌自皸坼, 背石卷起, 故石常各自一石, 而附土爲固而已, 甎得灰縫如魚膘之合木, 鵬砂之續金, 萬甓凝合, 膠成一城, 故一甎之堅, 誠不如石, 而一石之堅, 又不及萬甎之膠。 此其甓與石之利害便否。 所以易辨也。」
paragraphs.reading: 여왈, 「군부지야. 아국성제부전이석, 비계야. 부전일함출구칙만전동양. 갱무비력. 마탁지공, 일요소성, 만전좌득. 갱무모인운치지로, 제균방정, 역생공배, 운지경이축지이, 막전약야. 금부석촉지어산, 당용장기인, 연운지시, 당용부기인, 기운지후, 당용장기인, 이탁치지, 기탁치지공, 우당재비기일. 축지지시, 안배일석지공, 우당재용부기인, 어시삭애이피지, 시토육이석의야. 외사준정, 내실얼올. 석기참치부제, 칙항이소석탱기고부, 애여성지간, 실이쇄력, 잡이이토, 일경요우, 장허복창, 일석소탈, 만석쟁궤, 차이견지세야. 차석회지성, 능점어전, 이불능첩석, 여상여차수논성제. 혹왈 '벽지견강안능당석', 차수대성왈, '벽지승어석, 기교일벽일석지위재'. 차가위철론. 대약석회불능첩석, 칙용회미다, 이미자군탁, 배석권기, 고석상각자일석, 이부토위고이이, 전득회봉여어표지합목, 붕사지속금, 만벽응합, 교성일성, 고일전지견, 성불여석, 이일석지견, 우불급만전지교. 차기벽여석지이해편부. 소이이변야.」
paragraphs.en: I said, “You do not know. That our country’s fortresses are made not of brick but of stone is not a good plan. Once the brick mold has been made to the pattern, ten thousand bricks are of the same shape, and there is no further labor; the work of polishing and carving is done—one firing of the kiln, and ten thousand bricks are got at a stroke. There is no toil of recruiting men to haul them; being even and square, the strength is saved and the work doubled; they are light to carry and easy to lay; nothing equals brick. Now stone is quarried from a mountain, requiring so many craftsmen; at the time of carting it, so many laborers; after it has been brought, so many craftsmen to carve and finish it, and the labor of carving and finishing takes again so many days. At the time of laying, the work of setting one stone requires again so many laborers; then the cliff is cut away and covered over—this is earth for flesh and stone for clothing. Outside it looks stern and neat, but inside it is really shaky. Since the stones are uneven, they always prop up the rump with small stones, and between the cliff and the wall they fill in with crushed gravel mixed with clay; once a heavy rain passes, the bowels are empty and the belly swells; if one stone comes loose, ten thousand fight to collapse—this is an easy thing to see. Moreover, the nature of lime is that it can stick to brick but cannot adhere to stone. I once discussed the construction of walls with Chasu. Someone said, ‘How can the hardness of brick match stone?’ Chasu said loudly, ‘That brick beats stone—how could it be a matter of comparing one brick with one stone?’ This could be an iron-clad argument. In general, since lime cannot adhere to stone, the more lime is used, the more it cracks, curling away from the stone; so the stones always remain each one a stone by itself, firm only by attaching to earth, whereas brick with its lime joints is like fish glue joining wood, or borax welding metal; ten thousand bricks congeal together and are glued into a single fortress. Therefore one brick is truly not as hard as stone, but the hardness of one stone is again inferior to ten thousand bricks glued together. This is the advantage and disadvantage, the convenience and inconvenience, of brick and stone, which are easily distinguished.”

paragraphs.orig: 鄭於馬上傴僂欲墮, 葢睡已久矣。 余以扇搠其脅大罵曰, 「長者爲語, 何睡不聽也。」 鄭笑曰, 「吾已盡聽之 甓不如石 石不如睡也。」 余忿欲敺之, 相與大笑。
paragraphs.reading: 정어마상구루욕타, 개수이구의. 여이선삭기협대매왈, 「장자위어, 하수불청야.」 정소왈, 「오이진청지 벽불여석 석불여수야.」 여분욕구지, 상여대소.
paragraphs.en: Jeong, on horseback, was bent over and about to fall; he had been asleep for some time. I jabbed his ribs with my fan and cursed loudly: “When an elder is speaking, how can you sleep and not listen?” Jeong laughed: “I have heard it all. Brick is not as good as stone, and stone is not as good as sleep.” I was so angry I wanted to beat him, and then we both laughed.

paragraphs.orig: 至河邊, 得柳陰納凉。 五渡河, 五里之間, 一臺子, 所謂頭臺子, 二臺子, 三臺子, 皆烽堡也。 甎築如城, 高五六丈, 正圓如筆筒。 上施垜堞, 多毁壞而不修葺何也。 道傍或有柩, 累石壓之。 年久露置, 木頭朽敗, 葢待其骨枯, 擧而焚之云。 沿道多有墳塋, 其封高銳, 亦不被莎。 多樹白楊, 排行正直, 行旅步走者絶少。 步走者, 必肩擔鋪盖。 寢具謂鋪盖。 無鋪盖者, 店房不許留接, 疑其姦宄也。 掛鏡而行者, 養目者也。 乘馬者, 皆着黑緞靴子, 步行者, 皆着靑布靴子, 其底皆衲布數十重。 絶不見麻鞋藁屨。 宿松店, 一名雪裡店, 又號薛劉店。 是日行七十里, 或曰, 此舊鎭東堡也。
paragraphs.reading: 지하변, 득유음납량. 오도하, 오리지간, 일대자, 소위두대자, 이대자, 삼대자, 개봉보야. 전축여성, 고오륙장, 정원여필통. 상시타첩, 다훼괴이불수즙하야. 도방혹유구, 누석압지. 연구노치, 목두후패, 개대기골고, 거이분지운. 연도다유분영, 기봉고예, 역불피사. 다수백양, 배행정직, 행려보주자절소. 보주자, 필견담포개. 침구위포개. 무포개자, 점방불허유접, 의기간귀야. 괘경이행자, 양목자야. 승마자, 개착흑단화자, 보행자, 개착청포화자, 기저개납포수십중. 절불견마혜고구. 숙송점, 일명설리점, 우호설유점. 시일행칠십리, 혹왈, 차구진동보야.
paragraphs.en: At the riverside we found willow shade and cooled ourselves. At the Wudu River, at every five li there is a taizi—the so-called first taizi, second taizi and third taizi—all of them beacon forts. They are built of brick like fortresses, five or six zhang high, perfectly round like a brush holder. On top are set battlements, many ruined and not repaired—why? By the roadside there were sometimes coffins, weighted with piled stones. Left exposed for years, the wood ends were rotten and broken; apparently they wait for the bones to dry, then lift them and burn them. Along the road were many graves, their mounds high and pointed, and not covered with grass. Many white poplars were planted, in straight rows, and travelers on foot were extremely few. Those who go on foot must carry their bedding on their shoulders. Bedding is called pugai. Those without pugai are not allowed to lodge at the inns, as they are suspected of being villains. Those who travel with spectacles hung on are those who look after their eyes. Those who ride horses all wear black satin boots; those on foot all wear blue cloth boots, and the soles are all quilted with dozens of layers of cloth. Not a single hemp sandal or straw shoe was to be seen. We lodged at Songdian (the Pine Inn), which is also called Xueli Inn and also named Xueliu Inn. That day we traveled seventy li; some say this is the old Zhendongbao.

paragraphs.orig: ## 삼가하에서 통원보까지
paragraphs.en: From the Sanjia River to Tongyuanbu

paragraphs.orig: 二十九日丙子 (晴)
paragraphs.reading: 이십구일병자 (청)
paragraphs.en: The twenty-ninth day, byeongja (clear).

paragraphs.orig: 舟渡三家河。 舟如馬槽, 全木刳成, 無櫓槳。 兩岸立丫木, 橫截大繩, 緣繩而行, 則舟自來往。 馬皆浮渡。 又舟渡劉家河, 中火黃河庄。 午極熱。 馬渡金家河, 所謂八渡河也。 林家臺, 范家臺, 大小方身五里十里之間。 村閭相望, 桑麻菀然。 時方早黍黃熟, 薥黍發穗, 而皆刈去其葉以飼馬騾, 亦所以爲黍柄, 養其全氣也。 到處有關廟。 數家相聚, 必有一座大窰以燒甎。 范印晒曝, 新舊燔燒, 處處山積。 葢甓爲日用先務也。
paragraphs.reading: 주도삼가하. 주여마조, 전목고성, 무노장. 양안립아목, 횡절대승, 연승이행, 칙주자래왕. 마개부도. 우주도유가하, 중화황하장. 오극열. 마도김가하, 소위팔도하야. 임가대, 범가대, 대소방신오리십리지간. 촌려상망, 상마울연. 시방조서황숙, 촉서발수, 이개예거기엽이사마라, 역소이위서병, 양기전기야. 도처유관묘. 수가상취, 필유일좌대요이소전. 범인쇄폭, 신구번소, 처처산적. 개벽위일용선무야.
paragraphs.en: We crossed the Sanjia River by boat. The boat was like a horse trough, hollowed out of a single log, with neither scull nor oar. On each bank a forked post was set up, and a great rope was stretched across between them; by pulling along the rope the boat goes back and forth of itself. The horses all crossed by swimming. We crossed the Liujia River by boat again, and took our midday meal at Huanghezhuang. At noon it was fiercely hot. The horses forded the Jinjia River, which is what is called the Eight Fords River. Linjiatai, Fanjiatai, and Dafangshen and Xiaofangshen lie five or ten li apart, with villages in sight of one another and mulberry and hemp growing lush. It was just the time when the early millet was ripening yellow and the sorghum was heading out, yet everywhere they had stripped the leaves from it to feed the horses and mules, which is also done for the sake of the millet stalks, so that they nourish the plant's whole vigour. Everywhere there are temples to Guan Yu. Wherever a few households cluster together there is sure to be one great kiln for firing bricks. The bricks are moulded and sun-dried, new ones and old being fired together, and they are piled up like hills in every place. For bricks are the first business of daily use.

paragraphs.orig: 少憩典當舖。 主人引至中堂, 勸一椀熱茶。 位置多異玩, 設架齊梁, 整置所典之物, 皆衣服也。 褓裹付紙籤, 書物主姓名別號, 相標, 居住, 再書某年月日典當某件子, 某字號舖親手交付云云。 其利殖之法, 無過什二, 過期一朔, 許賣。 典當題著金字柱聯曰, 「洪範九疇先言富, 大學十章半論財。」 以薥黍柄, 巧搆樓閣, 置艸蟲一枚, 以聽鳴聲。 簷端懸彫籠, 養一異鳥。
paragraphs.reading: 소게전당포. 주인인지중당, 권일완열다. 위치다이완, 설가제량, 정치소전지물, 개의복야. 보과부지첨, 서물주성명별호, 상표, 거주, 재서모년월일전당모건자, 모자호포친수교부운운. 기이식지법, 무과십이, 과기일삭, 허매. 전당제착금자주련왈, 「홍범구주선언부, 대학십장반논재.」 이촉서병, 교구루각, 치초충일매, 이청명성. 첨단현조롱, 양일이조.
paragraphs.en: We rested a little at a pawnshop. The master led us into the central hall and pressed on us a bowl of hot tea. The room was furnished with many curious antiques. Racks were set up level with the beams, and on them the pledged goods were neatly arranged, all of them clothing. Each was wrapped in a cloth bundle with a paper slip attached, on which were written the owner's name and sobriquet, marks for identifying him, and his address; and it was written again that on such a year, month and day such an article was pawned, and handed over in person at such-and-such a shop, and so on. As for the way they make their profit, it does not exceed two in ten; if the term is a month overdue, the pledge may be sold. On the pawnshop's pillar was inscribed, in gilt characters, a couplet: "The Great Plan's nine divisions put wealth first; of the Great Learning's ten chapters, half discourse on finance." With sorghum stalks they had cleverly built a little pavilion, and in it kept a single grass insect so as to listen to its chirping. From the eaves hung a carved cage, in which they kept a rare bird.

paragraphs.orig: 是日行五十里, 宿通遠堡, 卽鎭夷堡也。
paragraphs.reading: 시일행오십리, 숙통원보, 즉진이보야.
paragraphs.en: That day we travelled fifty li and lodged at Tongyuanbu, which is the same as Zhenyibu.

paragraphs.orig: ## 만주족 민가의 모습
paragraphs.en: A Manchu Household

paragraphs.orig: 七月初一日丁丑 (曉大雨)
paragraphs.reading: 칠월초일일정축 (효대우)
paragraphs.en: The first day of the seventh month, jeongchuk (heavy rain at dawn).

paragraphs.orig: 留行。
paragraphs.reading: 유행.
paragraphs.en: We stayed where we were.

paragraphs.orig: 與鄭進士, 周主簿, 卞君, 來源, 趙主簿, 學東, 上房乾粮判事, 賭紙牌以遣閒, 且博飮資也。 諸君以余手劣, 黜之座, 但囑安坐飮酒, 諺所謂, 光但喫餠也。 尤爲忿恨, 亦復柰何。 坐觀成敗, 酒則先酌也, 非惡事。
paragraphs.reading: 여정진사, 주주부, 변군, 내원, 조주부, 학동, 상방건량판사, 도지패이견한, 차박음자야. 제군이여수렬, 출지좌, 단촉안좌음주, 언소위, 광단끽병야. 우위분한, 역부내하. 좌관성패, 주칙선작야, 비악사.
paragraphs.en: With the jinsa Jeong, Registrar Ju, Mr. Byeon, Rae-won, Registrar Jo, Hak-dong, and the provisions-officer interpreter of the chief envoy's quarters, I gambled at paper cards to while away the idle time, and also to win money for drink. My companions, finding my hand clumsy, expelled me from the table, and bade me only sit quietly and drink, as in the proverb, "Just eat the rice cakes." I was all the more indignant, but what could I do? Sitting and watching their wins and losses, with the wine poured first for me, was not a bad business at all.

paragraphs.orig: 時聞間壁婦人語, 聲嫩囀嬌愬, 燕燕鶯鶯, 意謂主家婆娘, 必是絶代佳人。 及爲歷翫堂室, 一婦人五旬以上年紀, 當戶據牀而坐, 貌極悍醜。 道了「叔叔千福。」 余答道 「托主人洪福。」 余故遲爲, 玩其服飾制度。 滿髻揷花, 金釧寶璫, 略施朱粉, 身着一領黑色長衣, 遍鎖銀紐, 足下穿一對靴子, 繡得草花蜂蝶。 葢滿女不纏脚, 不着弓鞋。
paragraphs.reading: 시문간벽부인어, 성눈전교소, 연연앵앵, 의위주가파낭, 필시절대가인. 급위역완당실, 일부인오순이상연기, 당호거상이좌, 모극한추. 도료「숙숙천복.」 여답도 「탁주인홍복.」 여고지위, 완기복식제도. 만계삽화, 금천보당, 약시주분, 신착일령흑색장의, 편쇄은뉴, 족하천일대화자, 수득초화봉접. 개만녀부전각, 불착궁혜.
paragraphs.en: At that time I heard a woman's voice from the room next door, soft and warbling, tender and coaxing, all swallows and orioles, and I thought that the mistress of the house must surely be a peerless beauty. But when I went on to look about the rooms, I found a woman of fifty or more years sitting on a couch squarely in the doorway, her looks fierce and hideous in the extreme. She said, "A thousand blessings upon you, uncle." I answered, "By the great fortune of the master of the house." I purposely dawdled so as to examine the fashion of her dress. Her chignon was full of stuck-in flowers; she wore gold bracelets and precious earrings, and had put on a little rouge and powder. On her body was a long black robe with silver buttons fastened all down it; on her feet a pair of boots embroidered with grass flowers, bees and butterflies. For Manchu women do not bind their feet, nor wear bow-shaped shoes.

paragraphs.orig: 簾中轉出一個處女。 年貌似是廿歲以上。 處女髻髮中分綰上, 以此爲辨, 貌亦傑悍, 而肌肉白淨。 把鐵鏇子, 傾綠色瓦盆。 滿勺了薥黍飯, 盛得一椀, 和鏇瀝水。 坐西壁下交椅, 以箸吸飯, 更拿數尺葱根, 連葉蘸醬, 一飯一佐。 項附鷄子大癭瘤, 噉飯喫茶, 略無羞容。 葢歲閱東人, 尋常親熟故也。
paragraphs.reading: 염중전출일개처녀. 연모사시입세이상. 처녀계발중분관상, 이차위변, 모역걸한, 이기육백정. 파철선자, 경녹색와분. 만작료촉서반, 성득일완, 화선역수. 좌서벽하교의, 이저흡반, 갱나수척총근, 연엽잠장, 일반일좌. 항부계자대영류, 담반끽다, 약무수용. 개세열동인, 심상친숙고야.
paragraphs.en: From behind the curtain there came out a maiden. By her looks and years she seemed to be past twenty. A maiden's hair is parted in the middle and coiled upward, and by this one tells them; her looks too were fierce and sturdy, yet her flesh was white and clean. Taking an iron ladle, she tipped it into a green earthenware basin; she scooped up a ladleful of sorghum rice, filled a bowl, and strained off the water, ladle and all. Sitting on a folding chair under the west wall, she sucked in the rice with chopsticks; then she took several feet of scallion root, leaves and all, dipped it in sauce, and ate one mouthful of rice with one bite of relish. On her neck was a goitre the size of a hen's egg, yet she ate her rice and drank her tea without the slightest look of shame. For year after year she has seen men of the Eastern Country, so to her we are quite ordinary and familiar.

paragraphs.orig: 庭廣數百間。 久雨泥淖, 河邊水磨小石如碁子大黃雀卵者, 本無用之物, 而揀其形色相類者, 當門處錯成九苞飛鳳, 以禦泥淖。 其無棄物, 推此可知。 鷄皆毛羽脫落. 一如抽鑷, 往往肉鷄蹁跚, 醜惡不忍見。
paragraphs.reading: 정광수백간. 구우이뇨, 하변수마소석여기자대황작란자, 본무용지물, 이간기형색상류자, 당문처착성구포비봉, 이어이뇨. 기무기물, 추차가지. 계개모우탈락. 일여추섭, 왕왕육계편산, 추악불인견.
paragraphs.en: The courtyard was several hundred kan (bays) wide. After the long rain it was a quagmire of mud. On the riverbank there were small water-polished stones the size of go pieces or of yellow sparrows' eggs, things that were of no use at all; but they had sorted out those alike in shape and colour and laid them in a mosaic at the gate as a nine-crested phoenix in flight, to keep out the mud. That nothing is thrown away can be inferred from this. The chickens had all lost their feathers, quite as though they had been plucked with tweezers, and here and there fat hens staggered about, so ugly I could not bear to look.

paragraphs.orig: ## 만주 민가의 생활 모습
paragraphs.en: Daily Life in a Manchu Household

paragraphs.orig: 初二日戊寅 (曉大雨 晩晴)
paragraphs.reading: 초이일무인 (효대우 만청)
paragraphs.en: The second day, muin (heavy rain at dawn, fair in the evening).

paragraphs.orig: 前溪大漲, 不可渡, 遂留行。 正使命來源及周主簿, 前往視水, 余亦隨行。 不數里, 巨浸當前, 不見涯涘。 使善泅者, 入水測其淺深, 不十步而肩已沒矣。 還報水勢, 正使愁悶, 盡招譯官及各房裨將, 使各陳渡水之策。 副使書狀, 亦來會, 副使曰 「多貰門扇及車輿, 作筏以渡何如。」 周主簿曰 「此計大妙。」 首譯曰 「門扇車輿, 難可多得。 此間造屋, 現有十餘間材木, 可以貰用, 但患葛絞難得。」 諸議紛然. 余曰, 「安用縛筏。 我有一兩隻舴艋櫓槳都具, 但欠一事。」 周問,「所欠甚事。」 余曰, 「只乏個副手梢公。」 一座哄笑。
paragraphs.reading: 전계대창, 불가도, 수유행. 정사명내원급주주부, 전왕시수, 여역수행. 불수리, 거침당전, 불견애사. 사선수자, 입수측기천심, 불십보이견이몰의. 환보수세, 정사수민, 진초역관급각방비장, 사각진도수지책. 부사서상, 역래회, 부사왈 「다세문선급거여, 작벌이도하여.」 주주부왈 「차계대묘.」 수역왈 「문선거여, 난가다득. 차간조옥, 현유십여간재목, 가이세용, 단환갈교난득.」 제의분연. 여왈, 「안용박벌. 아유일량척책맹노장도구, 단흠일사.」 주문,「소흠심사.」 여왈, 「지핍개부수초공.」 일좌홍소.
paragraphs.en: The stream in front had swollen greatly and could not be crossed, so we stayed. The chief envoy ordered Rae-won and Registrar Ju to go ahead and look at the water, and I went along too. Before we had gone a few li a vast flood lay in front of us, its shores nowhere to be seen. They sent a good swimmer into the water to sound its depth; before he had gone ten paces it was already over his shoulders. He came back and reported the state of the water. The chief envoy was grieved and perplexed, and summoned all the interpreters and the aides of each quarters, to have each propose a plan for crossing the water. The deputy envoy and the secretary also came to the meeting. The deputy envoy said, "What about hiring a good many door-leaves and carriages and making rafts to cross?" Registrar Ju said, "A marvellous plan." The chief interpreter said, "Door-leaves and carriages are hard to get in numbers. There is timber here at the moment for a dozen-odd rooms of a house under construction, which we could hire and use; the only worry is that kudzu rope is hard to get." Opinions were various and confused. I said, "Why bother lashing a raft? I have a boat or two, with sculls and oars all complete; only one thing is lacking." Ju asked, "What is lacking?" I said, "Only a deputy boatman." The whole room burst out laughing.

paragraphs.orig: 主人麁鹵, 目不識丁, 而丌上猶有楊升菴集, 四聲猿。 有尺餘正藍瓷甁, 斜揷趙南星鐵如意, 臘茶色小香爐, 雲間胡文明製椅卓屛鄣, 俱有雅致, 不似窮邊村野氣。 余問, 「爾家計粗足否。」對曰, 「終歲勤苦, 未免飢寒。 若非貴國使行時, 都沒了生涯。」 「有男女幾個。」 曰, 「只有一盜, 尙未招婿。」 余問, 「何謂一盜。」 曰, 「盜不過五女之門, 豈不是家之蟊賊。」
paragraphs.reading: 주인추로, 목불식정, 이기상유유양승암집, 사성원. 유척여정람자병, 사삽조남성철여의, 납다색소향로, 운간호문명제의탁병장, 구유아치, 불사궁변촌야기. 여문, 「이가계조족부.」대왈, 「종세근고, 미면기한. 약비귀국사행시, 도몰료생애.」 「유남녀기개.」 왈, 「지유일도, 상미초서.」 여문, 「하위일도.」 왈, 「도불과오녀지문, 기불시가지모적.」
paragraphs.en: The master was coarse and rough, and could not read a single character, yet on his table there still lay the Collected Works of Yang Shen and the Four Cries of the Gibbon. There was a deep-blue porcelain vase more than a foot tall, with Zhao Nanxing's iron ruyi slanting from it, a small incense burner the colour of wax tea, and chairs, tables and screens made by Hu Wenming of Yunjian; all had a refined taste, nothing like the rustic air of a poor frontier village. I asked, "Is your household fairly well off?" He answered, "All year we toil, and cannot escape hunger and cold. If it were not for your honourable country's envoys passing by, we would have no livelihood at all." "How many sons and daughters have you?" He said, "Only one thief; she has yet to take a husband." I asked, "What do you mean, one thief?" He said, "A thief does not pass by the gate of five daughters, so is she not the weevil of the household?"

paragraphs.orig: 午後出門, 閒行散悶。 薥黍田中, 急響了一聲鳥銃。 主人忙出門看, 那田中跳出一個漢子, 一手把銃 一手曳猪後脚。 猛視店主, 怒道, 「何故放這牲口入田中。」 店主面帶惶愧, 遜謝不已, 其人血淋淋拖猪而去。 店主佇立悵然, 再三惋歎。 余問, 「那漢所獲誰家牧的。」 店主曰, 「俺家牧的。」 余問, 「雖然, 這畜逸入他人田中。 不曾傷害了一柄薥黍, 柰何枉殺了這個牲口。 爾們應須追徵猪價麽。」 店主曰, 「那敢追徵。 不謹護牢, 是我之不是處。」
paragraphs.reading: 오후출문, 한행산민. 촉서전중, 급향료일성조총. 주인망출문간, 나전중도출일개한자, 일수파총 일수예저후각. 맹시점주, 노도, 「하고방저생구입전중.」 점주면대황괴, 손사불이, 기인혈임림타저이거. 점주저립창연, 재삼완탄. 여문, 「나한소획수가목적.」 점주왈, 「엄가목적.」 여문, 「수연, 저축일입타인전중. 부증상해료일병촉서, 내하왕살료저개생구. 이문응수추징저가마.」 점주왈, 「나감추징. 불근호뢰, 시아지불시처.」
paragraphs.en: In the afternoon I went out the gate and strolled idly to relieve my gloom. In a sorghum field a musket cracked sharply. The master hurried out to look; from the field there leaped a fellow, one hand holding a gun, the other dragging a pig by its hind leg. Glaring at the innkeeper he said angrily, "Why did you let this beast loose into the field?" The innkeeper looked ashamed and alarmed, and apologized over and over; the man dragged the dripping-bloody pig away. The innkeeper stood sorrowfully for a while and sighed again and again. I asked, "Whose pig was it, the one that fellow bagged?" The innkeeper said, "It was mine." I said, "Even so, this creature had strayed into another man's field. It had not damaged a single sorghum stalk; why was it wrongfully killed? Shouldn't you demand the price of the pig?" The innkeeper said, "How would I dare demand it? Not keeping it penned securely was my fault."

paragraphs.orig: 盖康煕甚重稼穡制, 牛馬踐穀者倍徵, 故放者杖六十, 羊豕入田中, 田主登時捕獲, 放牧者, 不敢認主。 但不得遮車道, 阻泥則引出田間, 故田主常常治道以護田云。
paragraphs.reading: 개강희심중가색제, 우마천곡자배징, 고방자장육십, 양시입전중, 전주등시포획, 방목자, 불감인주. 단부득차거도, 조니칙인출전간, 고전주상상치도이호전운.
paragraphs.en: For Kangxi set great weight on agriculture; by his regulation, oxen and horses that trample the grain are fined double, and the one who lets them loose is beaten sixty strokes with the staff; sheep and pigs that enter a field are caught on the spot by the owner of the field, and the herders dare not claim their master. Only, they may not block the carriage road; if mud obstructs it, carriages are led out through the fields, and so the owners of the fields are constantly mending the road to protect their fields, I was told.

paragraphs.orig: 村邊有二窰。 一恰裁燒畢, 塗泥竈門, 擔水數十桶。 連灌窰頂, 窰頂略坎, 受水不溢。 窰身方爛, 得水卽乾, 似當注水, 不焦爲候耳。 一窰先已燒冷, 方取甓出窰。 大約窰制, 與我東之窰判異, 先言我窰之誤, 然後窰制可得。
paragraphs.reading: 촌변유이요. 일흡재소필, 도니조문, 담수수십통. 연관요정, 요정약감, 수수불일. 요신방란, 득수즉건, 사당주수, 불초위후이. 일요선이소랭, 방취벽출요. 대약요제, 여아동지요판이, 선언아요지오, 연후요제가득.
paragraphs.en: At the edge of the village were two kilns. One had just finished firing; the oven door was being sealed with mud, and dozens of buckets of water were carried and poured over the kiln top continuously. The kiln top was slightly hollowed, so as to hold the water without overflowing. The body of the kiln was still scorching; the water dried at once, and it seems the water is to be poured on until it no longer scorches, which is the sign. The other kiln had already cooled after firing, and the bricks were being taken out. On the whole, the make of the kilns here is utterly different from our Eastern country's; I shall first state the faults of our kilns, and then the make of these can be understood.

paragraphs.orig: 我窰直一臥竈, 非窰也。 初無造窰之甎, 故支木而泥築薪。 以大松燒, 堅其窰, 其燒堅之費, 先已多矣。 窰長而不能高, 故火不炎上。 火不能炎上, 故火氣無力。 火氣無力, 故必爇松取猛, 爇松取猛, 故火候不齊。 火候不齊, 故瓦之近火者, 常患苦窳, 遠火者, 又恨不熟。 無論燔瓷燒瓮, 凡爲陶之家, 窰皆如此, 其爇松之法又同, 松膏烈勝他薪也。 松一剪則非再孽之樹, 而一遇陶戶, 四山童濯, 百年養之, 一朝盡之, 乃復鳥散逐松而去。 此緣一窰失法, 而國中之良材日盡, 陶戶亦日困矣。
paragraphs.reading: 아요직일와조, 비요야. 초무조요지전, 고지목이이축신. 이대송소, 견기요, 기소견지비, 선이다의. 요장이불능고, 고화불염상. 화불능염상, 고화기무력. 화기무력, 고필설송취맹, 설송취맹, 고화후부제. 화후부제, 고와지근화자, 상환고유, 원화자, 우한불숙. 무론번자소옹, 범위도지가, 요개여차, 기설송지법우동, 송고열승타신야. 송일전칙비재얼지수, 이일우도호, 사산동탁, 백년양지, 일조진지, 내부조산축송이거. 차연일요실법, 이국중지양재일진, 도호역일곤의.
paragraphs.en: Our kiln is simply a lying-down stove; it is not a kiln at all. At first there were no bricks to build a kiln with, so they prop up wood and plaster it with mud, and pile on firewood. They burn large pines to harden the kiln, and the cost of burning to harden it is already great beforehand. The kiln is long and cannot be made high, so the fire does not blaze upward. Since the fire cannot blaze upward, the fire's force has no strength. Since the fire has no strength, they must burn pine to get fierceness; since they burn pine for fierceness, the heat is uneven. Since the heat is uneven, the tiles near the fire are always plagued by warping and cracking, and those far from it by being underfired. Whether firing porcelain or baking jars, every household that makes pottery has a kiln like this and the same way of burning pine, for pine resin burns fiercer than any other fuel. Pine, once cut, is not a tree that sprouts again; yet whenever it meets a potter's household, the mountains on all four sides are stripped bare, what was nurtured for a hundred years is finished in one morning, and then they scatter like birds, pursuing pine elsewhere. Thus through the failure of one kiln's method, the fine timber of the whole country daily runs out, and the potters too are daily in distress.

paragraphs.orig: 今觀此窰, 甎築灰封, 初無燒堅之費, 任意高大。 形如覆鍾, 𥦔頂爲池, 容水數斛, 旁穿烟門四五, 火能炎上也。 置甎其中, 相支爲火道, 大約其妙在積, 今使我手能爲之至易也, 然口實難形。 正使問, 「其積類品字乎。」 余曰 「似是而非也。」 卞主簿問, 「其積類疊冊匣乎。」 余曰, 「似是而非也。」 甓不平置, 皆隅立爲十餘行, 若堗𣎒, 再於其上, 斜駕排立。 次次架積, 以抵窰頂, 孔穴自然踈通如麂眼。 火氣上達. 相爲咽喉. 引焰如吸, 萬喉遞呑, 火氣常猛, 雖薥稭黍柄, 能匀燔齊熟, 自無攣翻龜坼之患。
paragraphs.reading: 금관차요, 전축회봉, 초무소견지비, 임의고대. 형여복종, 𥦔정위지, 용수수곡, 방천연문사오, 화능염상야. 치전기중, 상지위화도, 대약기묘재적, 금사아수능위지지이야, 연구실난형. 정사문, 「기적유품자호.」 여왈 「사시이비야.」 변주부문, 「기적유첩책갑호.」 여왈, 「사시이비야.」 벽불평치, 개우립위십여항, 약돌𣎒, 재어기상, 사가배립. 차차가적, 이저요정, 공혈자연소통여궤안. 화기상달. 상위인후. 인염여흡, 만후체탄, 화기상맹, 수촉갈서병, 능균번제숙, 자무연번구탁지환.
paragraphs.en: Now, looking at this kiln, it is built of bricks and sealed with lime, with no cost for hardening it by firing, and it can be made as tall and big as one wishes. Its form is like an inverted bell; the top is dug out into a pool holding several hu of water, and four or five flue-holes are pierced in the sides, so the fire can blaze upward. Bricks are set inside, propping one another to form fire-channels; the subtlety lies largely in the stacking. If I were to do it with my own hands it would be quite easy, but it is hard to put into words. The chief envoy asked, "Does the stacking resemble the character 品?" I said, "It seems so but is not." Registrar Byeon asked, "Does it resemble stacked book-cases?" I said, "It seems so but is not." The bricks are not laid flat but all stood on end in a dozen or more rows, like the ondol flues (堗𣎒), and above them again others are set slantwise in rows; layer by layer they are built up to the kiln top, and the openings naturally lie thin and clear-through like the eyes of a muntjac. The fire's breath mounts upward, and the channels serve each other as throats: they draw the flame as though inhaling, ten thousand throats swallowing in turn, so that the fire is always fierce; even sorghum straw and stalks burn evenly and cook all alike, and there is naturally none of the warping and tortoise-shell cracking.

paragraphs.orig: 今我東陶戶不先究窰制, 而自非大松林, 不得設窰。 陶非可禁之事, 而松是有限之物, 則莫如先改窰制, 以兩利之。 鰲城李公恒福, 老稼齋皆說甓利, 而不詳窰制, 甚可恨也。 或云, 「薥稭三百握, 爲一窰之薪, 得甎八千。」 薥稭長一丈半, 拇指大則一握, 僅四五柄耳。 然則薥稭爲薪, 不過千餘柄, 可得近萬之甎耳。
paragraphs.reading: 금아동도호불선구요제, 이자비대송림, 부득설요. 도비가금지사, 이송시유한지물, 칙막여선개요제, 이양이지. 오성이공항복, 노가재개설벽리, 이불상요제, 심가한야. 혹운, 「촉갈삼백악, 위일요지신, 득전팔천.」 촉갈장일장반, 무지대칙일악, 근사오병이. 연칙촉갈위신, 불과천여병, 가득근만지전이.
paragraphs.en: Now our Eastern potters do not first study the make of the kiln, and unless there is a great pine forest they cannot set up a kiln. Pottery is not something that can be prohibited, and pine is a limited resource; so nothing is better than first to change the make of the kiln and benefit both. Yi Hang-bok, Lord of Oseong, and Nogajae both spoke of the benefit of bricks but did not detail the make of the kiln, which is greatly to be regretted. Someone says, "Three hundred fistfuls of sorghum stalks serve as fuel for one kiln and yield eight thousand bricks." A sorghum stalk is a jang and a half long, and a fistful of thumb-thick ones is only four or five stalks. Then using sorghum stalks as fuel would be no more than a thousand-odd stalks to yield nearly ten thousand bricks.

paragraphs.orig: 日長如年。 向夕尤暑, 不堪昏睡。 聞傍炕方會紙牌, 叫呶爭鬨。 余遂躍然投座, 連勝五次, 得錢百餘。 沽酒痛飮, 可雪前恥。 問, 「今復不服否。」 趙卞曰, 「偶然耳。」 相與大笑。 卞君及來源, 不勝忿寃, 要余更設。 余辭曰, 「得意之地勿再往, 知足不殆。」
paragraphs.reading: 일장여년. 향석우서, 불감혼수. 문방항방회지패, 규노쟁홍. 여수약연투좌, 연승오차, 득전백여. 고주통음, 가설전치. 문, 「금부불복부.」 조변왈, 「우연이.」 상여대소. 변군급내원, 불승분원, 요여갱설. 여사왈, 「득의지지물재왕, 지족불태.」
paragraphs.en: The days were long as years. Toward evening the heat grew worse, and I could not bear to doze off. I heard that in the room across the kang they were playing paper cards, shouting and quarrelling. I leapt up and took my seat there, and won five times running, gaining a hundred-odd coins. I bought wine and drank deep, a fair wiping out of my earlier shame. I asked, "Do you still not concede?" Jo and Byeon said, "It was chance." We all laughed together. Mr. Byeon and Rae-won, unable to bear their indignation, demanded that I set up another game. I declined: "Where one has gained one's wish, do not go again; know contentment and you will not be endangered."

paragraphs.orig: ## 결혼식 행렬과 시골 글방 선생
paragraphs.en: A Wedding Procession and the Village Schoolmaster

paragraphs.orig: 初三日己卯 (曉大雨 朝晝快晴 夜又大雨達曙)
paragraphs.reading: 초삼일기묘 (효대우 조주쾌청 야우대우달서)
paragraphs.en: The third day, gimyo (heavy rain at dawn; fair all through morning and noon; heavy rain again at night until daybreak).

paragraphs.orig: 又留。 朝起開牕, 積雨快霽。 光風時轉, 日色淸明。 可占午炎, 榴花滿地, 銷作紅泥, 繡毬浥露, 玉簪抽雪。 門前有簫笳鐃鉦之聲, 急出觀之, 乃迎親禮也。 彩畵紗燈六對, 靑盖一對, 紅盖一對, 簫一雙, 笳一雙, 觱篥一雙, 疊鉦一雙, 中央四人, 肩擔一座靑屋轎, 四面傅玻瓈爲牕, 四角嚲彩絲流蘇。 轎正腰爲杠, 以靑絲大繩, 橫絞杠之前後, 再以短杠, 當中貫絞, 兩頭肩荷。 四人八蹄, 一行接武, 不動不搖, 懸空而行, 此法大妙。 轎後有兩車, 皆以黑布爲屋, 駕一驢而行。 一車共載四個老婆, 面俱老醜, 而不廢朱粉, 顚髮盡禿, 光赭如匏, 寸髻北指, 猶滿揷花朶, 兩耳垂璫, 黑衣黃裳。 一車共載三少婦, 朱袴或綠袴, 都不繫裳。 其中一少女, 頗有姿色。 盖老是粧婆乳媼, 少的是丫鬟也。三十餘騎簇擁, 着一個胖大莽漢, 口旁頤邊, 黑髭鬆鬆, 權着九爪蟒袍, 白馬金鞍, 穩踏銀鐙, 堆着笑臉。 後有三兩車, 滿載衣。
